If one does not understand in the beginning but continues to hear again and again, the wonderful effects of Lord Chaitanya’s pastimes will bring love for Kṛṣṇa. Gradually one will come to understand the loving affairs between Kṛṣṇa and the <span class="e3">gopīs</span> and other associates of Vṛndāvan. Everyone is advised to continue to hear over and over again in order to greatly benefit.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>

Rear | Wall
(9)
āmi guru-dāsa — nahi anya
I am guru’s slave, nothing else.
āmi kariva bhramaṇa chaudda-bhuvana<br />svarūpe sabaya kari’ udbodhana<br />hāte laye yāba premera niśāna<br />dharāba svarūpa chihna
I will walk the fourteen worlds, doing service and awakening everyone to their true selves. I will go taking into my hand the banner of divine love which I will decorate with a sign of true self.
āmi chhāḍāba sakale sarva-dharma<br />kariba chūrṇa jñāna o karma<br />rachiba viśāla bhakati-harmya<br />guru-dāsa nahi anya
I will give up all kinds of religion, will grind into powder knowledge, <span class="e3">jñāna,</span> and action, <span class="e3">karma.</span> I will make a huge palace for devotion, <span class="e3">bhakti.</span> I am guru’s slave, nothing else.
āmi bajaba jagate vijaya-daṅkā<br />ghuchāba sakala dvandva-śaṅkā<br />bahāba viśve bhakati-gaṅgā<br />tuṣi’ hari labhi puṇya
I will beat a drum making a great sound everywhere in the world. I will dispel all quarrel and fear. I will carry to the whole of material universe the Ganges waters of devotion, <span class="e3">bhakti.</span> Pleasing Hari, I attain virtue.
āmi āryānārya mlechchha sabaya<br />lāgāiba bale kṛṣṇa-sevāya<br />chāḍāibā sabe golokera nā’ya<br />pṛthvī kariba śūṇya
Serving respectable persons and the uncivilized, as well as the savage <span class="e3">mlechas,</span> I will attain strength for service to Kṛṣṇa. I will embark everybody onto the boat of Goloka and will vacate the earth.
āmi chālāba sakale guru-pada bale<br />vādāma tūliba hari-bola bale<br />mahāmāyā-vinī chhalanā chhalile<br />kariba chinna-bhinna
I will apply all power of Gurupad and hoist the sail by the strength of chanting of the Holy Names. If <span class="e3">mahā-māyā </span>deceives with her illusions, and I will cut that asunder.
sabe eka parichaye dibe parichaya<br />labhibe svarūpa amṛtamaya<br />pūjibe śrī-hari dibe jaya jaya<br />nehāri’ ha-iba dhanya
Everyone will introduce themselves to all and will attain the nectarean true self. They will worship Śrī Hari, will chant, <span class="e3">“Jaya! Jayat</span> Seeing this I will become successful.
āmi guru-dāsa nahi anya
I am guru’s slave, nothing else.
āmi nāi vā gelāma purī,<br />gayā, kāśī, badarīnārā’ṇa<br />nāi vā elāma ghari’
I went neither to Purī, nor Gayā, nor Kāśī, nor Badarīnārāyaṇa, and neither did I come to other sights.
yadi kona janme pāire hote<br />vaiṣṇava-kiṅkara
If only some birth I could become a servant of a Vaiṣṇava!
āmāra sakala āśāi miṭve re<br />bhāi pāi yadi ai bara
If I get such blessing, oh brother, all my desires will come to an end.
āmi chāi nā pete mukti<br />hāte-bhuktire ke māge?
I dont want to have liberation in my belly, nor to have enjoyment at my hand, who wants that?
yadi gauraharira charaṇa-sevaka<br />charaṇa pāire lāge
If only I could obtain the lotus feet of a servant of the lotus feet of Gaurahari!
āmi chāi re śudhu śachī-sutera<br />sevaka-charaṇa-rāge
Oh, how I want the pure love to the feet of the servants of Śachīsuta, Son of Śachī Devī.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Govinda Dev-Goswāmī</span>
(10.1)
nārāyaṇo’pi vikṛtiṁ yāti<br />guroḥ prachyutasya durbuddheḥ<br />kamalasya jalād apaiti<br />raviḥ śuśyati nāśayati cha
The disciple is like a lotus. The spiritual master is like the water around the lotus, just as in a pond or a lake. And Kṛṣṇa is like the sun. As long as the lotus is floating on the water, the sun will nourish the lotus. But if the water vanishes, that very sun will burn the lotus. Without water, the Kṛṣṇa sun will burn the lotus. Without the help of the guru, the disciple is nowhere.
<span class="e3">—Keṣāñchit (revered votary)</span>
(10.2)
śravaṇayāpi bahubhir yo na labhyaḥ<br />śṛṇvanto ’pi bahavo yaṁ na vidyuḥ<br />āścaryo vaktā kuśalo ’sya labdhā<br />āścaryo ’sya jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ
Despite their hearing [about the Lord and/or the soul], many may not understand it. Despite their listening [about the Lord and/or the soul], many may not know it. Those who have received the intelligence, speak of it as a wonder. Those to whom the intelligence was revealed, know this as a wonder.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Kaṭha Upaniṣada</span>
(10.3)
yasya prasādād bhagavat-prasādo<br />yasyāprasādān na gatiḥ kuto ’pi<br />dhyāyan stuvaṁs tasya yaśas tri-sandhyaṁ<br />vande guroḥ śrī-caraṇāravindam
I bow down to the lotus feet of Śrī Gurudeva. By his grace we achieve the grace of Kṛṣṇa; without his grace, we are lost. Therefore, at daybreak, noon, and evening, we meditate upon and sing the glories of Śrī Gurudeva, and pray for his mercy.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravarti Ṭhākura</span>
(10.4)
guru-pāda-padme rahe yāra niṣṭhā-bhakti<br />brahmāṇḍe tārite se dhare mahā-śakti
Who keeps unflinching devotion to the lotus feet <span class="e3">of guru,</span> he has the great power to deliver the whole universe.
(11.1)
nitāi-pada-kamala, koṭī-chandra-suśītala,<br />ye chāyāya jagata juḍāya<br />hena nitāi bine bhāi, rādhā-kṛṣṇa pāite nāi,<br />dṛḍha kari dhara nitāira pāya
The lotus feet of Nitāi are extremely cool and pleasing like millions of moons, in the shade of these feet the world becomes cool and relieved. Without such Nitāi, it is not possible to get Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Firmly hold the feet of Nitāi.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Narottama Ṭhākura</span>
(11.2)
preme matta nityānanda kṛpā-avatāra<br />uttama, adhama, kichhu nā kare vichāra<br />ye āge paḍaye, tāre karaye nistāra
Because Lord Nityānanda is intoxicated by ecstatic love and is an incarnation of mercy, He does not distinguish between the good and the bad. He delivers all those who fall down before Him.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>
(11.3)
saṁsārera pāra haiyā bhaktira sāgare<br />ye ḍubibe se bhajuka nitāichādere
Who wants to sail through the mundane world without drowning in the ocean of devotion, he should worship the moon-like Nitāi.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Vṛndāvana Dasa Ṭhākura</span>
(11.4)
sphurad-amala-kirīṭaṁ kiṅkiṇī-kaṅkaṇārhaṁ<br />chalad-alaka-kapolaṁ kuṇḍala-śrī-mukhābjam<br />tuhina-giri-manojñaṁ nīla-meghāmbarāḍhyaṁ<br />hala-muṣala-viśālaṁ kāma-pālaṁ samīḍe
I worship Him who has a shining pure crown, bangles, moving curls of hair on His cheeks, His lotus face decorated with earrings, who as charming as a snow-covered mountain, who is adorned with the best clothes of blue-cloud color, carrying His huge plough and club, and who gratifies all desires.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Garga Saṁhitā</span>
(12.1)
muktir hitvānyathā rūpaṁ sva-rūpeṇa vyavasthitiḥ
Liberation means being situated in one’s eternal original form, which he attains after giving up the changeable gross and subtle bodies.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(12.2)
bhaktiḥ pareśānubhavo viraktir<br />anyatra caiṣa trika eka-kālaḥ<br />prapadyamānasya yathāśnataḥ syus<br />tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ kṣud-apāyo ’nu-ghāsam
Devotion, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and detachment from other things — these three occur simultaneously for one who has taken shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, in the same way that pleasure, nourishment and relief from hunger come simultaneously and increasingly, with each bite, for a person engaged in eating.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(12.3)
“prema-dhana vinā vyartha daridra jīvana<br />‘dāsa’ kari’ vetana more deha prema-dhana”
[Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu said:] “Without love of Godhead, My life is useless. Therefore I pray that You accept Me as Your servant and give Me the salary of ecstatic love of God.”
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>
(12.4)
ātmendriya-prīti-vāñchā—tāre bali ‘kāma’<br />kṛṣṇendriya-prīti-icchā dhare ‘prema’ nāma<br />ataeva kāma-preme bahuta antara<br />kāma — andha-tamaḥ, prema — nirmala bhāskara
The desire to gratify one’s own senses is <span class="e3">kāma</span> (lust), but the desire to please the senses of Lord Kṛṣṇa is <span class="e3">prema</span> (love). Therefore lust and love are quite different. Lust is like dense darkness, but love is like the bright sun.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>
(13.1)
varṣāyāṁ vai sajala-jalado vādayan mandra-bheriṁ<br />yadvad-viśve bhramati bahudhā vāridhārāṣcha varṣan<br />tadvad-bhūmau bhramasi sagaṇair ghoṣayan gaura-gāthā<br />nityaṁ divyāmṛta-sukaruṇāṁ tvaṁ hi deva! pravarṣan
Generally in the rainy season the water-bearing clouds wander about and beat a deep-sounding drum. Just as in this world clouds wander about and shed torrents of water, you and your men wander about this earth, marching and proclaiming the glories of Gaura. Oh my Lord, indeed you always pour without reservation the divine nectar of your mercy.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Govinda Dev-Goswāmī</span>
(13.2)
dāsa-vṛndāvanaṁ vande kṛṣṇa-dāsa-prabhuṁ tathā<br />chhannāvatāra-chaitanya-līlā-vistāra-kāriṇau<br />dvau nityānanda-pādābja-karuṇā-reṇu-bhūṣitau<br />vyakta-chchhannau budhāchintyau vāvande vyāsa-rūpinau<br />śrī-guru-gaura-gāndharvā-govindāś cha gaṇaiḥ saha<br />jayanti pāṭhakaś chātra sarveṣāṁ karuṇārthinaḥ
I offer my obeisances to Dāsa Vṛndāvana and Kṛṣṇadāsa Prabhu, who made public the pastimes of the hidden <span class="e3">avatāra, </span>Śrī Chaitanya. They were both decorated by the mercy-dust of the lotus feet of Nityānanda. I offer my obeisances to these two inconceivable sages who assumed the form of Vyāsadeva, one — explicitly (Vṛndāvan Dās Ṭhākur), another — hidden (Kṛṣṇa Dās Kavirāj Goswāmī). Together with Śrī Guru Gaurāṅga Gāndharvā Govinda and Their associates they conquer scholars who then all seek their mercy.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Govinda Dev-Goswāmī</span>
(13.3)
yaḥ sankhya-paṅkena kutarka-pāṁśunā<br />vivarta-gartena cha lupta-dīdhitim<br />śuddhaṁ vyadhād vāk-sudhayā maheśvaraṁ<br />kṛṣṇaṁ sa jīvaḥ prabhur astu me gatiḥ
He who with his brilliance removed the mud of analytic approach, the dust of useless arguments, as well as the pit of illusion, who by his nectarean vibration perfectly established Kṛṣṇa as the Supreme Lord, may that Jīva Prabhu be my goal of life.
(14.1)
śṛṇvantu viśve amṛtasya putrā
O, you sons of nectar, sons of the nectarine ocean: please listen to me.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣada</span>
(14.2)
uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata kṣurasya dhārā<br />niśitā duratyayā durgaṁ pathas tat kavayo vadanti
Please wake up and try to understand the boon that you now have in this human form of life. The path of spiritual realization is very difficult; it is sharp like a razor’s edge. That is the opinion of learned transcendental scholars.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Kaṭha Upaniṣada</span>
(14.3)
sahasā vidadhīta na kriyām
“Suddenly not to do anything.”
(14.4)
kṛṣṇa-bhakta — niṣkāma, ataeva ‘śānta’<br />bhukti-mukti-siddhi-kāmī — sakali ‘aśānta’
Because a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa is desireless, he is peaceful. Fruitive workers desire material enjoyment, <span class="e3">jñānīs</span> desire liberation, and <span class="e3">yogīs</span> desire material opulence; therefore they are all lusty and cannot be peaceful.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>
(14.5)
saṁsāre ’smin kṣaṇārdho ’pi sat-saṅgaḥ śevadhir nṛṇām
Even half a moment’s association with pure devotees within this world of birth and death is a priceless treasure for any man.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(14.6)
ahaṁ bhakta-parādhīno hy asvatantra iva dvija<br />sādhubhir grasta-hṛdayo bhaktair bhakta-jana-priyaḥ
O My dear <span class="e3">brāhmaṇa</span>, I am subordinate to My devotee, and therefore I am like one who has no independence. The <span class="e3">sādhu </span>devotees have captured My heart. And not to speak of My devotees, those who are devoted to My devotees are also dear to Me.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(14.7)
yāha, bhāgavata paḍa vaiṣṇavera sthāne<br />ekānta āśraya kara caitanya-caraṇe
If you want to understand <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam,</span> you must approach a self-realized Vaiṣṇava and hear from him. You can do this when you have completely taken shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>

Part IV
Right Side

Right | Pillars
(1)
dina-yāminyau sayam prātaḥ<br />śiśira-vasantau punar āyātaḥ<br />kālaḥ kriḍati gachchhaty āyus<br />tad api na muñchaty āśā-vāyuḥ
Everything comes and goes in the course of time, sunrise and sunset, day and night, winter and springtime, even life itself, but the false hope of material happiness never goes away.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Śaṅkarāchārya</span>
(2)
gurur na sa syāt sva-jano na sa syāt<br />pitā na sa syāj jananī na sā syāt<br />daivaṁ na tat syāt na patiś ca sa syān<br />na mocayed yaḥ samupeta-mṛtyum
One who cannot save other souls from the world of impending death — that is, one who cannot teach the path of devotion — he cannot be a teacher, although he may be called ‘guru’; he cannot be a relative — he is not worthy of the designation; he cannot be a father — he is not qualified to beget a son; she cannot be a mother — she should not bear a child; he cannot be a god — the demigods who cannot deliver others from material bondage are not entitled to accept worship from human society; and he cannot be a husband — his hand is not fit to accept in marriage.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(3)
aho bakī yaṁ stana-kāla-kūṭaṁ<br />jighāṁsayāpāyayad apy asādhvī<br />lebhe gatiṁ dhātry-ucitāṁ tato ’nyaṁ<br />kaṁ vā dayāluṁ śaraṇaṁ vrajema
How astonishing! When Pūtanā, the wicked sister of Bakāsura, tried to kill child Kṛṣṇa by offering Him deadly poison on her breast, she reached a position befitting the Lords nursemaid. Could I ever have as merciful a shelter as that Lord Kṛṣṇa?
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(4)
ahaṅkāra-yutanam hi<br />madhye parvata-rāśayaḥ<br />ahaṅkāra-nivṛttanam<br />keśavo nāhi duragah
The Supreme Lord Keśava remains in the company of persons who are free from a mundane conception of life; but there appears to be a great mountain range between the self-asserting egotists and the Lord.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Brahma-vaivartta Purāṇa</span>
(5)
jānanta eva jānantu<br />kiṁ bahūktyā na me prabho<br />manaso vapuṣo vāco<br />vaibhavaṁ tava go-caraḥ
There are people who say, “I know everything about Kṛṣṇa.” Let them think that way. As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O my Lord, let me say this much. As far as Your opulences are concerned, they are all beyond the reach of my mind, body, and words.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Bhāgavata</span>

Right | Niche
Śrī Nāma Prabhu
(6.1)
yad āsaṅga kriyā karma jānatā vāpy ajānatā<br />pūrṇaṁ bhavatu tat sarvaṁ śrī harer nāma-kīrttanāt
When an action is performed, it is performed according to the knowingly or unknowingly accumulated <span class="e3">karma.</span> May it then all become perfect by the chanting of the Holy Name of the Lord.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</span>
(6.2)
nāmaikaṁ yasya vāci smaraṇa-patha-gataṁ śrotra-mūlaṁ gataṁ vā<br />śuddhaṁ vāśuddha-varṇaṁ vyavahita-rahitaṁ tārayaty eva satyam<br />tac ced deha-draviṇa-janatā-lobha-pāṣaṇḍa-madhye<br />nikṣiptaṁ syān na phala-janakaṁ śīghram evātra vipra
If a devotee once utters the Holy Name of the Lord, or if it penetrates his mind or enters his ear, which is the channel of aural reception, that Holy Name will certainly deliver him from material bondage, whether vibrated properly or improperly, with correct or incorrect grammar, and properly joined or vibrated in separate parts. O <span class="e3">brāhmaṇa,</span> the potency of the Holy Name is therefore certainly great. However, if one uses the vibration of the Holy Name for the benefit of the material body, for material wealth and followers, or under the influence of greed or atheism — in other words, if one utters the Name with offenses — such chanting will not produce the desired result very soon. Therefore one should diligently avoid offenses in chanting the Holy Name of the Lord.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Padma Purāṇa</span>
(6.3)
nāmāparādha-yuktānāṁ nāmāny eva haranty agham<br />aviśrānti-prayuktāni tāny evārtha-karāṇi ca
We are chanting the Holy Name with offences, but if continuously we try to chant attentively, with love and affection, then Hari Nām’ Himself will automatically remove our offences.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Padma Purāṇa</span>
(6.4)
ākṛṣṭiḥ kṛta-cetasāṁ su-manasām uccāṭanaṁ cāṁhasām<br />ācaṇḍālam amūka-loka-sulabho vaśyaś ca mukti-śriyaḥ<br />no dīkṣāṁ na ca sat-kriyāṁ na ca puraścaryāṁ manāg īkṣate<br />mantro ’yaṁ rasanā-spṛg eva phalati śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāmātmakaḥ
The Holy Name of Lord Kṛṣṇa is an attractive feature for many saintly, liberal people. It is the annihilator of all sinful reactions and is so powerful that save for the dumb who cannot chant it, it is readily available to everyone, including the lowest type of man, the <span class="e3">chaṇḍāla.</span> The Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa is the controller of the opulence of liberation, and it is identical with Kṛṣṇa. Simply by touching the Holy Name with one’s tongue, immediate effects are produced. Chanting the Holy Name does not depend on initiation, pious activities or the <span class="e3">puraścaryā,</span> regulative principles generally observed before initiation. The Holy Name does not wait for all these activities. It is self-sufficient.
<span class="e3">—Śrī Lakṣmīdhara</span>
(6.5)
hṛdaya ha-ite bale, jihvāra agrete chale,<br />śabda-rūpe nāche anukṣaṇa
The Holy Name speaks from within my heart and moves on to my tongue, and incessantly dances in the form of the sound.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura</span>
(6.6)
nāma nāche jīva nāche nāche prema-dhana<br />jagat nāchāya māyā kare palāyana
The Name is dancing, the <span class="e3">jīva-souls</span> are dancing, the whole wealth of love is dancing. It makes the whole universe dance, and <span class="e3">māyā</span> flees from there.
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura</span>
(6.7)
sevā mora nāma-brahma-nāda
My service is to chant and glorify the divine name of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
<span class="e3">—Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākura</span>

Right | Wall
Daśavidha nāmāparādha
(7)
hari-nāma mahāmantra sarva-mantra-sāra<br />yadera karuṇā-bale jagate prachāra<br />sei nāma-parāyaṇa sādhu, mahājana<br />tahādera nindā nā kariha kadāchana [1]
The <span class="e3">mahā-mantra</span> of the Holy Name is the quintessence of all the <span class="e3">mantras.</span> He by whose mercy it is preached throughout the world, is devoted to the Name and is called a saint, a great man. Do not ever censure him.
vrajendra-nandana kṛṣṇa sarveśvareśvara<br />maheśvara ādi tara sevana-tatpara<br />nāma chintāmani kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-svarūpa<br />bheda-jñāna nā karibe līlā-guṇa-rūpa [2]
Vrajendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa is the Lord of Lords, everybody beginning with Lord Śiva are devoted to His service. The touchstone of the name is Kṛṣṇa consciousness embodied. Do not differentiate between His pastimes, qualities, and form.
“guru kṛṣṇa-rūpa hana śāstrera pramāṇe<br />guru-rūpe kṛṣṇa kṛpā kare bhāgyavāne”<br />se gurute martya-buddhi avajñādi tyaji<br />iṣṭa-lābha kara, nirantara nāma bhaji [3]
“According to the scriptural evidence, guru is a form of Kṛṣṇa. Through guru’s form Kṛṣṇa favours the fortunate ones.” Quit dishonouring, etc. such a guru as a man of mundane intellect. Fulfil your dream, always worship the Name.
śruti, śruti-mātā-saha sātvata purāṇa<br />śrī-nāma-charaṇa-padma kare nīrājana<br />sei śruti-śāstra yebā karaye nindana<br />se aparādhīra saṅga karibe varjana [4]
The <span class="e3">Vedas</span> along with the <span class="e3">veda mātā</span> (Gāyatrī), Purāṇas related to the Supreme Truth, they all worship the lotus feet of the Holy Name. You must avoid the association of such sinful offenders who vilify these scriptures.
nāmera mahimā sarva-śāstrete vākhāne<br />atistuti, hena kabhu nā bhāviha mane<br />agastya, ananta, brahmā, śivādi satata<br />ye nāma-mahimā-gāthā sankīrtana-rata<br />ye nāma-mahimā-sindhu ke pāibe pāra?<br />atistuti bale yei—sei durāchāra [5]
In all scriptures the glory of the Name is praised. Never consider in your mind that such praise is excessive or unreasonable. When Agastya, Ananta, Brahmā, Śiva, et al. are constantly engaged in the <span class="e3">saṁkīrtana,</span> chanting the glories of the Name, who can then cross this ocean of the glories of the Name? Those who say that it is excessive or unreasonable, are the wicked.
kṛṣṇa-nāmābalī nitya golokera dhana<br />kalpita, prākṛta, bhāve—aparādhī-jana [6]
All names of Kṛṣṇa are eternal wealth of Goloka. Those who think they are imaginary and vulgar, are offenders.
nāme sarva-pāpa-kṣaya sarva-śāstre kaya<br />sārā-dina pāpa kari sei bharasāya—<br />emata durbuddhi yāra sei aparādhī<br />māyā-pravañchita, duḥkha bhuñje niravadhi [7]
All scriptures say that the Name destroys all sins. Those who hope that they can sin all the time, are stupid and offensive. They are deceived by <span class="e3">māyā</span> and enjoy endless sorrow.
atulya śrī-kṛṣṇa-nāma pūrṇa-rasa-nidhi<br />tara sama nā bhāviha śubha-karma ādi [8]
The incomparable Name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is an ocean full of ecstasy. Do not consider it identical with auspicious actions or religious rites, etc.
nāme śraddhā-hīna-jana—vidhātā vañchita<br />tāre nāma dāne aparādha suniśchita [9]
To give the Name to those who are deceived by the Providence and have no faith in the Name, is definitely an offence.
śuniyāo kṛṣṇa-nāma-māhātmya apāra<br />ye prīti-rahita, sei narādhama chhāra<br />ahaṁtā mamatā yāra antare bāhire<br />śuddha kṛṣṇa-nāma tāra kabhu nāhi sphure [10]
Those who, hearing the boundless glories of the Name of Kṛṣṇa, remain devoid of love, are vile, worthless wretches. The pure Name of Kṛṣṇa will never manifest to one is within and without filled with the “I and mine” mentality.
ei daśa aparādha kariyā varjana<br />ye sujana kare hari-nāma sankīrtana<br />apūrva śrī-kṛṣṇa-prema labhya tāra haya<br />nāma-prabhu tara hṛde nitya vilasaya [11]
Giving up these ten offences, those good-natured souls who engage in congregational chanting of the Holy Name, achieve extraordinary love to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and the Nāma Prabhu forever sports in their hearts.
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Govinda Dev-Goswāmī</span>
(8.1)
kāmādīnāṁ kati na katidhā pālitā durnideśās<br />teṣāṁ jātā mayi na karuṇā na trapā nopaśāntiḥ<br />utsṛjyaitān atha yadu-pate sāmprataṁ labdha-buddhis<br />tvām āyātaḥ śaraṇam abhayaṁ māṁ niyuṅkṣvātma-dāsye
O Lord, for so long have I obeyed the unending, wicked dictates of lust, anger, greed, madness, delusion, and hatred, but they never took pity upon me, and I have felt neither shame nor the desire to abandon them. O Lord of the Yadus, after all this, I am leaving them behind. At last I have found my genuine sanity: I am surrendered wholly unto Your lotus feet, which are the abode of fearlessness. Please now engage me as Your personal servitor.
—<span class="e3">Keṣāñchit (revered votary)</span>
(8.2)
māṁ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye ’pi syuḥ pāpa-yonayaḥ<br />striyo vaiśyās tathā śūdrās te ’pi yānti parāṁ gatim
O son of Pṛthā, persons of low birth, women, merchants or labourers — they, too, attain the supreme destination by taking full refuge in Me.
—<span class="e3">Śrī Gītā</span>
(8.3)
na nāka-pṛṣṭhaṁ na ca pārameṣṭhyaṁ<br />na sārva-bhaumaṁ na rasādhipatyam<br />na yoga-siddhīr apunar-bhavaṁ vā<br />samañjasa tvā virahayya kāṅkṣe
O my Lord, source of all opportunities, I do not desire to enjoy in Dhruvaloka, the heavenly planets or the planet where Lord Brahma resides, nor do I want to be the supreme ruler of all the earthly planets or the lower planetary systems. I do not desire to be master of the powers of mystic <span class="e3">yoga,</span> nor do I want liberation if I have to give up Your lotus feet.
—<span class="e3">Śrī Bhāgavata</span>
(8.4)
emana durmmati, saṁsāra bhitare, paḍiyā āchhinu āmi<br />tava nija-jana, kona mahājane, pāṭhāiyā dile tumi
My wicked mind has forced me to fall into this material existence, but You sent (here) one of your owns, this great soul.
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura</span>
(8.5)
vairāgya-yug-bhakti-rasaṁ prayatnair<br />apāyayan mām anabhīpsum andham<br />kṛpāmbudhir yaḥ para-duḥkha-duḥkhī<br />sanātanas taṁ prabhum āśrayāmi
I was unwilling to drink the nectar of devotional service possessed of renunciation, but Sanātana Goswāmī, out of his causeless mercy, made me drink it, even though I was otherwise unable to do so. Therefore he is an ocean of mercy. He is very compassionate to fallen souls like me, and thus it is my duty to offer my respectful obeisances unto his lotus feet.
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Dāsa Goswāmīpāda</span>
(9.1)
pādābjayos tava vinā vara-dāsyam eva<br />nānyat kadāpi samaye kila devi yāche<br />sakhyāya te mama namo ’stu namo ’stu nityaṁ<br />dasyāya te mama raso ’stu raso ’stu satyam
Oh Devī, servitude to Your lotus feet is definitely the best. I shall never ever ask You for anything other than that. Eternally shall I pay my obeisances, shall I pay my obeisances to the friendly relationship with You, and forever shall I relish, shall I relish the servitude to You.
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Dāsa Goswāmīpāda</span>
(9.2)
sakhī vinā ei līlāya anyera nāhi gati<br />sakhī-bhāve ye tāṅre kare anugati<br />rādhā-kṛṣṇa-kuñjasevā-sādhya sei pāya<br />sei sādhya pāite āra nāhika upāya
Without the help of the <span class="e3">gopīs,</span> one cannot enter into these pastimes. Only he who worships the Lord in the ecstasy of the <span class="e3">gopīs,</span> following in their footsteps, can engage in the service of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in the bushes of Vṛndāvan. Only then can one understand the conjugal love between Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. There is no other procedure for understanding.
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Goswāmī</span>
(9.3)
tvaṁ rūpa-mañjari sakhi prathitā pure ’smin<br />puṁsaḥ parasya vadanaṁ na hi paśyasīti<br />bimbādhare kṣatam anāgata-bhartṛkāyā<br />yat te vyadhāyi kim u tach chuka-puṅgavena
Oh friend Rūpa Mañjari, people of this town respect and trust you, thus you definitely do not see the face of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. But there are cuts on your red <span class="e3">bimba </span>lips although your husband has not come yet. Did that great parrot strike them?
—<span class="e3">Śrīla Dāsa Goswāmīpāda</span>
(9.4)
mātala hari-jana kīrtana-raṅge<br />pujala rāga-patha gaurava-bhaṅge
From afar we shall worship the <span class="e3">rāga-patha,</span> the path of spontaneous affectionate service, while we ourselves shall live within the <span class="e3">Vedic</span> guide-line.

Śrī Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅgau Jayataḥ
Vyasa-Puja Offering, 1997
āpanāke jānāi koti daṇḍavat nati |<br />chira-dina oi pade thāke yena mati ||<br />māyā pāśe yadi phamsi ye kona samaya |<br />taribāra lāgi yena, ḍāki go tomāya ||<br />sādhu, guru, vaiṣṇavera gāne, sukha pāi |<br />yakhana yā khuśī mane, takhani tā gāi ||<br />pāpa pūrṇa lābha kṣati, nāhika vichāra |<br />jāni, vaiṣṇava kṛpāte saba yābe anāchāra ||<br />tandera guṇa-gāna-śakti, mora kabhu nāi |<br />tabu pāgalera mata, ki ye yena gāi ||<br />sādhu, guru, vaiṣṇava, kṛṣṇera prāṇa-dhana |<br />tandera pada-jala-reṇu māge mora mana ||<br />manera pipāsā baḍa sādhu sane vāsa |<br />sarvasva tyajiyā tāi kari abhilāsa ||<br />tandera charaṇe kata koti pāpa kari |<br />mana tabu paḍe thāke oi pada dhari ||<br />ārao kata bale mana, koṭi duḥkha sahi |<br />janme janme yena āmi, oi pade rahi ||
• I offer ten millions of prostrate obeisances. My desire is to forever remain at your feet. • Although anytime I can be strangled by the noose of <span class="e3">māyā,</span> to escape it, I am beseeching you for help. • Hearing the song of saints, gurus, and Vaiṣṇavas, I become happy. When this joy comes to my mind, then immediately I (begin to) sing. • There is no consideration for me whether something is full of sin, whether it is beneficial or harmful, I know that by the mercy of Vaiṣṇavas, all bad things, deviation will go away. • Their qualities and potency will never be mine. And yet, how come I sing like a madman? • My mind begs for the feet dust and the water from washing the feet of those who are life and soul of the saints, gurus, Vaiṣṇavas, and Kṛṣṇa. • My mind is extremely thirsty for living in a saints house. I long for this, giving up everything else. • How many millions of sins do I commit to your feet? Despite this, my mind keeps falling, and I am clasping your feet. • Moreover, how strong my mind is! I tolerate millions of distresses so that birth after birth I (could) remain at your feet.
haṭhāt deśe uṭhala sārā, śahara theke sakala pāḍā, vichitra kutūhale<br />sakale āja ānandete, ekatre sava uṭhala mete, nāche gāya dale dale
All of a sudden, throughout the country, in all wards of the town, there arose a peculiar delight. Today everybody is filled with bliss and they all gathered together in astonishment and began to dance and sing in groups.
bhakta-gaṇa sava avirata, śraddhāñjali dichchhe kata, śrī-maṭhete āsi<br />gauḍa deśera hṛdaya mājhye, yena sakala, dupura, saje, bājachhe, mohana vaśī
All devotees were continuously bringing so much tribute, coming to the holy temple. That noon, in the twilight, throughout the land of Gaura, Bengal, there sounded a stupefying flute.
śubha atharoi ḍisembara, kṛṣṇa-dvitīyā buddhabāra, barddhamānera ākāśa kari ālo<br />bāmuna pāḍāra bāmuna ghare, janama nilā jīvera tare, apūrva sundara śiśu mohaniyā bhālo
On the auspicious day of December 18, on the second night of the waning moon, on Wednesday, a ray of light fell from the sky. In the district of Bāmuna (<span class="e3">brāhmaṇas</span>), in a <span class="e3">brāhmaṇa </span>house, for the sake of <span class="e3">jīva</span>-souls there took birth an unprecedentedly beautiful child, attracting all good.
śrī taraṅgiṇī devī mātā, nitāi pada, nitya pitā, śrī devakī-vasudeva sama<br />guru-rūpe nanda-kumāra, yena kṛpā karilā evāra, jīvera nāśive rajaḥ tama
His mother Śrī Taraṅgiṇī Devī and eternal father Nitāipada are non-different from Śrī Devakī and Vasudeva. The youthful son of Nanda in form of a guru now bestowed his mercy to destroy the ignorance and passion in the<span class="e3"> jīva</span>-souls.
sei śiśu āja mahājana, bhakti sundara govinda dhana, jagater ananta gaurava<br />brahmāṇḍa bhodiyā goloka dhāma, sarvatra prakāśa tomāra nāma, he prabhu, tava sevā-saurabha
That child is now a great soul, the treasure named Bhakti Sundar Govinda, the eternal glory of the world. Revealing Goloka Dhāma in the whole universe, everywhere your name is renowned, my Lord, and there can be felt a sweet fragrance of your service.
tomāra komala murati āja, gānthā raya yena hṛdaya mājha, chintiba o pada niti<br />bhakta sajjana mile kata, mahimā rachibe śata śata, ke kata gāhibe tava gīti
At present your form is very soft and graceful. Just as all streams enter the core of a heart, I will eternally meditate upon your feet. You meet so many noble devotees and they compose hundreds of verses of glorification, but who is able to sing your glories?
pāiyā tava śītala charaṇa, maṅgalākāṅkṣī karibe varaṇa, parābe phulera mālā<br />jīvera lāgi dharile kāyā, tomāra bhaye pālābe māyā, juḍābe jagata jvālā
Obtaining your cooling lotus feet, desiring everyone’s welfare, I will perform worship and garland them. You accepted a body for the sake of the <span class="e3">jīva</span>-souls, <span class="e3">māyā</span> will flee for the fear of you, and all the burning pain of the whole creation will be soothed.
rājāsanera rājā yemana, tomāra śobhā ājake temana, rājā michhe, tumi nitya satya<br />agādha tava śāstra jñāne, golokera sei nitya-dhane, bilāo bharuk ārtta jīvera chitta
Your beauty and lustre are such that you resemble a king on a royal throne. However, a king is false, useless, but you are eternally true. Your knowledge of the scriptures is unfathomable, please distribute this eternal wealth of Goloka to fill the minds of the distressed souls.
paramparāra sūtra dhare, āsiyāchha modanī pare, prakāśite jīvoddhāra līlā<br />kṛpāra ādhāra guru-mahārāja, tomāte sarva-śakti sañchāra, kariyā sva-siṁhāsana dilā
You have come to make — by manifesting your human-like pastimes — the line of disciplic succession more charming. Guru Mahārāja, the very foundation of mercy, passing all potency onto you, gave you his own throne.
chira paṅkila dharaṇī-tala, śuddha bhakati prakaṭa karile’ yena apūrva chinmaya saroja<br />tāra sumadhura divya gandha, tomāra mājhāre ankichhe chhanda, bilābe sakale prema-varaja
On this ever covered with mud surface of the earth, you have revealed pure devotion which is like an extraordinary transcendental lotus. Its extremely sweet smell has born a desire within you to distribute to everybody the plantation of the divine love.
tava kṛpā-taru-śītala chhāyāya, e duḥkhī-jana yena ṭhani pāya, ohe dīna-dayāla ṭhākura<br />tumi navodita nirmala bhāskara, dayāmaya deva bhakati sundara, bhāvio tomāra kukura
Oh my Lord, merciful to the poor, this miserable man got a place in the cool shade under your mercy-tree. You are the spotless newly risen sun, merciful Deva Bhakti Sundara, please consider me your dog.
śrī-bhakti-rakṣaka prabhu śrī śrīdhara, tomāke bānāla bhava karṇa-dhāra, mo sama patita lāgi<br />tāi tava śubha āvirbhāva dine, gati nāi ai-charaṇa vihane, e patita kande kṛpā māgī
Prabhu Śrī Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrī Śrīdhara made you the helmsman of the world for the sake of such fallen, degraded souls like me. So, on the auspicious day of your appearance, there is no other refuge for me other than your feet, and this fallen soul is crying and begging you for mercy.
—<span class="e3">Śrī Bhakti Nirmala Āchārya</span>

Translator’s Note
With overflowing joy in my heart, I would like to begin by offering my obeisance unto my spiritual masters, the devotees, and the readers of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, praying this publication is pleasing to them all.
Content
In this introductory note I will briefly explain the content of this book and the method by which it has been presented. Following this introduction is a short compilation of expressions by Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj and Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj in praise of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, and an English translation of the Editor’s Note from the original 1949 Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh Bengali edition. Thereafter, the text of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> herself is presented along with the <span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya</span>.
In accordance with the 1949 edition, sections entitled <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgatera Prārthanā</span> (a collection of prayers compiled from <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> and other scriptures) and <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Hari-Guru-Vaiṣṇava-vandanā</span> (a set of prayers recited daily in Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh) have been included. These sections conclude the <span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya</span>. Following them, a poem by the commentator entitled <span class="e3">Mā Muñcha Pañcha-daśakam</span>, which deeply illus­trates śaraṇāgati’s integral mood of dainya, humility, is presented as an appendix. Lastly, an introductory guide to reading and pronoun­cing Bengali is provided.
Layout
The verses of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> have been presented in a five-fold format: 1) the Bengali text of each verse; 2) its Roman transliteration; 3) its word-for-word gloss; 4) its prose translation; and 5) a translation of the commentary on the verse from the <span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya</span>.
The <span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya</span> consists of three types of annotations: 1) synonyms: common sādhu-bhāṣā or chalit-bhāṣā forms of rare or esoteric sādhu-bhāṣā and Vraja-bhūli expressions; 2) scriptural references: citations of verses from texts such as <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>, <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>, and <span class="e3">Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span> which reveal the origins and profundity of the expressions within the verses; and 3) explanatory prose: short expla­nations of significant or enigmatic words or concepts within the verses (in many cases the Bengali prose explanations are themselves citations from other writings of Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur).
The Bengali synonyms given in the <span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya</span> have been presented in parentheses within the word-for-word gloss. Where the synonyms are virtually identical in meaning to the original text, no additional translation of them has been given. In all other instances the synonyms have been translated and presented in parentheses. All the scriptural references have been translated and presented as notes below the prose translations of the verses to which they refer. The Bengali explanatory prose has been translated and presented in some instances in parentheses within the word-for-word gloss, and in all others as notes.
Translation
With regard for the direct, heart-touching simplicity of the original text, as well as the brevity and feel of the commentary (styled <span class="e3">laghu</span>, lit. ‘light’ or ‘gentle’), the translation has aimed at simply and clearly conveying the concepts and sentiments expressed within the text using language that is succinct and readily understandable. As far as possible, the use of English idioms, embellishments, affec­tations, and so forth, has been avoided. The axiom <span class="e3">mitañcha sārañcha vacho hi vāgmitā</span>, ‘True eloquence is concise, essential speech’ (<span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>: Ādi-līlā, 1.106), has been the guiding principle.
All translation has been undertaken with reference to relevant treatises: most commonly Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj’s <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span>, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s <span class="e3">Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya</span> and <span class="e3">Pīyūṣa-varṣiṇī-vṛtti</span>, and Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur’s <span class="e3">Anubhāṣya</span> and <span class="e3">Anuvṛtti</span>.
Acknowledgements
Out of affection and appreciation, I feel compelled to mention the numerous devotees who helped with this publication. Śrīpād Bhakti Prapanna Tīrtha Mahārāj supported and guided me over the course of the project. Kānāi Lāl Prabhu, Puruṣottam Jagannāth Prabhu, and Aninditā Devī Dāsī assisted with translation. Śrī Lekhā Devī Dāsī, Kṛṣṇa Prema Prabhu, Nṛsiṁha Chaitanya Prabhu, Jagadānanda Prabhu, and Sundar Gopāl Prabhu proofread the text. Rasa Mayī Paṇḍita Devī Dāsī prepared the Bengali text and assisted with proofreading. Biśākhā Devī Dāsī provided indispensable assistance with all aspects of the project: proofreading, formatting, editing, typesetting, and so on. Lalita Mādhav Prabhu provided essential guidance regarding method­ology and thoroughly edited the text. His work greatly improved both the accuracy and clarity with which the original text and the concepts it expresses have been represented. I am deeply indebted to him for his contribution and consider that this publication really should be credited to him. Mahāmantra Prabhu prepared the photos of the Guru-paramparā and designed the cover. Śrīla Bhakti Sudhīr Goswāmī Mahārāj and Śrīpād Mahānanda Prabhu Bhakti Rañjan did the final checking of the book as a whole.
Despite all the assistance I have received from these devotees it is inevitable that, as one who is perpetually subject to misunderstanding (bhram) and erroneous perception (karaṇāpāṭava), I have made mistakes within this publication. I beg all the revered readers’ forgiveness for this.
Genesis
To conclude this introduction I would like to explain how this publication of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> came about. In gist, I was present in a class given by our beloved Gurudev, Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj, in February of 2009 in which His Divine Grace spoke as follows:
“There are many very sweet, sweet songs in the book <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>. It is my request to the devotees that, if possible, they try to memorise those songs. When I joined the Mission of Śrīla Guru Mahārāj he gave me this book and said, ‘If you can memorise it, you take it.’ … Now I am thinking, ‘After me, who will be able to recite?’ I have some hope that in our sampradāya there must be someone who will be able to continue. There are many very sweet, sweet songs in <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, and at least devotees can learn songs like <span class="e3">Ātma-samarpaṇe gelā abhimāna</span> and <span class="e3">Sarvasva Tomāra charaṇe sa̐piyā</span>. There are so many sweet songs in <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> which are very nice to chant every day.”
The next day I enquired from Śrīla Govinda Mahārāj as follows:
<span class="e2">Kamal Kṛṣṇa Dās: </span>Yesterday you requested the devotees to memorise the songs of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>. You mentioned that Śrīla Guru Mahārāj tick-marked thirty-two songs for you to memorise. Could you tell us which songs those were? And would it be pleasing to you for us to print an English version of this book?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Govinda Mahārāj:</span> It is not necessary to print only those thirty-two songs; it is necessary to print all of the songs. Actually, all of the songs in <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> are very impor­tant. Sometimes some songs are a little less important, but otherwise all of the songs are very important. I can tick-mark the songs Śrīla Guru Mahārāj chose for me though, no problem.
<span class="e2">Kamal Kṛṣṇa Dās:</span> So it would be pleasing to you for us to try to make an English version of this book?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Govinda Mahārāj:</span> That would be very good.
<span class="e2">Kamal Kṛṣṇa Dās: </span>With Śrīla Guru Mahārāj’s Laghu-chandrikā commentary?
<span class="e2">Śrīla Govinda Mahārāj: </span>It has not been printed already?
<span class="e2">Kamal Kṛṣṇa Dās:</span> No.
<span class="e2">Śrīla Govinda Mahārāj:</span> Okay. If you can do it, that is very good, because you know: the only life of a practitioner is śaraṇāgati, surrender.
In his introduction Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur similarly sings: <span class="e3">śikhāya śaraṇāgati bhakatera prāṇa</span>, ‘the teachings of śaraṇāgati are the life of the devotees.’
In closing, it is my earnest prayer that, by the grace of Śrīla Govinda Mahārāj, everyone will find in this presentation of Śaraṇāgati a profound source of spiritual vitality and thus receive inspiration to dedicate their lives to surrendered service unto Śrī Guru and Vaiṣṇav (ānugatya-bhajan).
Śrī Gaura-jana-kiṅkar,
Bhakti Kamal Tyāgī
Śrī Gadādhar Paṇḍit Āvirbhāv Tithi
3 May 2011
Śrī Chaitanya Sāraswat Maṭh, Nabadwīp

In Praise of <span class="e2">Śaraṇāgati</span>
Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
Śrīla Guru Mahārāj, Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj, gave much attention to the writings of Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur. Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur is very sober and has expressed our conception in a very beautiful way through his songs. I feel and think that for anyone who practises Kṛṣṇa consciousness, who is eager to practise Kṛṣṇa consciousness, and has affection for the line of Kṛṣṇa consciousness, it is not necessary to read anything else—the songs of Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur are sufficient. That is, one will obtain all knowledge through his songs. You may not find all the references for this knowledge in his songs, but you will find all knowledge and our conception expressed very clearly there.
I think the songs of Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur are sufficient for every­one, and whenever I get a chance I read the songs of Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur. You do not know how much happiness I felt when <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati </span>was published in a beautiful form. Many books of Śrīla Guru Mahārāj had been published. We were very happy to see even <span class="e3">Brahma-saṁhitā</span> published. But when <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> was published, I was overjoyed to see her form.
Bankim Chandra, the emperor of Bengali literature, wrote, “<span class="e3">Bālya-prema vara saṅgādi</span>”. This means that the very strong love felt between young men and women is unbreakable and is the sweetest form of love in this world. When I was very young and first joined Kṛṣṇa consciousness, Śrīla Guru Mahārāj gave me <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>. I first published <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> for Śrīla Guru Mahārāj in 1949, and at that time I felt this type of happiness; I felt my exper­ience of bālya-prema was with <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>.
When I joined the lotus feet of Śrīla Guru Mahārāj as a young boy, he gave me this book and said, “If you can memorise it, you take it.” I had some capacity as a kīrtan singer from my childhood, and Śrīla Guru Mahārāj wanted to begin training me according to my qualifications. As a boy I had learned from my father many Vaiṣṇava songs. They were good songs, no doubt, but they are songs which are sung by sahajīyās. Śrīla Guru Mahārāj told me, “First you must forget all of those songs.” I said, “Yes, I will not sing any of those songs again.” And I never sang those songs again. Later, maybe twenty-five or thirty years later, Śrīla Guru Mahārāj wanted to hear some of those songs from me and he asked me, “Can you remember those songs now?” I said, “Mahārāj, I cannot remember the style of singing for those songs.”
Anyhow, when Śrīla Guru Mahārāj first gave me <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, he tick-marked thirty-two songs and said, “Memorise these thirty-two songs within seven days. Then every day, one by one or as required, you can sing those songs.” That book is still in my room, and I memorised those songs. How that happened, I do not know.
Now my memory is not always working; still, I hate to look at the book when I am singing. I never want to sing any song which I do not know. All the songs are within my memory. Now maybe I may miss one point as I am singing, but still I am never prepared to read from the book as I sing. And that was Śrīla Guru Mahārāj’s style. Guru Mahārāj knew all the songs and he would always sing them without the book. Previously he sang so much; he sang all the songs and showed us everything. After I joined, Guru Mahārāj got some relief and would give charge to me, saying, “Govinda Mahārāj, you sing, you sing, you sing.”
During assemblies of devotees, Śrīla Guru Mahārāj would always request me to sing two particular songs from <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>:<span class="e3"> Emana durmati saṁsāra bhitare </span>and <span class="e3">Ki jāni ki bale Tomāra dhāmete</span>. Guru Mahārāj gave me these two songs for my own real­isation. He wanted that every day I would really think, “<span class="e3">Ki jāni ki bale Tomāra dhāmete ha-inu śaraṇāgata</span>—by what force have I surrendered unto your lotus feet?”
Every day very nice saṅkīrtan is happening here in our temple. I cannot go and join the saṅkīrtan party, but I am always joining with the devotees mentally. I also hear the songs they are singing; every day they are singing such beautiful songs. It is very important though to have some realisation about those songs. Every phrase within the songs we sing is very sweet and very meaningful, and it is necessary to realise why we are singing these songs every day. Through that realisation we can cross over illusion.
We have heard from Śrīla Guru Mahārāj many times that Prabhupād Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākur would tell his disciples that some of the songs are very important to realise. He would say especially that the song <span class="e3">Āmāra jīvana sadā pāpe rata</span> is very important for practitioners to realise. Śrīla Guru Mahārāj told us that he would say that we must realise the position of our own self. What are we doing? What are we eating? How are our activities going on? We must have some realisation about these things.
I am thinking it is no doubt difficult for everyone to go on living every day without worldly forms of enjoyment. I am always thinking so much about the situation of the conditioned souls in this mundane world. It is unpalatable and very hard, no doubt. But Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākur’s advice is that we must clean our mind every day by singing the songs of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, and especially this song, <span class="e3">Āmāra jīvana sadā pāpe rata</span>. Just as we clean our home when we awaken in the morning by sweeping with a broom, so we should clean our mind by sweeping it with this song. By sweeping our mind with this song, the dirt within it is removed, it becomes cleaned, and our activities are redirected in the proper way. Śrīla Guru Mahārāj told us this many times: it is necessary to sweep clean our minds every day through saṅkīrtan.
It is very good that the devotees are patiently trying to follow this. I am getting inspiration by seeing their activities. Māyā, the illusory environment of Lord Kṛṣṇa, is always living beside us and trying to attract us. But by the grace of the mood of surrender and devotion to Lord Kṛṣṇa, under the direction of Guru-Vaiṣṇava, we must cross over the illusory environment.
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur, and Śrīla Guru Mahārāj have tried to give the conditioned souls inspiration to surrender. This is the primary purpose of their teachings. I have seen that it is not necessary to know so many things. If you know how to swim then you can cross a river. You do not need to know where the river is coming from, where it is going, what is inside the river, or which way the river is flowing. You do not need to check the speed at which the river is flowing or analyse the river with a barometer, temperature gauge, or any­thing else. You only need to know how to swim and in which direction you need to swim. That is sufficient for swimming across a river. The knowledge presented in <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> by Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur is like that. It is clear, simple knowledge which by itself is sufficient for us to cross over this illusory environment and reach the divine abode of the Lord.
<span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> is a small book, but all wealth is present within it in a glorious way. Through the songs of Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur we get the gist of all the scriptures. If all the scriptures disappeared from this mundane world but Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s songs remained, we would still have everything. We can get everything through his songs.
In Praise of <span class="e2">Śaraṇāgati</span><span class="e13">1</span>
Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
When I entered Śrī Gauḍīya Maṭh, I received Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s small Bengali book <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> for the very first time. It was so sweet to me that I purchased several copies and distributed them amongst my friends. Its price was only four paise. It was so sweet, it touched my heart. I thought, “Here is Kṛṣṇa—Kṛṣṇa-kathā (talks of Kṛṣṇa) is Kṛṣṇa Himself. Here is talk about Kṛṣṇa, the adhokṣaja, the transcendental.” I later composed a short commentary when I was in Nanda Grām, and it is published along with Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s commentary in Bengali.
I wrote an introductory poem to the commentary on <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>:
svairāchārābdhi-saṁmagnān jīvān gaurāṅghri-paṅkaje<br />uddhṛtya śaraṇāpatter māhātmyaṁ samabodhayat
“All the conditioned souls are saṁmagnān—they are diving or struggling in the ocean of svairāchāra or pleasure-seeking—anyābhilāṣ—immoral or whimsical activities. <span class="e3">Gaurāṅghri-paṅkaje uddhṛtya</span>: taking them out of that ocean, you put them in the lotus—you took them to the lotus feet of Gaurāṅga. You collected them from the wide, troubled ocean, and gave them to the lotus feet of Gaurāṅga. <span class="e3">Uddhṛtya śaraṇāpatter māhātmyaṁ samabodhayat</span>: and so, having placed them there, you began to instruct them about the great nobility and high value of śaraṇāgati, exclusive surrender. <span class="e3">Samabodhayat</span>: you tried to make them understand and realise the efficacy of śaraṇāgati proper. You, my Gurudev, Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur Prabhupād, did so, so I bow down unto you first.” Then I also wrote a verse offering obeisance unto the writer of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur.<span class="e13">2</span>

Editor’s Note
(translated from the original 1949 Bengali edition)
Śrīla Sachchidānanda Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, the magnanimous, eternally liberated associate of Śrī Gaurasundar—the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who descends in the Age of Kali as the saviour of the fallen—has described the fundamental characteristics of pure devotion in his songbook known as <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>. The author of <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span>, Śrīla Kṛṣṇa Dās Kavirāj Goswāmī Prabhu, has described the distinction between surrender (śaraṇāgati) and detachment (akiñchanatva) as follows:
śaraṇāgatera, akiñchanera—eka-i lakṣaṇa<br />tāra madhye praveśaye ‘ātma-samarpaṇa’<br />śaraṇa lañā kare kṛṣṇe ātma-samarpaṇa<br />kṛṣṇa tā̐re kare tat-kāle ātma-sama
(Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta: Madhya-līlā, 22.96, 99)
“Although a devotee who is surrendered to Kṛṣṇa (śaraṇāgata) and a devo­tee who is detached from this world (akiñ­chan) have the same external characteristics, the surrendered devotee has the superlative qualification of having fully offered their very soul to Kṛṣṇa. As soon as a surrendered soul takes shelter of Kṛṣṇa and fully offers themself to Him, Kṛṣṇa immediately accepts him as His own (as an associate equal to Himself).”
Being detached from this world (akiñchan), maintaining gen­uine faith (śraddhā) within the heart, and taking shelter of the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa in all respects, is said to be śaraṇāgati. The fundamental teachings of śaraṇāgati are found within the Vedas, <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>,<span class="e3"> Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span>, the <span class="e3">Rāmāyaṇa</span>, the Purāṇas, other scriptures auxiliary to the Vedas, and the writings of all the previous Āchāryas. Herein, I am citing a few examples from these sources of knowledge:
In the Śruti:
śyāmāch chchhavalaṁ prapadye<br />śavalāch chchhyāmaṁ prapadye
(Chhāndogya-upaniṣad: 8.13.1)
“By the mercy of Śyām (Kṛṣṇa), I surrender unto Śavalā (Rādhā). By the mercy of Śavalā, I surrender unto Śyam.”
yo brahmāṇaṁ vidadhāti pūrvaṁ yo brahma-vidyāṁ<br />tasmai gāḥ pālayati sma kṛṣṇaḥ<br />taṁ hi devam ātma-vṛtti-prakāśaṁ<br />mumukṣur vai śaraṇam amuṁ vrajet
(Tāpanyāṁ, Brahmā-saṁhitā ṭīkā)
“In the beginning of creation, He who created Brahmā, and then imparted to him knowledge of Brahma—He is the selfsame Lord Kṛṣṇa, who tends cows. Those desirous of liberation should surrender unto that Lord, who reveals the innate function of the soul.”
yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre<br />’staṁ gachchhanti nāma-rūpe vihāya<br />tathā vidvān nāma-rūpad vimuktāḥ<br />parāt paraṁ puruṣam upaiti divyam
(Muṇḍaka-upaniṣad: 3.2.8)
“As flowing rivers, abandoning their names and forms, return to the ocean, so the enlightened souls, being completely liberated from their mundane names and forms, meet the supramundane Supreme Personality of Godhead.”
In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>:
tasmāt tvam uddhavotsṛjya chodanāṁ pratichodanām<br />pravṛttiñ cha nivṛttiñ cha śrotavyaṁ śrutam eva cha<br />mām ekam eva śaraṇam ātmānaṁ sarva-dehinām<br />yāhi sarvātma-bhāvena mayā syā hy akuto-bhayaḥ
(11.12.14–15)
[Kṛṣṇa says:] “O Uddhava, totally abandoning the Vedas and their auxiliaries, all of their prescriptions and prohibitions, and everything you have ever heard or may come to hear, take exclusive shelter of Me, the life of all beings, with all your heart. By My grace you will become completely fearless.”
devarṣi-bhūtāpta-nṛṇāṁ pitṝṇāṁ<br />na kiṅkaro nāyam ṛṇī cha rājan<br />sarvātmanā yaḥ śaraṇaṁ śaraṇyaṁ<br />gato mukundaṁ parihṛtya kartam
(11.5.41)
“One who has completely abandoned all worldly duties and surrendered wholeheartedly unto the ultimate shelter, Mukunda, is no longer a debtor to, nor a servant of, the demigods, sages, other living entities, relatives, mankind, or ancestors.”
martyo yadā tyakta-samasta-karmā<br />niveditātmā vichikīrṣito me<br />tadāmṛtatvaṁ pratipadyamāno<br />mayātma-bhūyāya cha kalpate vai
(11.29.34)
[Kṛṣṇa says to Uddhava:] “When a mortal being completely abandons all mundane endeavours, surrenders themself unto Me, and acts according to My desires, he attains immortality and becomes fit to associate with Me.”
yeṣāṁ sa eva bhagavān dayayed anantaḥ<br />sarvātmanāśrita-pado yadi nirvyalīkam<br />te dustarām atitaranti cha deva-māyāṁ<br />naiṣāṁ mamāham iti dhīḥ śva-śṛgāla-bhakṣye
(2.7.42)
“If one wholeheartedly takes shelter of the Infinite Supreme Lord’s feet, the Lord bestows His true mercy upon him and he thereby transcends the Lord’s insurmountable māyā. The Lord does not bestow His mercy upon those who ascribe the conceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ to the material body, which is nothing more than food for jackals and dogs.”
kaḥ paṇḍitas tvad aparaṁ śaraṇaṁ samīyād<br />bhakta-priyād ṛta-giraḥ suhṛdaḥ kṛta-jñāt<br />sarvān dadāti suhṛdo bhajato ’bhikāmān<br />ātmānam apy upachayāpachayau na yasya
(10.48.26)
“O Lord, You are the truthful, grateful, and affectionate friend of Your devotees. What learned person would ever take shelter of any­one but You? You fulfil all the desires of Your friends who serve You—You even give Your very self to them—and yet You are neither augmented nor diminished thereby.”
aho bakī yaṁ stana-kāla-kūṭaṁ<br />jighāṁsayāpāyayad apy asādhvī<br />lebhe gatiṁ dhātry-uchitāṁ tato ’nyaṁ<br />kaṁ vā dayāluṁ śaraṇaṁ vrajema
(3.2.23)
[Lamenting in separation, Uddhava marvels:] “Oh! Even though the wicked Pūtanā nursed Kṛṣṇa with her poison-smeared breasts, intending to kill Him, Kṛṣṇa granted her a position befitting His mother! Of what merciful Lord shall we take shelter other than Him?”
kiṁ durāpādanaṁ teṣāṁ puṁsām uddāma-chetasām<br />yair āśritas tīrtha-padaś charaṇo vyasanātyayaḥ
(3.23.42)
“The Supreme Lord’s feet destroy all material attachment. What remains unobtainable for even persons of agitated mind who surrender unto them?”
nāham ātmānam āśāse mad-bhaktaiḥ sādhubhir vinā<br />śriyaṁ chātyantikīṁ brahman yeṣāṁ gatir ahaṁ parā
(9.4.64)
[Nārāyaṇ declares to Durvāsā Muni:] “O brāhmaṇ, without My devotees, those sādhus for whom I am the only shelter, I desire neither the bliss of My own nature nor My six eternal opulences.”
samāśritā ye pada-pallava-plavaṁ<br />mahat-padaṁ puṇya-yaśo murāreḥ<br />bhavāmbudhir vatsa-padaṁ paraṁ padaṁ<br />padaṁ padaṁ yad vipadāṁ na teṣām
(10.14.58)
“For those who have taken refuge in the supreme shelter—the boat of the lotus feet of Śrī Murāri, who is renowned as purity personified—the ocean of material existence becomes as insignificant as the water contained in a calf’s hoof-print. Their destination is the supreme abode, never this world where there is danger at every step.”
chiram iha vṛjinārtas tapyamāno ’nutāpair<br />avitṛṣa-ṣaḍ-amitro ’labdha-śāntiḥ kathañchit<br />śaraṇa-da samupetas tvat-padābjaṁ parātman<br />abhayam ṛtam aśokaṁ pāhi māpannam īśa
(10.51.57)
“O Supreme Soul, for so long in this world I have been tor­mented by sin, burned by remorse, and constantly harassed by my six insatiable enemies. I have never obtained peace. O Bestower of Shelter, somehow I have come before Your lotus feet, which are the abode of fearlessness, sorrowlessness, and immortality. O Lord, please protect me; I am in danger.”
tan me bhavān khalu vṛtaḥ patir aṅga jāyām<br />ātmārpitaś cha bhavato ’tra vibho vidhehi<br />mā vīra-bhāgam abhimarśatu chaidya ārād<br />gomāyu-van mṛga-pater balim ambujākṣa
(10.52.39)
[A letter of appeal from Rukmiṇī to Kṛṣṇa:] “O lotus-eyed Lord, I have chosen You as my husband and offered myself unto You. Therefore, O Almighty One, please come and take me as Your wife, before Śiśupāl, like a jackal plundering a lion’s prey, suddenly touches me; I am to be enjoyed by You alone.”
In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span>:
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja<br />ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śuchaḥ
(18.66)
“Abandon all forms of religion and surrender exclusively unto Me. I will liberate you from all sin. Do not despair.”
tam eva śaraṇaṁ gachchha sarva-bhāvena bhārata<br />tat-prasādāt parāṁ śāntiṁ sthānaṁ prāpsyasi śāśvatam
(18.62)
“O Arjun, surrender unto the Lord in all respects. By His grace you will attain His eternal abode and supreme peace.”
daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā<br />mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te
(7.14)
“My alluring, trimodal māyā is insurmountable. Only those who surrender unto Me can transcend māyā.”
bahūnāṁ janmanām ante jñānavān māṁ prapadyate<br />vāsudevaḥ sarvam iti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ
(7.19)
“After many births, an enlightened soul surrenders unto Me, realising, ‘Vāsudev is everything’. Such a great soul is extremely rare.”
And so on. In the <span class="e3">Viṣṇu-purāṇa</span>:
smṛte sakala-kalyāṇa-bhājanaṁ yatra jāyate<br />puruṣas tam ajaṁ nityaṁ vrajāmi śaraṇaṁ harim
“Upon remembering Śrī Hari, the soul becomes a recipient of all auspiciousness. I take shelter of Him, the unborn, eternal Supreme Lord.”
In the <span class="e3">Brahma-vaivarta-purāṇa</span>:
prāpyāpi durlabhataraṁ mānuṣyaṁ vibudhepsitam<br />yair āśrito na govindas tair ātmā vañchitaś chiram
“Those who attain a human birth, which is extremely rare and desired by even the demigods, but do not take shelter of Govinda deceive themselves perpetually.”
In the <span class="e3">Bṛhan-nāradīya-purāṇa</span>:
saṁsāre ’smin mahā-ghore moha-nidrā-samākule<br />ye hariṁ śaraṇaṁ yānti te kṛtārtha na saṁśayaḥ
“Within this ghastly material world, which is engulfed in ignorance and sleep, those who surrender unto the Supreme Lord are successful in all their endeavours. Of this there is no doubt.”
paramārtham aśeṣasya jagatām ādi kāraṇam<br />śaraṇyaṁ śaraṇaṁ yāto govindaṁ nāvasīdati
“Govinda is the origin of all the universes, the Supreme Truth, and the ultimate shelter. One who surrenders unto Him never falls down.”
In the <span class="e3">Padma-purāṇa</span>:
ahaṅkṛtir ma-kāraḥ syān na-kāras tan niṣedhakaḥ<br />tasmāt tu namasā kṣetri-svātantryaṁ pratiṣidhyate<br />bhagavat-paratantro ’sau tadāyatātma-jīvanaḥ<br />tasmāt sva-sāmarthya-vidhiṁ tyajet sarvam aśeṣataḥ
“In the word <span class="e3">namaḥ</span> (‘obeisance’), the syllable <span class="e3">ma</span> indicates the self-asserting ego (<span class="e3">ahaṅkār</span>, lit. ‘I am the doer’), and the syllable <span class="e3">na </span>indicates its prevention. Thus, the act of offering obeisance (namaḥ) nullifies the offerer’s independence. The soul is by nature subordinate to the Supreme Lord; their innate function is servitude to Him. Therefore, all actions performed with the conception, ‘I am the doer’ should be utterly abandoned.”
In the <span class="e3">Nārasiṁha-purāṇa</span>:
tvāṁ prapanno ’smi śaraṇaṁ deva-devaṁ janārdanam<br />iti yaḥ śaraṇaṁ prāptas taṁ kleśād uddharāmy aham
“I deliver from all suffering one who takes shelter of Me, declaring, ‘O Supreme Refuge, O Lord of Lords, O Janārdan, I am surrendered unto You.’”
sarvāchāra-vivarjitāḥ śaṭha-dhiyo vrātyā jagad-vañchakā<br />dambhāhaṅkṛti-pāna-paiśuna-parāḥ pāpāntyajā niṣṭhurāḥ<br />ye chānye dhana-dāra-putra-niratāḥ sarvādhamās te ’pi hi<br />śrī-govinda-padāravinda-śaraṇā muktā bhavanti dvija
“O twice-born, persons who are devoid of all virtuous practices, deceitful, uncultured, fraudulent, arrogant, egotistical, addicted to intoxicants, sinful, malicious, cruel-natured, grossly infatuated with son, wife, wealth, and so forth—even such extremely fallen persons are liberated by surrendering unto the lotus feet of Śrī Govinda.”
In the <span class="e3">Rāmāyaṇa</span>:
sakṛd eva prapanno yas tavāsmīti cha yāchate<br />abhayaṁ sarvadā tasmai dadāmy etad vrataṁ mama
(Rāmāyaṇa: Yuddha-kāṇḍa, 18.33)
[Rāmchandra proclaims:] “Anyone who even once sincerely surren­ders unto Me, declaring, ‘I am Yours’, and prays for fearlessness—it is My vow that I will always grant that to them.”
Examples of expressions of śaraṇāgati from the writings of the Āchāryas prior to Śrīman Mahāprabhu:
Śrī Yāmun Āchārya:
na dharma-niṣṭho ’smi na chātma-vedī<br />na bhaktimāṁs tvach-charaṇāravinde<br />akiñchano ’nanya-gatiḥ śaraṇya<br />tvat-pāda-mūlaṁ śaraṇam prapadye
(Śrī Stotra-ratna: 22)
“O Supreme Refuge, I am not religious, I do not know the nature of the soul, and I do not have any devotion to Your lotus feet. I am bereft and have no other shelter. Such as I am, I surrender unto the soles of Your feet.”
Śrī Kulaśekhar:
bhava-jaladhi-gatānāṁ dvandva-vātāhatānāṁ<br />suta-duhitṛ-kalatra-trāṇa-bhārārditānām<br />viṣama-viṣaya-toye majjatām aplavānāṁ<br />bhavati śaraṇam eko viṣṇu-poto narāṇām
(Mukunda-mālā-stotra: 11)
“For those persons who have fallen into the ocean of mundane existence; who are being lashed by the hurricane of duality; who are crushed by the burden of maintaining their wife, family, and so on; who are drowning in the ghastly whirlpool of sensual pleasures and bereft of a vessel—the only shelter is the lifeboat of the Supreme Lord.”
And so on and so forth.
The teachings of śaraṇāgati given to the world by the supremely merciful Avatār, Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, are of unparalleled greatness. This is because His teachings are able to bestow the fortune of loving service (prema-sevā) to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the ori­gin and embodiment of all rasas. In this book Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s follower, the great soul Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, has taught the souls of this world those very teachings of śaraṇāgati.
It is certain that the supreme feet of Viṣṇu and the service of Kṛṣṇa are attainable through śaraṇāgati. The Supreme Lord is by nature affectionate to the surrendered souls (Śaraṇāgata-vatsal); He dispels their suffering and showers His supramundane sweetness upon their hearts.
Some have said that śaraṇāgati is realisation of the non-separateness of all living beings and objects which is brought about by vision of the indwelling omnipresence of the Supreme Lord. Such realisation, however, is a part of jñāna-bhakti (devotion adulterated by knowledge); it is not integral to pure devotion.
We, as enjoyers who have forgotten the Lord, are perpetually burning in the blazing fire of the threefold miseries of this illusory universe. Various evil desires (anarthas) have made us forgetful of our true selves—that we are Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s servants and children of nectar—and turned us into slaves of māyā.
Thus the magnanimous Ṭhākur, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod, being sorrowful about the sorrow of others, has sung:
vinoda kahe hāya! hāya!<br />hari-dāsa hari nāhi pāya
“Alas! Alas! The Lord’s servants have not attained the Lord!”
We cannot attain happiness in this world by our own persistent endeavours because we have rejected happiness Himself, ecstasy Himself, the embodiment of all rasas (Akhila-rasāmṛta-mūrti), Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
To attain true happiness, we must serve that Supreme Person whom the Vedas have described with the expression <span class="e3">Raso vai Saḥ</span>. Thus, the great souls have said that there is no other recourse for the souls than to become detached from this world (niṣkiñchan) and surrender to the lotus feet of that Supreme Person—ecstasy Himself.
Without śaraṇāgati, the state of truly being ‘His own’ (‘tadīyatva’) is never realised. Thus, the learned profusely praise śaraṇāgati’s unprecedented fruit.
In the <span class="e3">Vaiṣṇava-tantra</span>, the characteristics of śaraṇāgati have been explained as follows:
ānukūlyasya saṅkalpaḥ prātikūlya-vivarjanam<br />rakṣiṣyatīti viśvāso goptṛtve varaṇaṁ tathā<br />ātma-nikṣepa-kārpaṇye ṣaḍ-vidhā śaraṇāgatiḥ
“Accepting everything favourable, rejecting everything unfavour­able, being confident that Kṛṣṇa will grant His protection, embra­cing Kṛṣṇa’s guardianship, fully offering one’s self to Kṛṣṇa, and feeling oneself to be lowly are the six aspects of śaraṇāgati.”
Among these six aspects, goptṛtve varaṇam (‘embracing the Lord’s guardianship’) is the complete embodiment (aṅgī) of śaraṇāgati; the other five aspects are limbs (aṅgas).
There are three ways in which one embraces the Lord as one’s guardian: physically, verbally, and mentally. These are described in <span class="e3">Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</span>:
tavāsmīti vadan vāchā tathaiva manasā vidan<br />tat-sthānam āśritas tanvā modate śaraṇāgataḥ
“Declaring with their words, ‘I am Yours’, knowing this within their mind, and taking shelter of Your abode with their body, the surrendered soul rejoices.”
Surrender performed in full in these three ways swiftly grants complete success. Otherwise, the result obtained is proportionate to the depth of one’s surrender.
In order to learn śaraṇāgati, one must first fall at the feet of Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, the teacher of śaraṇagati to the souls who is the personification of the ideal of supramundane devotion (and non-different from the āchāryas Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Sanātan), and pray:
kā̐diyā kā̐diyā bale—‘āmi ta’ adhama<br />śikhāye śaraṇāgati karahe uttama’
“Crying incessantly, I pray, ‘I am so lowly! Please elevate me by teaching me śaraṇāgati.’”
In the teachings of our Param Gurudev, the supremely worshippable, radiant Vaiṣṇava Āchārya Om Viṣṇupād Śrī Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Goswāmī Prabhupād, we find: “The good fortune of the world will be realised by profuse preaching of the songs of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>.” Thus, in accordance with Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākur’s teachings and desire, our dearly beloved Gurudev, the embodiment of eternal ecstasy (Nityānanda), Om Viṣṇupād Aṣṭottara-śata-śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj, has, for the ultimate welfare of all souls, written a befitting commentary for relishing the poetry of <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> known as<span class="e3"> Śrī Laghu-chandrikā</span>.
This edition has been compiled to help those desirous of shelter to see the way of progress towards the feet of the Lord. Only after obtaining my Gurudev’s merciful blessings, which bestow good fortune upon the world, has an unworthy and fallen servant such as I become engaged in the publication of this book.
In this connection I could not restrain my eagerness to cite his unprecedented treatise on śaraṇāgati, the compilation known as <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span>. Within that book are recorded numerous fundamental truths, conceptual analyses, and so forth, related to surrender, which are essential for faithful and inquisitive persons to understand.
This edition has been published for the welfare of the world. For the convenience of elderly readers, it has been formatted with large lettered type-setting for the main text and slightly smaller lettered type-setting for the commentary. It has also been furnished at the end with a collection of prayers by surrendered souls (<span class="e3">Śaraṇāgatera Prārthanā</span>) and prayers unto Śrī Guru (<span class="e3">Śrī Guru Vandanā</span>).
On account of my various shortcomings, there is no doubt that faults and omissions have occurred within this beautiful book. O Vaiṣṇavas—saviours of the fallen—and well-wishing readers, please bestow your forgiveness and affectionate mercy on this fallen soul; purify him and make him fit to serve Śrī Guru and Śrī Gaurāṅga.
In conclusion, this humble soul’s prayer at the feet of Śrī Hari, Guru, and Vaiṣṇava is that this book, <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>, may reveal her innate supramundane sweetness all over the world and thereby bestow eternal welfare upon the souls.
The Editor
Śrī Gaurendu Brahmachārī Vidyārañjan<span class="e13">3</span>

শ্রীলঘুচন্দ্রিকাভাষ্য – মঙ্গলাচরণ
Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya <br />– Maṅgalācharaṇa
Gentle Moonlight Commentary <br />– Invocation of Auspiciousness
মহাপ্রভু শ্রীচৈতন্য<span class="e22">	রাধাকৃষ্ণ নহে অন্য<br /></span><span class="e23">	রূপানুগ জনের জীবন ।<br /></span>বিশ্বম্ভর প্রিয়ঙ্কর<span class="e22">	শ্রীস্বরূপ-দামোদর<br /></span><span class="e23">	শ্রীগোস্বামী রূপ-সনাতন ॥১॥</span>
mahāprabhu śrī-chaitanya,<span class="e5">	rādhā-kṛṣṇa nahe anya,<br /></span><span class="e6">	rūpānuga janerna jīvana<br /></span>viśvambhara priyaṅkara<span class="e5">	śrī svarūpa dāmodara<br /></span><span class="e6">	śrī gosvāmī rūpa-sanātana </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">mahāprabhu śrī-chaitanya</span>–Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">rādhā-kṛṣṇa</span>–Śrī Śrī Gāndharvā Govindasundar; <span class="e2">nahe</span>–is not; <span class="e2">anya</span>–different; <span class="e2">rūpānuga</span>–followers of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">janera</span>–of those persons; <span class="e2">jīvana</span>–the very life; <span class="e2">viśvambhara</span>–Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">priyaṅkara</span>–most dear, pleasing; <span class="e2">śrī svarūpa dāmodara</span>–Śrīla Svarūp Dāmodar; <span class="e2">śrī gosvāmī rūpa-sanātana</span>–Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu and Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu is non-different from Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and is the very life of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu’s followers. Śrīla Svarūp Dāmodar Goswāmī, Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu, and Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Pra­bhu are most dear to Viśvambhar.
রূপপ্রিয় মহাজন<span class="e22">	জীব-রঘুনাথ হন<br /></span><span class="e23">	তাঁর প্রিয় কবি কৃষ্ণদাস ।<br /></span>কৃষ্ণদাস-প্রিয়বর<span class="e22">	নরোত্তম সেবাপর<br /></span><span class="e23">	যাঁর পদ বিশ্বনাথ-আশ ॥২॥</span>
rūpa-priya mahājana<span class="e5">	jīva, raghunātha hana<br /></span><span class="e6">	tā̐ra priya kavi kṛṣṇa-dāsa<br /></span>kṛṣṇa-dāsa priya-vara<span class="e5">	narottama sevā-para,<br /></span><span class="e6">	yā̐ra pada viśvanātha-āśa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">rūpa</span>–to Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">priya</span>–dear; <span class="e2">mahājana</span>–the great souls; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">raghunātha</span>–Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">hana</span>–became; <span class="e2">tā̐ra</span>–their; <span class="e2">priya</span>–dear; <span class="e2">kavi kṛṣṇa-dāsa</span>–Śrīla Kṛṣṇa Dās Kavirāj Goswāmī; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa dāsa</span>–of Śrīla Kṛṣṇa Dās Kavirāj Goswāmī; <span class="e2">priya-vara</span>–dearmost; <span class="e2">narottama</span>–Śrīla Narottam Dās Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">sevā</span>–service; <span class="e2">para</span>–engaged in; <span class="e2">yā̐ra</span>–whose; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">viśvanātha</span>–Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">āśa</span>–aspiration. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> The great souls Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu and Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Prabhu are the dear followers of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu. Their dear follower is Śrīla Kṛṣṇa Dās Kavirāj Goswāmī. His dearmost follower is Śrīla Narottam Dās Ṭhākur, who is ever engaged in divine service. His feet are the aspiration of Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī Ṭhākur.
বিশ্বনাথ ভক্তসাথ<span class="e22">	বলদেব, জগন্নাথ<br /></span><span class="e23">	তাঁর প্রিয় শ্রীভক্তিবিনোদ ।<br /></span>মহাভাগবত-বর<span class="e22">	শ্রীগৌরকিশোর-বর<br /></span><span class="e23">	হরি ভজনেতে যাঁর মোদ ॥৩॥</span>
viśvanātha bhakta-sātha<span class="e5">	baladeva, jagannātha<br /></span><span class="e6">	tā̐ra priya śrī-bhakti-vinoda<br /></span>mahābhāgavata-vara<span class="e5">	śrī gaura-kiśora-vara,<br /></span><span class="e6">	hari-bhajanete yā̐ra moda </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">viśvanātha</span>–Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–devotees; <span class="e2">sātha</span>–with; <span class="e2">baladeva</span>–Śrīla Baladev Vidyābhūṣaṇ; <span class="e2">jagannātha</span>–Śrīla Jagannāth Dās Bābājī; <span class="e2">tā̐ra</span>–his; <span class="e2">priya</span>–dear; <span class="e2">śrī-bhakti-vinoda</span>–Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">mahā</span>–topmost; <span class="e2">bhāgavata</span>–of the devotees; <span class="e2">vara</span>–best; <span class="e2">śrī-gaura-kiśora</span>–Śrīla Gaura Kiśor Dās Bābājī Mahārāj; <span class="e2">vara</span>–the great; <span class="e2">hari</span>–of Śrī Hari; <span class="e2">bhajanete</span>–in the service; <span class="e2">yā̐ra</span>–whose; <span class="e2">moda</span>–joy. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> The foremost devotees of Śrīla Viśvanāth Chakravartī Ṭhākur are Śrīla Baladev Vidyābhūṣaṇ and Śrīla Jagannāth Dās Bābājī. Their dear follower is Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur. His associate is the best of the topmost devotees, Śrīla Gaura Kiśor Dās Bābājī, whose sole joy is the service of Śrī Hari.
তদনুগ মহাজন<span class="e22">	শ্রীকৃষ্ণ-কীর্ত্তন-ধন<br /></span><span class="e23">	যেবা দিল পুরি’ জগ কাম ।<br /></span>শ্রীবার্ষভানবীবরা<span class="e22">	সদা সেব্য সেবাপরা<br /></span><span class="e23">	তাঁহার ‘দয়িতদাস’ নাম ॥৪॥</span>
tadanuga mahājana<span class="e5">	śrī-kṛṣṇa-kīrtana-dhana<br /></span><span class="e6">	yebā dila puri’ jaga kāma<br /></span>śrī-vārṣabhānavī-varā<span class="e5">	sadā sevya-sevā-parā<br /></span><span class="e6">	tā̐hāra ‘dayita-dāsa’ nāma </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tad</span>–His; <span class="e2">anuga</span>–follower; <span class="e2">mahājana</span>–great soul; <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa-kīrtana</span>–the glori­fication of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–the wealth; <span class="e2">yebā</span>–who; <span class="e2">dila</span>–gave; <span class="e2">puri’</span>–fulfilling; <span class="e2">jaga</span>–of the universe; <span class="e2">kāma</span>–desires; <span class="e2">śrī-vārṣabhānavī</span>–of the daughter of Mahārāj Vṛṣābhānu, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; <span class="e2">varā</span>–dearmost; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">sevya</span>–who is to be served—Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Śrī Gurudev; <span class="e2">sevā</span>–service; <span class="e2">parā</span>–engaged in, aspires for; <span class="e2">tā̐hāra</span>–his; <span class="e2">dayita-dāsa</span>–Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–name. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> The follower of Śrīla Gaura Kiśor Dās Bābājī, the great soul Dayita Dās (Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākur), whose wealth is Śrī Kṛṣṇa-kīrtan, fulfils the desires of the whole world. He is the dearmost of Śrī Vārṣabhānavī and is always engaged in Her service.
জীবাভিন্ন দেহ দিব্য<span class="e22">	স্বরূপ-রূপ-রঘু-জীব্য<br /></span><span class="e23">	সদা সেব্য সেই পাদপদ্ম ।<br /></span>যার ভাগ্যোদয় শন্দ<span class="e22">	দাস রামানন্দ মন্দ<br /></span><span class="e23">	শ্রীচন্দ্রিকা দেখে সেবাসদ্ম ॥৫॥</span>
