jīvābhinna deha divya<span class="e5">	svarūpa-rūpa-raghu-jīvya<br /></span><span class="e6">	sadā sevya sei pādapadma<br /></span>yāra bhāgyodaya śanda<span class="e5">	dāsa rāmānanda manda<br /></span><span class="e6">	śrī-chandrikā dekhe sevā-sadma </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jīva</span>–from Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">abhinna</span>–non-different; <span class="e2">deha</span>–form; <span class="e2">divya</span>–divine; <span class="e2">svarūpa</span>–Śrīla Svarūp Dāmodar; <span class="e2">rūpa</span>–Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Pra­bhu; <span class="e2">raghu</span>–Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī; <span class="e2">jīvya</span>–life; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">sevya</span>–who is to be served; <span class="e2">sei</span>–he; <span class="e2">pāda</span>–feet; <span class="e2">padma</span>–lotus; <span class="e2">yāra</span>–whose; <span class="e2">bhāgya</span>–fortune; <span class="e2">udaya</span>–appear; <span class="e2">śanda</span>–auspiciousness; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servitor; <span class="e2">rāmānanda</span>–Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj; <span class="e2">manda</span>–feeble; <span class="e2">śrī-chandrikā</span>–<span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā</span> commentary; <span class="e2">dekhe</span>–sees; <span class="e2">sevā</span>–service; <span class="e2">sadma</span>–temple. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> The divine personage Śrī Dayita Dās is non-different from Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu. His very life is Śrīla Svarūp Dāmodar, Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu, and Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Prabhu. His lotus feet are to be served eternally.
The feeble Rāmānanda Dās, whose good fortune has arisen, sees this <span class="e3">Śrī Laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣya</span> as the temple of his service.
স্বৈরাছারাব্ধি সংমগ্নান্ জীবান্ গৌরাঙ্ঘ্রি-পঙ্কজে ।<br />উদ্ধৃত্য শরণাপত্তে র্মাহাত্ম্যং সমবোধয়ৎ ॥৬॥<br />যস্তস্য ভক্তি-সিদ্ধান্ত-সরস্বতী-প্রভোর্গুরোঃ ।<br />অত্যুদার-পদাম্ভোজ-ধূলিঃ স্যাং জন্ম জন্মনি ॥৭॥
svairāchārābdhi saṁmagnān jīvān gaurāṅghri-paṅkaje<br />uddhṛtya śaraṇāpatter māhātmyaṁ samabodhayat <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />yas tasya bhakti-siddhānta-sarasvatī-prabhor guroḥ<br />atyudāra-padāmbhoja-dhūliḥ syāṁ janma janmani <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">svairāchāra</span>–whimsical activities;<span class="e2"> abdhi</span>–in the ocean;<span class="e2"> saṁmagnān</span>–submerged;<span class="e2"> jīvān</span>–the jīvas;<span class="e2"> gaura</span>–of Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">aṅghri</span>–feet; <span class="e2">paṅkaje</span>–to the lotus;<span class="e2"> uddhṛtya</span>–uplifting;<span class="e2"> śaraṇāpatteḥ</span>–of śaraṇāgati;<span class="e2"> māhātmyam</span>–about the greatness;<span class="e2"> samabodhayat</span>–enlightened; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> bhakti-siddhānta-sarasvatī-prabhoḥ</span>–Śrī Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Prabhupād;<span class="e2"> guroḥ</span>–spiritual master’s; <span class="e2">ati</span>–extremely; <span class="e2">udāra</span>–magnanimous; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">ambhoja</span>–lotus; <span class="e2">dhūliḥ</span>–dust;<span class="e2"> syām</span>–may I be;<span class="e2"> janma</span>–birth;<span class="e2"> janmani</span>–after birth. [<span class="e24">6–7</span>]
(6–7<span class="e14">)</span> Birth after birth, let me be a speck of dust at the supremely magnanimous lotus feet of the universal Guru, Bhagavān Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur, who uplifted the conditioned souls submerged in the ocean of their whimsical activities to the lotus feet of Śrī Gaurāṅga and enlightened them about the greatness of śaraṇāgati.
গুরুদং গ্রন্থদং গৌরধামদং নামদং মুদা ।<br />ভক্তিদং ভূরিদং বন্দে ভক্তিবিনোদকং সদা ॥৮॥
guru-daṁ grantha-daṁ gaura-dhāma-daṁ nāma-daṁ mudā<br />bhakti-daṁ bhūri-daṁ vande bhakti-vinodakaṁ sadā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">guru</span>–of the spiritual master; <span class="e2">dam</span>–giver;<span class="e2"> grantha</span>–of scriptures; <span class="e2">dam</span>–giver;<span class="e2"> gaura</span>–of Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">dhāma</span>–the abode; <span class="e2">dam</span>–giver;<span class="e2"> nāma</span>–of the Name; <span class="e2">dam</span>–giver;<span class="e2"> mudā</span>–joy;<span class="e2"> bhakti</span>–of devotion; <span class="e2">dam</span>–giver;<span class="e2"> bhūri</span>–abundance; <span class="e2">dam</span>–giver;<span class="e2"> vande</span>–I offer my obeisance;<span class="e2"> bhakti-vinodakaṁ</span>–Śrī Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur;<span class="e2"> sadā</span>–always.<span class="e2"> </span>[<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> I perpetually offer my obeisance unto Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur with great joy. <span class="e3">Guru-dam</span>: he is (first and foremost) the giver of Śrī Guru—Bhagavān Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur (the inaugurator of the new era of Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavism). <span class="e3">Grantha-dam</span>: he is the author of numerous commentaries, treatises, articles, novels, and songbooks (which represent the condensed essence of revealed truth). <span class="e3">Gaura-dhāma-dam</span>: he is the revealer of the abode of Śrīman Mahāprabhu (which had become lost due to the course of time). <span class="e3">Nāma-dam</span>: he is the giver of the Name (the proper conception of the Name). <span class="e3">Bhakti-dam</span>: he is the giver of pure devotion (the proper conception of pure devotion in the line of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu). <span class="e3">Bhūri-dam</span>: he is the bestower of an abundance of divine fortune (ultimately, the service of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī).
ভক্তি-বিনোদ-দেবেন ‘শরণাগতি’-নামিকা ।<br />রচিতা পুস্তিকা কাচিত্তস্যা ভাষ্যে কৃতোদ্যমঃ ॥৯॥
bhakti-vinoda-devena ‘śaraṇāgati’-nāmikā<br />rachitā pustikā kāchit tasyā bhāṣye kṛtodyamaḥ <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">9</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakti-vinoda-devena</span>–by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur;<span class="e2"> ‘śaraṇāgati’</span>–as ‘<span class="e3">Śaraṇā­gati</span>’; <span class="e2">nāmikā</span>–entitled;<span class="e2"> rachitā</span>–composed;<span class="e2"> pustikā</span>–short book;<span class="e2"> kāchit</span>–some;<span class="e2"> tasyāḥ</span>–­on her;<span class="e2"> bhāṣye</span>–in regard to a commentary;<span class="e2"> kṛta</span>–done; <span class="e2">udyamaḥ</span>–undertaking.<span class="e2"> </span>[<span class="e24">9</span>]
(9<span class="e14">)</span> Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur composed a short book entitled <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span> upon which I have written a commentary.
ইদানীমতিমন্দোঽপি ভক্তেভ্যো ভক্তিসংগ্রহে ।<br />শ্রীলঘু-চন্দ্রিকাভাষ্যং প্রকাশার্থং দদাম্যহম্ ॥১০॥
idānīm atimando ’pi bhaktebhyo bhakti-saṁgrahe<br />śrī-laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣyaṁ prakāśārthaṁ dadāmyaham <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">10</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">idānīm</span>–now;<span class="e2"> ati</span>–very<span class="e2">; mandaḥ</span>–dull-witted;<span class="e2"> api</span>–although;<span class="e2"> bhaktebhyaḥ</span>–to the devotees;<span class="e2"> bhakti</span>–devotion; <span class="e2">saṁgrahe</span>–in representing;<span class="e2"> śrī-laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣyaṁ</span>–<span class="e3">Gentle Moonlight Commentary</span>;<span class="e2"> prakāśa</span>–of illumination; <span class="e2">artham</span>–for the purpose;<span class="e2"> dadāmi</span>–give;<span class="e2"> aham</span>–I.<span class="e2"> </span>[<span class="e24">10</span>]
(10<span class="e14">)</span> Now, though I am very dull-witted, for the sake of illumination, I offer the devotees this <span class="e3">Gentle Moonlight Commentary</span>, which represents the conclusions of pure devotion.

মুখবন্ধ
Preface
by Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanyadev has clearly declared within this material world the message that the fortune of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema, divine love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa, which condemns the four ends of conven­tional reli­gion—dharma, piety; artha, wealth; kāma, enjoyment; and mokṣa, liberation—is the fifth and supreme end of human life. Śaraṇāgati is the sole means to obtain that topmost end of human life. To enlighten the souls conditioned in the material world about this, and to reveal the process of śaraṇāgati, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanyadev Himself descended, along with His eternal asso­ciates and divine abode Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām. He taught śaraṇā­gati through His own practice and preaching, as well as through the practice and preaching of His capable servants. Some time later, one of His devotee-associates, Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, gave extensive guidance about the practice of śaraṇāgati through analysis and description of its limbs and sub-limbs in this small book named <span class="e3">Śaraṇāgati</span>.
Prior to Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, other Āchāryas also spoke at length about śaraṇāgati. Additionally, the fundamental teachings of śaraṇāgati are found within <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span> and <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span>. The subject of śaraṇāgati is also especially well known within the Śrī sampradāya. Still, the way in which Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanyachandra has revealed the fundamental nature of śaraṇāgati is unparalleled; He has taught that śaraṇāgati is the appropriate means of attaining the fortune of the divine loving service (prema-sevā) of Vrajendra Nandan Kṛṣṇa, the whimsical enjoyer of the wives of the cowherd men of Vraja, whose divine form is the origin of the Absolute Truth. Therefore, in order to distribute these illustrious teachings of śaraṇāgati, Śrīmad Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur has invoked the benediction of that supreme munifi­cent origin of all Avatārs, Śrī Chaitanyachandra, by first mentioning His name while establishing the theme of his treatise within his invocation of auspiciousness.

শরণাগতি – মঙ্গলাচরণ
Śaraṇāgati – Maṅgalācharaṇa
Surrender – Invocation of Auspiciousness
(১)
(1)
শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য প্রভু জীবে দয়া করি’ ।<br />স্বপার্ষদ স্বীয় ধাম সহ অবতরি’ ॥১॥
śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya prabhu jīve dayā kari’<br />sva-pārṣada svīya dhāma saha avatari’ <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya</span>–Śrī Gaurasundar; <span class="e2">prabhu</span>–Lord; <span class="e2">jīve</span>–to the conditioned souls; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy;<span class="e2"> kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">sva-pārṣada</span>–His own associates; <span class="e2">svīya</span>–His own; <span class="e2">dhāma</span>–abode; <span class="e2">saha</span>–with; <span class="e2">avatari’</span>–descending. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> Being merciful to the souls, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu descends with His associates and abode.
(1<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya:</span> ‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya’ is the sannyās name of Śrī Gaurasundar. Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭāchārya uses this name in his prayers to the Lord:
kālān naṣṭaṁ bhakti-yogaṁ nijaṁ yaḥ<br />prāduṣkartuṁ kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-nāmā<br />āvirbhūtas tasya pādāravinde<br />gāḍhaṁ gāḍhaṁ līyatāṁ chitta-bhṛṅgaḥ
(Śrī Chaitanya-bhāgavat: Antya-līlā, 3.123)
“May the honeybee of my heart be ever more deeply attached to the lotus feet of He who has now appeared as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya to revive the practice of devotion to Himself, which had become lost due to the influence of time.”
In<span class="e3"> Śrī Chaitanya-bhāgavat</span> (Madhya-līlā, 28.175–176, 181), Śrī Gaurasundar’s sannyās ceremony is described:
yata jagatere tumi ‘kṛṣṇa’ bolāilā<br />karāilā chaitanya—kīrtana prakāśilā<br />eteke tomāra nāma śrī kṛṣṇa chaitanya<br />sarvaloka tomā’ haite yāte haila dhanya
[Śrī Keśava Bharatī said:] “You have induced the whole world to chant Kṛṣṇa’s Name and brought everyone to life (chaitanya) by inau­gurating the saṅkīrtan movement. Therefore Your name will be ‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya’. Because of You, everyone in the whole universe has become fortunate.”
hena mate sannyāsa kariyā prabhu dhanya<br />prakāśila ātma-nāma “śrī kṛṣṇa chaitanya”
“In this way, the Lord gloriously accepted sannyās and revealed His name ‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya’.”
<span class="e2">sva-pārṣada: </span>“His associates.” This means His servants, as is implied in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(9.25):
yānti deva-vratā devān pitṝn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ<br />bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti mad-yājino ’pi mām
“Those who are devoted to the demigods go to the realm of the demigods; those who are devoted to the ancestors go to the realm of their ancestors; those who are devoted to ghosts and spirits go to the realm of such beings; and those who are devoted to Me come to Me (reside in My abode).”
<span class="e2">dhāma: </span>“Abode.” This means the spiritual domain of the Lord. Kṛṣṇa describes His abode in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(15.6):
na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ<br />yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama
“Having reached My supreme abode, which cannot be illuminated by the sun, the moon, or fire (anything material), the surrendered souls never return to this mundane world.”
অত্যন্ত দুর্ল্লভ প্রেম করিবারে দান ।<br />শিখায় শরণাগতি ভকতের প্রাণ ॥২॥
atyanta durlabha prema karibāre dāna<br />śikhāya śaraṇāgati bhakatera prāṇa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">atyanta</span>–extremely; <span class="e2">durlabha</span>–rare, precious, difficult to obtain; <span class="e2">prema</span>–divine love; <span class="e2">karibāre</span>–in order to do; <span class="e2">dāna</span>–distribution; <span class="e2">śikhāya</span>–teaches; <span class="e2">śaraṇāgati</span>–surrender; <span class="e2">bhakatera</span>–of the devotees; <span class="e2">prāṇa</span>–the life. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> To distribute the most rare form of prema, He teaches śaraṇāgati, which is the life of the devotees.
(<span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> atyanta durlabha prema:</span> “The most rare form of prema.” This refers to the fifth (ultimate) end of human life: Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema. The rarity of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema has been noted by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu in his <span class="e3">Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu </span>(1.1.36):
jñānataḥ sulabhā muktir bhuktir yajñādi-puṇyataḥ<br />seyaṁ sādhana-sāhasrair hari-bhaktiḥ sudurlabhā
[Śiva says:] “Liberation (mokṣa) is easily attained by cultivating knowledge of Brahma (jñān). Heavenly enjoyment (bhukti) is easily attained by performing various types of pious activities (karma), such as sacrifices. However, even by following thousands of different spiritual practices, Hari-bhakti is extremely difficult to attain (as it requires: servitude to the Lord’s pure devotees; a proper conception of the Lord’s divine nature; firmly fixed loving attachment for the Lord devoid of any impurities (āsakti); and the Lord’s merciful acceptance of the practitioner).”
In <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> (Ādi-līlā, 1.4), this most rare form of prema, which Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu came to distribute, is described as follows:
anarpita-charīṁ chirāt karuṇayāvatīrṇaḥ kalau<br />samarpayitum unnatojjvala-rasāṁ sva-bhakti-śriyam<br />hariḥ puraṭa-sundara-dyuti-kadamba-sandīpitaḥ<br />sadā hṛdaya-kandare sphuratu vaḥ śachī-nandanaḥ
“May the radiant, golden Lord, Śrī Śachī Nandan, always be manifest in the core of your heart. He mercifully descended in the Age of Kali to give the wealth devotion to Himself—supremely exalted madhura-rasa—which had never been given before.”
<span class="e2">śaraṇāgati:</span> “Surrender.” This means to take shelter of the Lord in all respects. Śaraṇāgati is defined in essence in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (1.35):
bhagavad-bhaktitaḥ sarvam ity utsṛjya vidher api<br />kaiṅkaryaṁ kṛṣṇa-pādaikāśrayatvaṁ śaraṇāgatiḥ
“Having faith that everything is attained by serving the Supreme Lord, abandoning subservience to even scriptural injunctions, and taking shelter of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s feet exclusively, is known as <span class="e3">śaraṇāgati</span>.”
দৈন্য, আত্মনিবেদন, গোপ্তৃত্বে বরণ ।<br />‘অবশ্য রক্ষিবে কৃষ্ণ’—বিশ্বাস পালন ॥৩॥<br />ভক্তি-অনুকূল মাত্র কার্য্যের স্বীকার ।<br />ভক্তি-প্রতিকূল-ভাব বর্জ্জনাঙ্গীকার ॥৪॥<br />ষড়অঙ্গ শরণাগতি হইবে যাঁহার ।<br />তাঁহার প্রার্থনা শুনে শ্রীনন্দকুমার ॥৫॥
dainya, ātma-nivedana, goptṛtve varaṇa<br />‘avaśya rakṣibe kṛṣṇa’—viśvāsa pālana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />bhakti-anukūla-mātra kāryera svīkāra<br />bhakti-pratikūla-bhāva varjanāṅgīkāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />ṣaḍ-aṅga śaraṇāgati ha-ibe yā̐hāra<br />tā̐hāra prārthanā śune śrī-nanda-kumāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dainya</span>–humility; <span class="e2">ātma</span>–self; <span class="e2">nivedana—</span>submission; <span class="e2">goptṛtve</span>–of guardianship; <span class="e2">varaṇa</span>–acceptance; <span class="e2">avaśya</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">rakṣibe</span>–will protect; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–the Supreme Personality of Godhead; <span class="e2">viśvāsa</span>–faith; <span class="e2">pālana</span>–maintenance; <span class="e2">bhakti</span>–to devotion; <span class="e2">anukūla</span>–favourable; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">kāryera</span>–of actions; <span class="e2">svīkāra</span>–acceptance; <span class="e2">bhakti</span>–to devotion; <span class="e2">pratikūla</span>–unfavourable; <span class="e2">bhāva</span>–nature, disposition; <span class="e2">varjana</span>–rejection; <span class="e2">aṅgīkāra</span>–acceptance. [<span class="e24">3–4</span>]
<span class="e2">ṣaḍ</span>–six; <span class="e2">aṅga (prakāra aṅgera dvārā)</span>–aspects (by way of these); <span class="e2">śaraṇāgati (prapatti)</span>–surrender; <span class="e2">ha-ibe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">yā̐hāra</span>–whose; <span class="e2">tā̐hāra</span>–his; <span class="e2">prārthanā</span>–prayers; <span class="e2">śune</span>–hears; <span class="e2">śrī-nanda-kumāra</span>–Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda Mahārāj. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(3–5<span class="e14">)</span> Humility, self-submission, embracing the Lord’s guardianship, maintaining the faith that ‘Kṛṣṇa will certainly protect me’, engaging only in activities which are favourable to devo­tion, and rejecting everything unfavourable to devotion—Śrī Nanda Kumar hears the prayers of one who surrenders in this six-fold way.
(<span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> dainya:</span> “Humility.” This is also known as <span class="e3">kārpaṇya</span>, experience of one’s lamentable condition. <span class="e3">Dainya</span> has been defined in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (8.1–2):
bhagavan rakṣa rakṣaivam ārta-bhāvena sarvataḥ<br />asamorddhva-dayā-sindhor hareḥ kāruṇya-vaibhavam<br />smaratāṁś cha viśeṣeṇa nijāti-śochya-nīchatām<br />bhaktānām ārti-bhāvas tu kārpaṇyaṁ kathyate budhaiḥ
“‘O Lord, please protect me, protect me …’ Praying thus in a mood of distress, while remembering in all respects the greatness of the mercy of the Supreme Lord, the unparalleled ocean of compassion, and remembering in particular one’s own most lamentable lowliness—this condition of the devotees is described by the learned as <span class="e3">kārpaṇya</span>.”
<span class="e2">ātma-nivedana: </span>“Self-submission.” This is also known as <span class="e3">ātmotsarga</span>, self-dedication, and has been defined in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (7.4):
kṛṣṇāyārpita-dehasya nirmamasyānahaṅkrteḥ<br />manasas tat svarūpatvaṁ smṛtam ātmā-nivedanam
“<span class="e3">Ātmā-nivedan </span>is known as the condition of having offered one’s self to Kṛṣṇa (solely to satisfy Him), while being devoid of possessiveness and false egotism.”
<span class="e2">goptṛtve varaṇa: </span>“Embracing the Lord’s guardianship.” This is also referred to as accepting the Lord as one’s maintainer and has been defined in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (6.1–2):
he kṛṣṇa! pāhi māṁ nātha kṛpayātmagataṁ kuru<br />ity evaṁ prārthanaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ prāptuṁ svāmi-svarūpataḥ<br />goptṛtve varaṇam jñeyaṁ bhaktair hṛdyataraṁ param<br />prapatty ekārthakatvena tad aṅgitvena tat smṛtam
“‘O Kṛṣṇa, please protect me! O Lord, kindly accept me as Your own.’ This prayer to attain Śrī Kṛṣṇa as one’s master is supremely pleasing to the hearts of the devotees and is known as <span class="e3">goptṛtve varaṇam</span>, ‘embracing the Lord’s guardianship’. Goptṛtve varaṇam expresses the very ideal of surrender and is thus considered to be its complete embodi­ment (aṅgī). (The other five aspects of surrender are considered limbs (aṅgas).)”
<span class="e2">‘avaśya rakṣibe kṛṣṇa’:</span> “Kṛṣṇa will certainly protect me.” This refers to faith that ‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa will assuredly grant His protection’ and has been defined in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (5.1):
rakṣiṣyati hi mām kṛṣṇo bhaktānāṁ bāndhavaś cha saḥ<br />kṣemam vidhāsyatīti yad viśvāso ’traiva gṛhyate
“‘Certainly Kṛṣṇa will protect me, because He is the true friend of the devotees. He will definitely bless me with all good fortune.’ Herein, such faith is sustained.”
(<span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> anukūla</span>:<span class="e2"> </span>“Favourable.” This refers to anything helpful for attaining Kṛṣṇa and has been defined in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (3.1):
kṛṣṇa-kārṣṇaga-sad-bhakti prapannatvānukūlake<br />kṛtyatva-niśchayaś chānukūlya-saṅkalpa uchyate
“Resolute conviction to do everything that is favourable to the service of Kṛṣṇa, to the service of His devotees, and to surrender, is called <span class="e3">ānukūlyasya-saṅkalpaḥ, </span>acceptance of the favourable.”
<span class="e2">pratikūla: </span>“Unfavourable.” This refers to anything that is an obstacle to attaining Kṛṣṇa, and has been defined in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span> (4.1):
bhagavad-bhaktayor bhakteḥ prapatteḥ pratikūlake<br />varjyatve niśchayaḥ prātikūlya-varjanam uchyate
“Resolute conviction to abandon everything that is opposed to the service of the Lord, to the service of His devotees, and to surrender, is called <span class="e3">prātikūlya-varjanam, </span>rejection of the unfavourable.”
(5<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">ṣaḍ-aṅga śaraṇāgati: </span>“Surrenders in this six-fold way.” The six aspects of surrender are defined within <span class="e3">Śrī Vāyu-purāṇa</span> and the<span class="e3"> Vaiṣṇava-tantra</span>:
ānukūlyasya saṅkalpaḥ prātikūlya-vivarjanam<br />rakṣiṣyatīti viśvāso goptṛtve varaṇaṁ tathā<br />ātma-nikṣepa kārpaṇye ṣaḍ-vidhā śaraṇāgatiḥ
“Accepting everything favourable, rejecting everything unfavourable, being confident that Kṛṣṇa will grant His protection, embracing Kṛṣṇa’s guardianship, fully offering one’s self to Kṛṣṇa, and feeling oneself to be lowly are the six aspects of śaraṇāgati.”
<span class="e2">prārthanā śune:</span> “Śrī Nanda Kumar hears their prayers.” This means Kṛṣṇa reciprocates with the surrendered souls in accordance with their prayers.
sakṛd eva prapanno yas tavāsmīti cha yāchate<br />abhayaṁ sarvadā tasmai dadāmy etad vrataṁ mama
(Rāmāyaṇa: Yuddha-kāṇḍa, 18.33)
[Rāmchandra proclaims:] “Anyone who even once sincerely surrenders unto Me, declaring, ‘I am Yours’, and prays for fearlessness—it is My vow that I will always grant that to them.”
রূপ-সনাতন-পদে দন্তে তৃণ করি’ ।<br />ভকতিবিনোদ পডড় দুহুঁ পদ ধরি’ ॥৬॥
rūpa-sanātana-pade dante tṛṇa kari’<br />bhakati-vinoda paḍe duhu̐ pada dhari’ <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">rūpa</span>–Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">sanātana</span>–Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Pra­bhu; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet of; <span class="e2">dante</span>–in the teeth; <span class="e2">tṛṇa</span>–piece of straw; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">paḍe</span>–falls; <span class="e2">duhu̐</span>–both; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">dhari’</span>–clasping. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> Bhakti Vinod places a straw between his teeth and falls before Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu and Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu, clasping their feet.
(<span class="e2">6</span><span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">śrī-rūpa-sanātana:</span> Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu and Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu are the two Āchāryas who teach śaraṇāgati.
কাঁদিয়া কাঁদিয়া বলে আমি ত’ অধম ।<br />শিখায়ে শরণাগতি করহে উত্তম ॥৭॥
kā̐diyā kā̐diyā bale āmi ta’ adhama<br />śikhāye śaraṇāgati karahe uttama <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–crying; <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–and crying; <span class="e2">bale</span>–says; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">adhama</span>–fallen, lowest; <span class="e2">śikhāye</span>–by teaching; <span class="e2">śaraṇāgati</span>–surrender; <span class="e2">karahe</span>–please make; <span class="e2">uttama</span>–elevated, beyond the darkness of illusion. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> Crying incessantly, he prays, “I am so lowly! Please elevate me by teaching me śaraṇāgati.”
(<span class="e2">7</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> uttama: </span>“Elevated.” This refers to one who is qualified for the topmost form of devotion, prema-bhakti. In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(11.11.32), Kṛṣṇa says:
ājñāyaivaṁ guṇān doṣān mayādiṣṭān api svakān<br />dharmān santyajya yaḥ sarvān māṁ bhajet sa cha sattamaḥ
“Realising the qualities and faults of the socio-religious system (varṇāśram-dharma) which I have instituted, one who completely abandons it and serves Me is the best of all sādhus.”

দৈন্যাত্মিকা
<span class="e2">Dainyātmikā:</span> <br />Humility
(২)
(2)
ভুলিয়া তোমারে<span class="e25">	সংসারে আসিয়া<br /></span><span class="e26">	পেয়ে নানা-বিধ ব্যথা ।<br /></span>তোমার চরণে<span class="e25">	আসিয়াছি আমি<br /></span><span class="e26">	বলিব দুঃখের কথা ॥১॥</span>
bhuliyā tomāre<span class="e10">	saṁsāre āsiyā<br /></span><span class="e11">	peye nānā-vidha vyathā<br /></span>tomāra charaṇe<span class="e10">	āsiyāchhi āmi<br /></span><span class="e11">	baliba duḥkhera kathā </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhuliyā</span>–forgetting; <span class="e2">tomāre</span>–about You; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the material world; <span class="e2">āsiyā</span>–coming; <span class="e2">peye</span>–experiencing; <span class="e2">nānā</span>–various; <span class="e2">vidha</span>–forms; <span class="e2">vyathā</span>–of suffering; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">āsiyāchhi</span>–have come; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">baliba</span>–will say; <span class="e2">duḥkhera</span>–of distress; <span class="e2">kathā</span>–tale. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> Forgetting You and coming to the material world, I have undergone all sorts of suffering. Now I have come before Your feet and will express my tale of distress.
(<span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> bhuliyā tomāre … nānā-vidha vyathā: “</span>Forgetting You … I have undergone all sorts of suffering.” Undergoing the miseries of material existence is the result of forgetfulness of the Lord. This is described in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> (Madhya-līlā, 20.117) and <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(11.2.37):
kṛṣṇa bhuli’ sei jīva anādi-bahirmukha<br />ataeva māyā tāre deya saṁsārādi-duḥkha
“When a soul outside the realm of time and space (in the taṭasthā-śakti*) turns away from Kṛṣṇa and forgets Him, Māyā subjects him to the various miseries of worldly existence.”
bhayaṁ dvitīyābhiniveśataḥ syād<br />īśād apetasya viparyayo ’smṛtiḥ<br />tan-māyayāto budha ābhajet taṁ<br />bhaktyaikayeṣaṁ guru-devatātmā
“By the influence of the Lord’s māyā, those who are intent upon selfish enjoyment and turn away from the Lord forget the Lord, consider themself to be the opposite of their true self, and become stricken with fear. Thus the wise should serve the Lord with unalloyed devotion, considering Śrī Guru to be non-different from the Lord and most beloved.”
<span class="e2">nānā-vidha vyathā: </span>“All sorts of suffering.” This refers to the threefold miseries (lit. burning heat) of material existence: ādhyātmik-tāp, miseries caused by one’s body and mind; ādhibhautik-tāp, miseries caused by other souls; and ādhidaivik-tāp, miseries caused by the demigods and demons.
The suffering mentioned in this verse also refers to a fivefold state of affliction (kleś): (1) avidyā: ignorance of one’s true identity as an eternal soul and servant of Kṛṣṇa; (2) asmitā: identification with the mundane ego, mind, and body; (3) abhiniveś: absorption in mundane experience; (4) rāga: obsession with mundane pleasures and their paraphernalia; and (5) dveṣ: revulsion to dissatisfaction and its causes.
জননী-জঠরে<span class="e25">	ছিলাম যখন<br /></span><span class="e26">	বিষম বন্ধন-পাশে ।<br /></span>একবার প্রভু!<span class="e25">	দেখা দিয়া মোরে<br /></span><span class="e26">	বঞ্চিলে এ দীন দাসে ॥২॥</span>
jananī-jaṭhare<span class="e10">	chhilāma yakhana<br /></span><span class="e11">	viṣama </span><span class="e11">bandhana-pāśe<br /></span>eka-bāra prabhu!<span class="e10">	dekhā diyā more<br /></span><span class="e11">	vañchile e dīna dāse </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jananī</span>–of my mother; <span class="e2">jaṭhare</span>–in the womb; <span class="e2">chhilāma</span>–I was; <span class="e2">yakhana</span>–when; <span class="e2">viṣama</span>–terrible; <span class="e2">bandhana</span>–binding; <span class="e2">pāśe</span>–with the ropes; <span class="e2">eka</span>–one; <span class="e2">bāra</span>–time; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">dekha</span>–sight; <span class="e2">diyā</span>–giving; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">vañchile</span>–deprived; <span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–poor; <span class="e2">dāse</span>–to this servant. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> While I was bound in the terrible confines of my mother’s womb, You once revealed Yourself to me, O Lord! Yet since then You have deprived this poor servant.
(<span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> jananī-jaṭhare … e dīna dāse: “</span>O Lord! … You have deprived this poor servant.” Only souls who, through divine fortune, ­directly meet the Lord while bound within the womb of their mother feel separation from Him (upon being born) and are able to say, “O Lord! You have deprived this poor servant.” This is not the case for all souls. Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu has established this conclusion in his <span class="e3">Sandarbhas</span>.
তখন ভাবিনু<span class="e25">	জনম পাইয়া<br /></span><span class="e26">	করিব ভজন তব ।<br /></span>জনম হইল<span class="e25">	পড়ি’ মায়া-জালে<br /></span><span class="e26">	না হইল জ্ঞান-লব ॥৩॥</span>
takhana bhāvinu<span class="e10">	janama pāiyā<br /></span><span class="e11">	kariba bhajana tava<br /></span>janama ha-ila<span class="e10">	paḍi’ māyā-jāle<br /></span><span class="e11">	nā ha-ila jñāna-lava </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">takhana</span>–then; <span class="e2">bhāvinu</span>–I thought; <span class="e2">janama</span>–birth; <span class="e2">pāiyā</span>–obtaining; <span class="e2">kariba</span>–I will do; <span class="e2">bhajana</span>–service; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">janama</span>–birth; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–happened; <span class="e2">paḍi’</span>–falling; <span class="e2">māyā (māyāra)</span>–of Māyā; <span class="e2">jāle (phā̐de)</span>–into the net (trap); <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">jñāna (jñānera)</span>–of knowledge; <span class="e2">lava (leśa)</span>–a fraction (trace). [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> At that moment I thought I would engage in Your service after taking birth. Yet when I was born, I fell into māyā’s trap, and not a trace of such consciousness remained.
(<span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">māyā-jāle:</span> “Māyā’s trap.” Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur has described the function of māyā as follows:
svarūpārthair hīnān nija-sukha-parān kṛṣṇa-vimukhān<br />harer māyā daṇḍyān guṇa-nigaḍa-jālaiḥ kalayati<br />tathā sthūlair liṅgair dvividha-varaṇaiḥ kleśa-nikarair<br />mahā-karmālānair nayati patitān svarga-nirayau
(Daśa-mūla-śikṣa: 6)
“With the shackles of the modes of material nature, Śrī Hari’s māyā binds those who have turned away from Him, become intent upon selfish happiness, and forgotten the actual interest of their true selves. Covering them with gross and subtle material bodies, and subjecting them to all sorts of suffering, māyā perpetually drags them by the heavy ropes of their karma throughout heavenly and hellish conditions.”
Also, in <span class="e3">Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu </span>(1.1.4) ‘Māyā’s trap’ is described as <span class="e3">paribhūtaṁ kāla-jāla-bhiyaḥ</span>, “The fearsome net of time (which is the cause of the continuous succession of miseries produced by the bondage of birth, death, and so forth).”
আদরের ছেলে<span class="e25">	স্বজনের কোলে<br /></span><span class="e26">	হাসিয়া কাটানু কাল ।<br /></span>জনক-জননী-<span class="e25">	স্নেহেতে ভুলিয়া<br /></span><span class="e26">	সংসার লাগিল ভাল ॥৪॥</span>
ādarera chhele<span class="e10">	svajanera kole<br /></span><span class="e11">	hāsiyā kāṭānu kāla<br /></span>janaka-jananī-<span class="e10">	snehete bhuliyā<br /></span><span class="e11">	saṁsāra lāgila bhāla </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ādarera</span>–of adoring parents; <span class="e2">chhele</span>–a son; <span class="e2">svajanera</span>–of relatives; <span class="e2">kole</span>–in the lap; <span class="e2">hāsiyā</span>–smiling, laughing; <span class="e2">kāṭānu</span>–I passed; <span class="e2">kāla</span>–time; <span class="e2">janaka</span>–of my father; <span class="e2">jananī</span>–of my mother; <span class="e2">snehete</span>–due to the affection; <span class="e2">bhuliyā</span>–forgetting; <span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–family life, the material world; <span class="e2">lāgila</span>–felt; <span class="e2">bhāla</span>–good. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> As a son of adoring parents, I spent my time in their laps, smiling and laughing. Because of my mother and father’s affection, I forgot You and took pleasure in family life (material existence).
ক্রমে দিন দিন<span class="e25">	বালক হইয়া<br /></span><span class="e26">	খেলিনু বালক সহ ।<br /></span>আর কিছুদিনে<span class="e25">	জ্ঞান উপজিল<br /></span><span class="e26">	পাঠ পড়ি অহরহঃ ॥৫॥</span>
krame dina dina<span class="e10">	bālaka ha-iyā<br /></span><span class="e11">	khelinu bālaka saha<br /></span>āra kichhu-dine<span class="e10">	jñāna upajila<br /></span><span class="e11">	pāṭha paḍi ahar-ahaḥ </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">krame</span>–gradually; <span class="e2">dina</span>–day; <span class="e2">dina</span>–day; <span class="e2">bālaka</span>–a boy; <span class="e2">ha-iyā</span>–becoming; <span class="e2">khelinu</span>–I played; <span class="e2">bālaka</span>–boys; <span class="e2">saha</span>–with; <span class="e2">āra</span>–more; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–some; <span class="e2">dine</span>–after days; <span class="e2">jñāna</span>–faculty of knowledge; <span class="e2">upajila (udita ha-ila)</span>–arose; <span class="e2">pāṭha</span>–lessons; <span class="e2">paḍi</span>–I study; <span class="e2">ahar-ahaḥ (dina dina, sarva-kṣaṇa)</span>–day after day (all the time). [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Day by day I grew into a young boy and played with other young boys. Later on my intellect developed, and I studied my lessons day in and day out.
বিদ্যার গৌরবে<span class="e25">	ভ্রমি’ দেশে দেশে<br /></span><span class="e26">	ধন উপার্জ্জন করি’ ।<br /></span>স্বজন-পালন<span class="e25">	করি এক-মনে<br /></span><span class="e26">	ভুলিনু তোমারে, হরি! ॥৬॥</span>
<span class="e2">vidyāra gaurave</span><span class="e10">	bhrami’ deśe deśe</span><span class="e2"><br /></span><span class="e11">	dhana upārjana kari’</span><span class="e2"><br />svajana-pālana</span><span class="e10">	kari eka-mane</span><span class="e2"><br /></span><span class="e11">	bhulinu tomāre hari! </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vidyāra</span>–of learning; <span class="e2">gaurave</span>–on the strength; <span class="e2">bhrami’</span>–travelling; <span class="e2">deśe</span>–in country; <span class="e2">deśe</span>–in (another) country; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–wealth; <span class="e2">upārjana</span>–earning; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">svajana</span>–relatives; <span class="e2">pālana</span>–maintenance; <span class="e2">kari</span>–I do; <span class="e2">eka</span>–single;<span class="e2"> mane</span>–with a mind; <span class="e2">bhulinu</span>–I forgot; <span class="e2">tomāre</span>–about You; <span class="e2">hari!</span>–O Lord! [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> Then on the strength of my learning, I travelled from place to place, earned money, and maintained my family with undivided attention. I forgot You, O Lord!
(<span class="e2">6</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> dhana upārjana o svajana-pālana:</span> “Earned money and maintained my family.” This is described by Śukadev Goswāmī to Mahārāj Parīkṣit in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (2.1.3):
nidrayā hriyate naktaṁ vyavāyena cha vā vayaḥ<br />divā chārthehayā rājan kuṭumba-bharaṇena vā
“O King, the lifetime of materialistic householders is wasted by night in sleeping or engaging in sexual indulgence, and by day in earning money and maintaining family members.”
বার্দ্ধক্যে এখন<span class="e25">	ভকতিবিনোদ<br /></span><span class="e26">	কাঁদিয়া কাতর অতি ।<br /></span>না ভজিয়া তোরে<span class="e25">	দিন বৃথা গেল<br /></span><span class="e26">	এখন কি হ’বে গতি ॥৭॥</span>
vārddhakye ekhana<span class="e10">	bhakati-vinoda<br /></span><span class="e11">	kā̐diyā kātara ati<br /></span>nā bhajiyā tore<span class="e10">	dina vṛthā gela<br /></span><span class="e11">	ekhana ki ha’be gati? </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vārddhakye</span>–in old age; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–crying; <span class="e2">kātara</span>–distressed; <span class="e2">ati</span>–very; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">bhajiyā</span>–serving; <span class="e2">tore</span>–to You; <span class="e2">dina</span>–days; <span class="e2">vṛthā</span>–vain; <span class="e2">gela</span>–passed; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what?; <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">gati</span>–destination. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7) Now aged, Bhakti Vinod cries in great distress, “Not serving You, I have passed my days in vain. What will be my fate now?”
