(3)
বিদ্যার বিলাসে<span class="e25">	কাটাইনু কাল<br /></span><span class="e26">	পরম সাহসে আমি ।<br /></span>তোমার চরণ<span class="e25">	না ভজিনু কভু<br /></span><span class="e26">	এখন শরণ তুমি ॥১॥</span>
vidyāra vilāse<span class="e10">	kāṭāinu kāla<br /></span><span class="e11">	parama sāhase āmi<br /></span>tomāra charaṇa<span class="e10">	nā bhajinu kabhu<br /></span><span class="e11">	ekhana śaraṇa tumi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vidyāra</span>–of learning; <span class="e2">vilāse</span>–in the pleasures; <span class="e2">kāṭāinu</span>–I passed; <span class="e2">kāla</span>–the time; <span class="e2">parama</span>–great; <span class="e2">sāhase</span>–with confidence; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">bhajinu</span>–I served; <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–ever; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">śaraṇa</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I spent my time absorbed in the pleasures of learning with great confidence. I never served Your feet. Now You are my shelter.
পড়িতে পড়িতে<span class="e25">	ভরসা বাড়িল<br /></span><span class="e26">	জ্ঞানে গতি হবে মানি’ ।<br /></span>সে আশা বিফল<span class="e25">	সে জ্ঞান দুর্ব্বল<br /></span><span class="e26">	সে জ্ঞান অজ্ঞান জানি ॥২॥</span>
paḍite paḍite<span class="e10">	bharasā bāḍila<br /></span><span class="e11">	jñāne gati habe māni’<br /></span>se āśā biphala<span class="e10">	se jñāna durbala<br /></span><span class="e11">	se jñāna ajñāna jāni </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">paḍite</span>–studying; <span class="e2">paḍite</span>–and studying; <span class="e2">bharasā</span>–confidence; <span class="e2">bāḍila</span>–increased; <span class="e2">jñāne</span>–through knowledge; <span class="e2">gati</span>–goal; <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be attained; <span class="e2">māni’</span>–considering; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">āśā</span>–hope; <span class="e2">biphala</span>–fruitless; <span class="e2">se</span>–that;<span class="e2"> jñāna</span>–know­ledge; <span class="e2">durbala</span>–powerless; <span class="e2">se</span>–that;<span class="e2"> jñāna</span>–knowledge; <span class="e2">ajñāna</span>–ignorance; <span class="e2">jāni</span>–I know. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> Studying continuously, my confidence that I would attain the fulfilment of life through knowledge increased. Yet that hope was futile, and that knowledge was useless. I now know such ‘knowledge’ to be ignorance.
(<span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> jñāne gati:</span> “I would attain the fulfilment of life through knowledge.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(4.33), Kṛṣṇa says:
sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate
“O Arjun, all actions culminate in knowledge.”
<span class="e2">se jñāna durbala: </span>“That knowledge was useless.” Knowledge alone is unable to fulfil one’s spiritual desires. This is explained by Śrīman Mahāprabhu to Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta </span>(Madhya-līlā, 22.17–18):
kṛṣṇa-bhakti haya abhidheya-pradhāna<br />bhakti-mukha-nirīkṣaka karma-yoga-jñāna<br />ei saba sādhanera ati tuchchha bala<br />kṛṣṇa-bhakti vinā tāhā dite nāre phala
“Kṛṣṇa-bhakti is the fundamental means of spiritual progress (because the soul is by nature an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa). Karma (pious action), yoga (self-regulation), and jñān (knowledge) are all dependent on bhakti; they have no actual power of their own. Without Kṛṣṇa-bhakti, they are all unable to deliver results.”
<span class="e2">se jñāna ajñāna: </span>“That ‘knowledge’ is ignorance.” All knowledge of the mundane world is really illusory knowledge, in other words, ignorance. This is described in the <span class="e3">Kaṭha-upaniṣad </span>(1.2.5):
avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ<br />svayaṁ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṁ manyamānāḥ<br />daṁdramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā<br />andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ
“Insincere fools who remain in ignorance yet consider themselves sober (free from any illusion) and wise (learned authorities) are deluded just like blind persons being led by other blind persons.”
জড়বিদ্যা যত<span class="e25">	মায়ার বৈভব<br /></span><span class="e26">	তোমার ভজনে বাধা ।<br /></span>মোহ জনমিয়া<span class="e25">	অনিত্য সংসারে<br /></span><span class="e26">	জীবকে করয়ে গাধা ॥৩॥</span>
jaḍa-vidyā yata<span class="e10">	māyāra vaibhava<br /></span><span class="e11">	tomāra bhajane bādhā<br /></span>moha janamiyā<span class="e10">	anitya saṁsāre<br /></span><span class="e11">	jīvake karaye gādhā </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jaḍa</span>–material; <span class="e2">vidyā</span>–learning; <span class="e2">yata</span>–all; <span class="e2">māyāra</span>–of the illusory energy; <span class="e2">vai­bhava</span>–the opulence; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> bhajane</span>–in the service; <span class="e2">bādhā</span>–an obstacle; <span class="e2">moha</span>–infatuation; <span class="e2">janamiyā</span>–bringing about; <span class="e2">anitya</span>–non-eternal; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the material world; <span class="e2">jīvake</span>–to the soul; <span class="e2">karaye</span>–makes; <span class="e2">gādhā</span>–an ass. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> All mundane learning is an exhibition of māyā and an obstacle to Your service. It brings about infatuation for the temporary world and makes an ass of the soul.
(<span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> jaḍa-vidyā … jīvake karaye gādhā: </span>“Mundane learning makes an ass of the soul.” This refers to aparā-vidyā, inferior knowledge, that is, knowledge which construes material objects as meant for one’s selfish enjoyment.
In this regard, shortly after returning from Gayā, Nimāi Paṇḍit advised His students as follows (<span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-bhāgavat</span>: Madhya-līlā, 1.158–9):
śāstrera nā jāne marma, adhyāpanā kare<br />garddabhera prāya yena śāstra bahi’ mare<br />paḍiñā śuniñā loka gela chhāre-khāre<br />kṛṣṇa mahā-mahotsave vañchilā tāhāre
“Those who do not know the purport of the scriptures yet teach them to others are like asses: they bear the load of the scriptures in vain. Reading and hearing the scriptures leads only to death and destruction for both these teachers and their audiences. They are all deprived of the joy of the grand festival of love for Kṛṣṇa.”
In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(10.84.13), Kṛṣṇa Himself explains:
yasyātma-buddhiḥ kuṇape tri-dhātuke<br />sva-dhīḥ kalatrādiṣu bhauma ijya-dhīḥ<br />yat-tīrtha-buddhiḥ salile na karhichij<br />janeṣv abhijñeṣu sa eva go-kharaḥ
“One who considers his decaying material body, made of mucus, bile, and air, to be his actual self (but does not realise himself to be a servant of the Lord); who considers his spouse, family, and associated paraphernalia to be his possessions (but feels no affectionate attachment for the Lord’s devotees); who considers a graven image made of earth or other material elements to be the Lord (but has no reverence for the Lord’s devotees); and who considers a body of water to be a place of pilgrimage (but fails to understand that the Lord’s devotees are the ultimate place of pilgrimage)—such a person is an ass among cows (a foolish beast fit only to bear the burden of carrying food for other animals).”
Kṛṣṇa explains the components of His inferior energy (aparā-prakṛti) in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(7.4–5):
bhūmir āpo ’nalo vāyuḥ khaṁ mano buddhir eva cha<br />ahaṅkāra itīyaṁ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā | apareyam
“Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intelligence, and false ego are the eight divisions of My inferior, material energy.”
সেই গাধা হ’য়ে<span class="e25">	সংসারের বোঝা<br /></span><span class="e26">	বহিনু অনেক কাল ।<br /></span>বার্দ্ধক্যে এখন<span class="e25">	শক্তির অভাবে<br /></span><span class="e26">	কিছু নাহি লাগে ভাল ॥৪॥</span>
sei gādhā ha’ye<span class="e10">	saṁsārera bojhā<br /></span><span class="e11">	bahinu aneka kāla<br /></span>vārddhakye ekhana<span class="e10">	śaktira abhāve<br /></span><span class="e11">	kichhu nāhi lāge bhāla </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sei</span>–that very; <span class="e2">gādhā</span>–ass; <span class="e2">ha’ye</span>–becoming; <span class="e2">saṁsārera</span>–of material existence, of family life; <span class="e2">bojhā</span>–the burden; <span class="e2">bahinu</span>–I carried; <span class="e2">aneka</span>–much; <span class="e2">kāla</span>–time; <span class="e2">vārddhakye</span>–in old age; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">śaktira</span>–of ability; <span class="e2">abhāve</span>–in the absence; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–something; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">lāge</span>–strikes; <span class="e2">bhāla</span>–good. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> I became such an ass and bore the burden of my household for so long. Now aged and devoid of strength, nothing brings me any pleasure.
জীবন যাতনা<span class="e25">	হইল এখন<br /></span><span class="e26">	সে বিদ্যা অবিদ্যা ভেল ।<br /></span>অবিদ্যার জ্বালা<span class="e25">	ঘটিল বিষম<br /></span><span class="e26">	সে বিদ্যা হইল শেল ॥৫॥</span>
jīvana yātanā<span class="e10">	ha-ila ekhana<br /></span><span class="e11">	se vidyā avidyā bhela<br /></span>avidyāra jvālā<span class="e10">	ghaṭila viṣama<br /></span><span class="e11">	se vidyā ha-ila śela </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jīvana</span>–life; <span class="e2">yātanā</span>–agony; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">vidyā</span>–learning; <span class="e2">avidyā</span>–ignorance; <span class="e2">bhela</span>–became; <span class="e2">avidyāra</span>–of ignorance; <span class="e2">jvālā</span>–the burning pain; <span class="e2">ghaṭila</span>–became; <span class="e2">viṣama</span>–torturous; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">vidyā</span>–learning; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">śela (marma-bhedī astra viśeṣa)</span>–a heart-piercing spear. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Now My life has become agony. My learning has proven to be ignorance, and the burning pain of that ignorance has become unbearably torturous. My ‘learning’ has turned into a spear (that has pierced my heart).
তোমার চরণ<span class="e25">	বিনা কিছু ধন<br /></span><span class="e26">	সংসারে না আছে আর ।<br /></span>ভকতিবিনোদ<span class="e25">	জড়বিদ্যা ছাড়ি’<br /></span><span class="e26">	তুয়া পদ করে সার ॥৬॥</span>
tomāra charaṇa<span class="e10">	vinā kichhu dhana<br /></span><span class="e11">	saṁsāre nā āchhe āra<br /></span>bhakati-vinoda<span class="e10">	jaḍa-vidyā chhāḍi’<br /></span><span class="e11">	tuyā pada kare sāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">vinā</span>–apart from; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–any; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–treasure; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the material world; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">āchhe</span>–is; <span class="e2">āra</span>–other; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">jaḍa</span>–material; <span class="e2">vidyā</span>–learning; <span class="e2">chhāḍi’</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">kare</span>–makes; <span class="e2">sāra</span>–the essence. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! There is nothing of value in this material world other than Your feet. Bhakti Vinod abandons all mundane learning and accepts Your feet as his be-all and end-all.
(৪)
(4)
যৌবনে যখন,<span class="e25">	ধন উপার্জ্জনে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হইনু বিপুল কামী ।<br /></span>ধরম স্মরিয়া,<span class="e25">	গৃহিণীর কর,<br /></span><span class="e26">	ধরিনু তখন আমি ॥১॥</span>
yauvane yakhana,<span class="e10">	dhana-upārjane,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ha-inu vipula kāmī<br /></span>dharama smariyā,<span class="e10">	gṛhiṇīra kara,<br /></span><span class="e11">	dharinu takhana āmi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">yauvane</span>–in youth; <span class="e2">yakhana</span>–when; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–wealth; <span class="e2">upārjane</span>–in earning; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>–I became; <span class="e2">vipula</span>–greatly; <span class="e2">kāmī</span>–desirous; <span class="e2">dharama</span>–religion; <span class="e2">smariyā</span>–remembering; <span class="e2">gṛhiṇīra</span>–of a wife; <span class="e2">kara</span>–the hand; <span class="e2">dharinu</span>–took; <span class="e2">takhana</span>–then; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1) When I was young I became greatly desirous of earning money. Remembering my religious duty, I took the hand of a wife.
(<span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> dharama smariyā: </span>“Remembering my religious duty.” This refers to the injunction: <span class="e3">sa-strīko dharmam ācharet</span>, one should practise religion with a wife.
সংসারে পাতা’য়ে,<span class="e25">	তাহার সহিত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কালক্ষয় কৈনু কত ।<br /></span>বহু সুত-সুতা,<span class="e25">	জনম লভিল,<br /></span><span class="e26">	মরমে হইনু হত ॥২॥</span>
saṁsāre pātā’ye,<span class="e10">	tāhāra sahita,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kāla-kṣaya kainu kata<br /></span>bahu suta-sutā,<span class="e10">	janama labhila,<br /></span><span class="e11">	marame ha-inu hata </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–to household life, material existence; <span class="e2">pātā’ye</span>–setting out; <span class="e2">tāhāra</span>–her; <span class="e2">sahita</span>–with; <span class="e2">kāla</span>–of time; <span class="e2">kṣaya</span>–destruction; <span class="e2">kainu</span>–did; <span class="e2">kata</span>–so much; <span class="e2">bahu</span>–many; <span class="e2">suta</span>–sons; <span class="e2">sutā</span>–and daughters; <span class="e2">janama</span>–birth; <span class="e2">labhila</span>–attained; <span class="e2">marame</span>–in my core; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>–I became; <span class="e2">hata</span>–distressed. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> </span>I established a household with her and wasted so much time. We had many sons and daughters, and I became distres­sed at heart.
সংসারের ভার,<span class="e25">	বাড়ে দিনে দিনে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অচল হইল গতি ।<br /></span>বার্দ্ধক্য আসিয়া,<span class="e25">	ঘেরিল আমারে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অস্থির হইল মতি ॥৩॥</span>
saṁsārera bhāra,<span class="e10">	bāḍe dine dine,<br /></span><span class="e11">	achala ha-ila gati<br /></span>vārddhakya āsiyā,<span class="e10">	gherila āmāre,<br /></span><span class="e11">	asthira ha-ila mati </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">saṁsārera</span>–of household life; <span class="e2">bhāra</span>–the burden; <span class="e2">bāḍe</span>–increasing; <span class="e2">dine</span>–day; <span class="e2">dine</span>–by day; <span class="e2">achala</span>–immobile; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">gati</span>–my path, destination; <span class="e2">vārddhakya</span>–old age; <span class="e2">āsiyā</span>–coming; <span class="e2">gherila</span>–besieged; <span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">asthira</span>–unsteady, restless; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">mati</span>–mind. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3)<span class="e2"> </span>The burden of my household increased day by day, and my progress towards attaining the goal of life came to a standstill. As old age came and besieged me, my mind became disturbed.
(<span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> achala ha-ila gati: </span>“My progress towards attaining the goal of life came to a standstill.” This is explained by Śrī Prabuddha to Mahārāj Nimi in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (11.3.18):
karmāṇy ārabhamāṇānāṁ duḥkha-hatyai sukhāya cha<br />paśyet pāka-viparyāsaṁ mithunī-chāriṇāṁ nṛṇām
“One must see that those humans who unite in conjugal relationships and make endeavours to eliminate their distress and attain happiness (through sexual relations, producing offspring, accumulating wealth, maintaining a household, and so forth) incur the exact opposite result.”
<span class="e2">vārddhakya āsiyā … asthira ha-ila mati:</span> “As old age came … my mind became disturbed.” Seeing everyone suffering in illusion as he wandered throughout ancient India, Śaṅkar Āchārya would lament:
bālas tāvat krīḍāsaktaḥ taruṇas tāvat taruṇī-raktaḥ<br />vṛddhas tāvat chintā-magnāḥ pare brahmaṇi ko ’pi na lagnaḥ
(Moha-mudgara-stotram: 7)
“Boys are attached to play. Youths are attached to young women. The elderly are absorbed in worries. Alas! No one is conscious of the Supreme Absolute (Parabrahma).”
পীড়ায় অস্থির,<span class="e25">	চিন্তায় জ্বরিত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অভাবে জ্বলিত চিত ।<br /></span>উপায় না দেখি,<span class="e25">	অন্ধকার-ময়,<br /></span><span class="e26">	এখন হয়েছি ভীত ॥৪॥</span>
pīḍāya asthira,<span class="e10">	chintāya jvarita,<br /></span><span class="e11">	abhāve jvalita chita<br /></span>upāya nā dekhi,<span class="e10">	andhakāra-maya,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ekhana hayechhi bhīta </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">pīḍāya</span>–with disease; <span class="e2">asthira</span>–unsteady; <span class="e2">chintāya</span>–with anxiety; <span class="e2">jvarita</span>–feverish; <span class="e2">abhāve</span>–in want, in privation;<span class="e2"> jvalita</span>–burning; <span class="e2">chita</span>–heart; <span class="e2">upāya</span>–way out; <span class="e2">na</span>–not; <span class="e2">dekhi</span>–I see; <span class="e2">andhakāra</span>–blinding darkness; <span class="e2">maya</span>–filled with; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">hayechhi</span>–I have become; <span class="e2">bhīta</span>–frightened. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Restless with disease and feverish with anxiety, my heart burns with unfulfilled desire. I see no way out of this darkness and have now become fearful.
সংসার-তটিনী-<span class="e25">	স্রোত নহে শেষ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	মরণ নিকটে ঘোর ।<br /></span>সব সমাপিয়া,<span class="e25">	ভজিব তোমায়,<br /></span><span class="e26">	এ আশা বিফল মোর ॥৫॥</span>
saṁsāra-taṭinī-<span class="e10">	srota nahe śeṣa,<br /></span><span class="e11">	maraṇa nikaṭe ghora<br /></span>saba samāpiyā,<span class="e10">	bhajiba tomāya,<br /></span><span class="e11">	e āśā biphala mora </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–of household life, of material existence; <span class="e2">taṭinī (nadī)</span>–the river; <span class="e2">srota</span>–the current; <span class="e2">nahe</span>–does not; <span class="e2">śeṣa</span>–end; <span class="e2">maraṇa</span>–death; <span class="e2">nikaṭe</span>–near; <span class="e2">ghora</span>–terrible; <span class="e2">saba</span>–everything; <span class="e2">samāpiyā</span>–concluding; <span class="e2">bhajiba</span>–will serve; <span class="e2">tomāya</span>–You; <span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">āśā</span>–hope; <span class="e2">biphala</span>–fruitless; <span class="e2">mora</span>–of mine. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> There is no end to the torrent of the river of household life, and fearsome death always looms nearby. “After finishing all of this, I will serve You”—this hope of mine has proven vain.
এবে শুন প্রভু!<span class="e25">	আমি গতিহীন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	ভকতিবিনোদ কয় ।<br /></span>তব কৃপা বিনা,<span class="e25">	সকলি নিরাশা,<br /></span><span class="e26">	দেহ’ মোরে পদাশ্রয় ॥৬॥</span>
ebe śuna prabhu!<span class="e10">	āmi gati-hīna,<br /></span><span class="e11">	bhakati-vinoda kaya<br /></span>tava kṛpā vinā,<span class="e10">	sakali nirāśā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	deha’ more padāśraya </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ebe</span>–now; <span class="e2">śuna</span>–please listen; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">gati</span>–means of deliverance; <span class="e2">hīna</span>–devoid of; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kaya</span>–says; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">vinā</span>–without; <span class="e2">sakali</span>–everything; <span class="e2">nirāśā</span>–hopeless; <span class="e2">deha’</span>–please bestow; <span class="e2">more</span>–upon me; <span class="e2">pada</span>–of Your feet; <span class="e2">āśraya</span>–the shelter. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> Now please listen, O Lord! I am utterly helpless. Bhakti Vinod prays, “Without Your mercy, everything is hopeless. Please give me the shelter of Your feet.”
(৫)
(5)
আমার জীবন,<span class="e25">	সদা পাপে রত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নাহিক পুণ্যের লেশ ।<br /></span>পরেরে উদ্বেগ,<span class="e25">	দিয়ছি যে কত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	দিয়াছি জীবেরে ক্লেশ ॥১॥</span>
āmāra jīvana,<span class="e10">	sadā pāpe rata,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nāhika puṇyera leśa<br /></span>parere udvega,<span class="e10">	diyāchhi ye kata,<br /></span><span class="e11">	diyāchhi jīvere kleśa</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">jīvana</span>–life; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">pāpe</span>–in sin; <span class="e2">rata</span>–engaged<span class="e2">;</span> <span class="e2">nāhika</span>–there is not; <span class="e2">puṇyera</span>–of piety; <span class="e2">leśa</span>–a trace; <span class="e2">parere</span>–to others; <span class="e2">udvega</span>–agitation; <span class="e2">diyāchhi</span>–I have given; <span class="e2">ye</span>–which; <span class="e2">kata</span>–so much; <span class="e2">diyāchhi</span>–I have given; <span class="e2">jīvere</span>–to other souls; <span class="e2">kleśa</span>–afflictions. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> My life is always engrossed in sin; there is not a trace of piety within it. I have caused others so much anxiety and trouble.
(<span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> sadā pāpe rata: </span>“Always engrossed in sin.” As Śaṅkar Āchārya expresses in his <span class="e3">Mohā-mudgara-stotram</span>:
pāpo ’haṁ pāpa-karmāhaṁ pāpātmā pāpa-sambhavaḥ
“I am sinful, my actions are sinful, my soul is sinful, and my birth is sinful.”
নিজ সুখ লাগি’,<span class="e25">	পাপে নাহি ডরি,<br /></span><span class="e26">	দয়াহীন স্বার্থপর ।<br /></span>পর-সুখে দুঃখী,<span class="e25">	সদা মিথ্যাভাষী,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পরদুঃখ সুখকর ॥২॥</span>
nija sukha lāgi’,<span class="e10">	pāpe nāhi ḍari,<br /></span><span class="e11">	dayā-hīna svārtha-para<br /></span>para-sukhe duḥkhī,<span class="e10">	sadā mithyā-bhāṣī,<br /></span><span class="e11">	para-duḥkha sukha-kara</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nija</span>–my own; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">lāgi’</span>–for the sake; <span class="e2">pāpe</span>–in sin; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–do not; <span class="e2">ḍari</span>–I fear; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">hīna</span>–devoid of; <span class="e2">svārtha</span>–self-interest; <span class="e2">para</span>–intent upon; <span class="e2">para</span>–of others; <span class="e2">sukhe</span>–by the happiness; <span class="e2">duḥkhī</span>–distressed; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">mithyā</span>–lies; <span class="e2">bhāṣī</span>–speaking; <span class="e2">para</span>–of others; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">kara</span>–producing. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> I am never afraid to engage in sinful activities for the sake of my own happiness. I am merciless and selfish. I am distressed by the happiness of others, I am a perpetual liar, and the distress of others pleases me.
অশেষ কামনা,<span class="e25">	হৃদি মাঝে মোর,<br /></span><span class="e26">	ক্রোধী, দম্ভপরায়ণ ।<br /></span>মদমত্ত সদা,<span class="e25">	বিষয়ে মোহিত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হিংসা-গর্ব্ব বিভূষণ ॥৩॥</span>
aśeṣa kāmanā,<span class="e10">	hṛdi mājhe mora,<br /></span><span class="e11">	krodhī, dambha-parāyaṇa<br /></span>mada-matta sadā,<span class="e10">	viṣaye mohita,<br /></span><span class="e11">	hiṁsā-garva vibhūṣaṇa</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">aśeṣa</span>–unlimited; <span class="e2">kāmanā</span>–sinful desires; <span class="e2">hṛdi</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">mājhe</span>–in the interior; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">krodhī</span>–angry; <span class="e2">dambha</span>–arrogance; <span class="e2">parāyaṇa</span>–filled with; <span class="e2">mada</span>–vanity; <span class="e2">matta</span>–intoxicated; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">viṣaye</span>–by mundanity; <span class="e2">mohita</span>–infatuated; <span class="e2">hiṁsā</span>–malice, jealousy, violence; <span class="e2">garva</span>–pride, egotism; <span class="e2">vibhūṣaṇa</span>–ornaments. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> There are unlimited sinful desires within the core of my heart. I am angry and arrogant, always maddened with vanity, infatuated with mundanity, and ornamented with malice and pride.
(<span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> dambha-parāyaṇa: “</span>Arrogant.” This refers to a dharma-dhvajī, a hypocrite who makes a show of being religious for mundane purposes (lit. one who waves the flag of dharma but does not practise it).
নিদ্রালস্য-হত,<span class="e25">	সুকার্য্যে বিরত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অকার্য্যে উদ্যোগী আমি ।<br /></span>প্রতিষ্ঠা লাগিয়া,<span class="e25">	শাঠ্য-আচরণ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	লোভ-হত সদা কামী ॥৪॥</span>
nidrālasya-hata,<span class="e10">	sukārye virata,<br /></span><span class="e11">	akārye udyogī āmi<br /></span>pratiṣṭhā lāgiyā,<span class="e10">	śāṭhya-ācharaṇa,<br /></span><span class="e11">	lobha-hata sadā kāmī</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nidrā</span>–by sleep; <span class="e2">alasya</span>–laziness; <span class="e2">hata</span>–subdued; <span class="e2">sukārye</span>–to good deeds; <span class="e2">virata</span>–averse; <span class="e2">akārye</span>–for sinful deeds; <span class="e2">udyogī</span>–eager; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">pratiṣṭhā (sammāna)</span>–fame (exaltation); <span class="e2">lāgiyā</span>–for; <span class="e2">śāṭhya (vañchanā)</span>–deceitful; <span class="e2">ācharaṇa</span>–behaviour; <span class="e2">lobha</span>–by greed; <span class="e2">hata</span>–attacked, destroyed, conquered; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">kāmī</span>–covetous. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> I am subdued by laziness and sleep, averse to performing good deeds, and eager to perform sinful deeds. I engage in deceitful behaviour in pursuit of prestige. I am ruined by greed and constantly covetous.
এ হেন দুর্জ্জন,<span class="e25">	সজ্জন-বর্জ্জিত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অপরাধী নিরন্তর ।<br /></span>শুভকার্য্যশূন্য,<span class="e25">	সদানর্থমনা,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নানা দুঃখে জর জর ॥৫॥</span>
e hena durjana,<span class="e10">	sajjana-varjita,<br /></span><span class="e11">	aparādhī nirantara<br /></span>śubha-kārya-śūnya,<span class="e10">	sadānartha-manā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nānā duḥkhe jara jara</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">hena</span>–such as; <span class="e2">durjana</span>–bad person; <span class="e2">sajjana</span>–by devotees; <span class="e2">varjita</span>–rejected; <span class="e2">aparādhī</span>–an offender; <span class="e2">nirantara</span>–incessantly; <span class="e2">śubha</span>–good; <span class="e2">kārya</span>–motive; <span class="e2">śūnya</span>–devoid of; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">anartha</span>–evil; <span class="e2">manā</span>–minded; <span class="e2">nānā</span>–various; <span class="e2">duḥkhe</span>–by miseries; <span class="e2">jara</span>–worn; <span class="e2">jara</span>–and torn. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Such a sinner as I is shunned by devotees, and is a constant offender. I am devoid of virtuous motives, always intent upon evil, and racked by various miseries.
(5<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">sadānartha-manā:</span> “Always intent upon evil.” This means incessantly malevolent.
বার্দ্ধক্যে এখন,<span class="e25">	উপায়-বিহীন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তা’তে দীন অকিঞ্চন ।<br /></span>ভকতিবিনোদ,<span class="e25">	প্রভুর চরণে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	করে দুঃখ নিবেদন ॥৬॥</span>
vārddhakye ekhana,<span class="e10">	upāya-vihīna,<br /></span><span class="e11">	tā’te dīna akiñchana<br /></span>bhakati-vinoda,<span class="e10">	prabhura charaṇe,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kare duḥkha nivedana</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vārddhakye</span>–in old age; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">upāya</span>–means; <span class="e2">vihīna</span>–devoid (of any other); <span class="e2">tā’te</span>–thereby; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–distressed; <span class="e2">akiñchana (saṅgati-śūnya)</span>–poor (without means); <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">prabhura</span>–of the Lord; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">kare</span>–makes; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–sorrow; <span class="e2">nivedana</span>–submission. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> Now aged, I am devoid of any means of deliverance, and thus destitute and distressed. Bhakti Vinod submits this remorseful confession at the feet of the Lord.

আত্মনিবেদনাত্মিকা
<span class="e2">Ātma-Nivedanātmikā:</span> <br />Self-Submission
(৬)
(6)
<span class="e23">	(প্রভু হে!) শুন মোর দুঃখের কাহিনী ।</span><br />বিষয়-হলাহল,<span class="e22">	সুধাভাণে পিয়লুঁ, <br /></span><span class="e23">	আব অবসান দিনমণি ॥১॥</span>
<span class="e11">	(prabhu he!) śuna mora duḥkhera kāhinī<br /></span>viṣaya halāhala,<span class="e10">	sudhā-bhāṇe piyalu̐,<br /></span><span class="e11">	āba avasāna dinamaṇi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">prabhu</span>–Lord; <span class="e2">he!</span>–oh!; <span class="e2">śuna</span>–please listen; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">duḥkhera</span>–of distress; <span class="e2">kāhinī</span>–tale; <span class="e2">viṣaya</span>–of mundanity; <span class="e2">halāhala (garala, viṣa)</span>–mortal poison (poisonous venom); <span class="e2">sudhā</span>–nectar; <span class="e2">bhāṇe (bhrame)</span>–as though enacting a drama<span class="e2"> (</span>by mistake); <span class="e2">piyalu̐ (pān karilāma)</span>–I drank; <span class="e2">āba (ekhana)</span>–now; <span class="e2">avasāna</span>–the disappearance; <span class="e2">dinamaṇi (sūrya)</span>–jewel of the day (sun). [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Please listen to my tale of distress. Mistaking it for nectar, I drank the terrible poison of mundanity, and now the sun is setting (my life is coming to an end).
খেলারসে শৈশব,<span class="e22">	পড়ইতে কৈশোর <br /></span><span class="e23">	গোঁয়াওলুঁ না ভেল বিবেক ।<br /></span>ভোগবশে যৌবনে,<span class="e22">	ঘর পাতি বসিলুঁ <br /></span><span class="e23">	সুত-মিত বাড়ল অনেক ॥২॥</span>
khelā-rase śaiśava,<span class="e10">	paḍaite kaiśora <br /></span><span class="e11">	go̐yāolu̐ nā bhela viveka<br /></span>bhoga-vaśe yauvane,<span class="e10">	ghara pāti vasilu̐ <br /></span><span class="e11">	suta-mita bāḍala aneka </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">khelā</span>–of play; <span class="e2">rase</span>–in the pleasure; <span class="e2">śaiśava</span>–childhood; <span class="e2">paḍaite (pāṭha karite)</span>–in studying; <span class="e2">kaiśora</span>–adolescence; <span class="e2">go̐yāolu̐ (ativāhita karilāma)</span>–I spent; <span class="e2">nā</span>–did not; <span class="e2">bhela (ha-ila)</span>–became; <span class="e2">viveka</span>–conscience; <span class="e2">bhoga</span>–of enjoyment; <span class="e2">vaśe</span>–under the control; <span class="e2">yauvane</span>–in my youth; <span class="e2">ghara</span>–a home; <span class="e2">pāti</span>–arrange; <span class="e2">vasilu̐</span>–I sat; <span class="e2">suta</span>–children; <span class="e2">mita (mitra)</span>–friends; <span class="e2">bāḍala (vṛddhi prāpta ha-ila)</span>–increased; <span class="e2">aneka</span>–many. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> I spent my childhood immersed in the pleasures of play and my adolescence in study. My conscience never developed. Captivated by worldly enjoyment in my youth, I established myself within household life, and my children and friends multiplied.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> khelā-rase śaiśava:</span> “I spent my childhood immersed in the pleasures of play.” Śaṅkar Āchārya describes the deluded masses in this way:
bālas tāvat krīḍāsaktaḥ taruṇas tāvat taruṇī-raktaḥ
vṛddhas tāvat chintā-magnāḥ pare brahmaṇi ko ’pi na lagnaḥ
(Moha-mudgara-stotram: 7)
“Boys are attached to play. Youths are attached to young women. The elderly are absorbed in worries. Alas! No one is conscious of the Supreme Absolute (Parabrahma).”
বৃদ্ধকাল আওল,<span class="e22">	সব সুখ ভাগল,<br /></span><span class="e23">	পীড়াবশে হইনু কাতর ।<br /></span>সর্ব্বেন্দ্রিয় দুর্ব্বল<span class="e22">	ক্ষীণ কলেবর,<br /></span><span class="e23">	ভোগাভাবে দুঃখিত অন্তর ॥৩॥</span>
vṛddha-kāla āola,<span class="e10">	saba sukha bhāgala,<br /></span><span class="e11">	pīḍā-vaśe ha-inu kātara<br /></span>sarvendriya durbala<span class="e10">	kṣīṇa kalevara,<br /></span><span class="e11">	bhogābhāve duḥkhita antara </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vṛddha</span>–old; <span class="e2">kāla</span>–age; <span class="e2">āola (āsila)</span>–came; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">bhāgala (palāyana karila)</span>–fled; <span class="e2">pīḍā</span>–of disease <span class="e2">vaśe</span>–under the control of; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>– I became; <span class="e2">kātara</span>–distressed; <span class="e2">sarvendriya</span>–all of my senses; <span class="e2">durbala</span>–incapacitated; <span class="e2">kṣīṇa</span>–emaciated;<span class="e2"> kalevara</span>–body; <span class="e2">bhoga</span>–enjoyment; <span class="e2">abhāve</span>–for want of; <span class="e2">duḥkhita</span>–sorrowful; <span class="e2">antara</span>–interior. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Then old age came, and all happiness fled. Subjugated by disease, I became distressed. All of my senses became incapacitated, and my body became emaciated. For want of enjoyment, my heart became sorrowful.
জ্ঞান-লব-হীন,<span class="e22">	ভক্তিরসে বঞ্চিত,</span><br /><span class="e23">	আর মোর কি হবে উপায় ।</span><br />পতিত-বন্ধু তুহুঁ,<span class="e22">	পতিতাধম হাম,</span><br /><span class="e23">	কৃপায় উঠাও তব পায় ॥৪॥</span>
jñāna-lava-hīna,<span class="e10">	bhakti-rase vañchita,<br /></span><span class="e11">	āra mora ki habe upāya<br /></span>patita-bandhu tuhu̐,<span class="e10">	patitādhama hāma,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kṛpāya uṭhāo tava pāya </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jñāna</span>–of knowledge; <span class="e2">lava</span>–a trace; <span class="e2">hīna</span>–devoid of; <span class="e2">bhakti</span>–of devotion; <span class="e2">rase</span>–in the nectar; <span class="e2">vañchita</span>–deprived of; <span class="e2">āra</span>–else; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what?; <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">upāya</span>–means; <span class="e2">patita</span>–of the fallen; <span class="e2">bandhu</span>–friend; <span class="e2">tuhu̐ (tumi)</span>–You; <span class="e2">patita</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">adhama</span>–lowly; <span class="e2">hāma (āmi)</span>–I; <span class="e2">kṛpāya</span>–by Your mercy; <span class="e2">uṭhāo</span>–please pick up; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pāya</span>–to the feet. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Now I am devoid of even a trace of actual knowledge and deprived of the nectar of devotion. What will be my means of deliverance? You are the friend of the fallen, and I am the lowest of the fallen; please mercifully uplift me to Your feet.
বিছারিতে আওবি,<span class="e22">	গুণ নাহি পাওবি,</span><br /><span class="e23">	কৃপা কর ছোড়ত বিচার ।</span><br />তব পদ-পঙ্কজ,<span class="e22">	সীধু পিবাওত,</span><br /><span class="e23">	ভকতিবিনোদে কর’ পার ॥৫॥</span>
vichārite āobi,<span class="e10">	guṇa nāhi pāobi,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kṛpā kara chhoḍata vichāra<br /></span>tava pada-paṅkaja,<span class="e10">	sīdhu pibāota,<br /></span><span class="e11">	bhakativinode kara’ pāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vichārite</span>–to judge; <span class="e2">āobi (āsibe)</span>–will come; <span class="e2">guṇa</span>–good qualities; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">pāobi (pāibe)</span>–will get; <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">kara</span>–please do; <span class="e2">chhoḍata (chhāḍa)</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">vichāra</span>–judgment; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">paṅkaja</span>–lotus; <span class="e2">sīdhu (madhu)</span>–nectar (flower nectar); <span class="e2">pibāota (pāna karāiyā)</span>–causing to drink; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinode</span>–of Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kara’</span>–please do; <span class="e2">pāra</span>–deliverance. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> If You come to judge me, you will not find any good qualities. So, mercifully forgo judgement and induce me to drink the nectar of Your lotus feet. Deliver this Bhakti Vinod.

<span class="e26">	(প্রভু হে!) তুয়া পদে এ মিনতি মোর ।</span><span class="e23"><br /></span>তুয়া পদপল্লব,<span class="e25">	ত্যজত মরুমন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	বিষম বিষয়ে ভেল ভোর ॥১॥</span>
<span class="e11">	(prabhu he!) tuyā pade e minati mora</span><span class="e6"><br /></span>tuyā pada-pallava,<span class="e10">	tyajata maru-mana,</span><span class="e5"><br /></span><span class="e11">	viṣama viṣaye bhela bhora </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">prabhu</span>–Lord; <span class="e2">he!</span>–oh; <span class="e2">tuyā (tomāra)</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">minati (anunaya)</span>–prayer (entreaty); <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">pallava</span>–tender new sprigs; <span class="e2">tyajata (tyāga kariyā)</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">maru-mana (maru-bhūmira nyāya mana)</span>–(my) desert-like heart; <span class="e2">viṣama (ghora)</span>–terrible; <span class="e2">viṣaye</span>–in mundanity; <span class="e2">bhela (ha-ila)</span>–became; <span class="e2">bhora (magna)</span>–deeply absorbed (submerged). [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! This is my prayer at Your feet. Abandoning Your tender feet, my desert-like heart has become deeply submerged in the terrors of mundanity.
উঠয়িতে তাকত,<span class="e25">	পুনঃ নাহি মিলই,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অনুদিন করহুঁ হুতাশ ।<br /></span>দীনজন-নাথ,<span class="e25">	তুহুঁ কহায়সি<br /></span><span class="e26">	তোহারি ছরণ মম আশ ॥২॥</span>
uṭhayite tākata,<span class="e10">	punaḥ nāhi mila-i,<br /></span><span class="e11">	anudina karahu̐ hutāśa<br /></span>dīna-jana-nātha,<span class="e10">	tuhu̐ kahāyasi<br /></span><span class="e11">	tohāri charaṇa mama āśa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">uṭhayite (uṭhite)</span>–to get up; <span class="e2">tākata (śakti, bala, sāmarthya, tāgad)</span>–power, strength, ability, capacity; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not;<span class="e2"> mila-i (militechhe)</span>–I am finding; <span class="e2">anudina (sarvadā)</span>–daily (always, constantly); <span class="e2">karahu̐ (karitechhi)</span>–I am doing; <span class="e2">hutāśa</span>–dismay; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">jana</span>–souls; <span class="e2">nātha</span>–<span class="e2"> </span>Lord; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–to You; <span class="e2">kahāyasi (kathita hao, balāiyā thāka)</span>–are known (it is said); <span class="e2">tohāri (tomāra-i)</span>–of only You;<span class="e2"> charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">āśa</span>–hope. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> I cannot find the strength to rise again, and thus I cons­tantly lament. You are known as the Lord of the fallen; Your feet are my only hope.
ঐছন দীনজন,<span class="e25">	কঁহি নাহি মিলই,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তুহুঁ মোরে কর পরসাদ ।</span><span class="e25"><br /></span>তুয়া জন সঙ্গে,<span class="e25">	তুয়া কথা-রঙ্গে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	ছাড়হুঁ সকল পরমাদ ॥৩॥</span>
aichhana dīna-jana,<span class="e10">	ka̐hi nāhi mila-i,<br /></span><span class="e11">	tuhu̐ more kara parasāda<br /></span>tuyā jana saṅge,<span class="e10">	tuyā kathā-raṅge,<br /></span><span class="e11">	chhāḍahu̐ sakala paramāda </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">aichana (airūpa)</span>–such (something of that kind); <span class="e2">dīna</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">jana</span>–soul; <span class="e2">ka̐hi (kothāo, kona-sthāne)</span>–anywhere, in any place; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">mila-i</span>–I find; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">kara</span>–please do; <span class="e2">parasāda (prasāda, anugraha, kṛpā)</span>–grace, favour, mercy; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">jana</span>–people; <span class="e2">saṅge</span>–in the company; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–of You; <span class="e2">kathā</span>–of discussion; <span class="e2">raṅge</span>–in ecstasy; <span class="e2">chhāḍahu̐</span>–I abandon; <span class="e2">sakala</span>–all; <span class="e2">paramāda</span>–illusion. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Such a fallen soul as I cannot be found anywhere. Please bestow Your mercy upon me. Then in the company of Your devotees, in the ecstasy of discussion about You, I will leave behind all illusion.
তুয়া ধাম-মাহে,<span class="e25">	তুয়া নাম গাওত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	গোঁয়ায়বুঁ দিবানিশি আশ ।</span><span class="e25"><br /></span>তুয়া পদছায়া<span class="e25">	পরম সুশীতল,<br /></span><span class="e26">	মাগে ভকতিবিনোদ দাস ॥৪॥</span>
tuyā dhāma-māhe,<span class="e10">	tuyā nāma gāota,<br /></span><span class="e11">	go̐yāyabu̐ divā-niśi āśa<br /></span>tuyā pada-chhāyā<span class="e10">	parama suśītala,<br /></span><span class="e11">	māge bhakati-vinoda dāsa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dhāma</span>–abode; <span class="e2">māhe (mājhe)</span>–within; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–Name; <span class="e2">gāota (gāhiyā)</span>–singing; <span class="e2">go̐yāyabu̐ (yāpana kariba)</span>–I will pass; <span class="e2">divā</span>–the days; <span class="e2">niśi</span>–and nights; <span class="e2">āśa</span>–hope, desire; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> pada</span>–of feet; <span class="e2">chhāyā</span>–the shade; <span class="e2">parama</span>–supremely; <span class="e2">suśītala</span>–cooling; <span class="e2">māge</span>–begs; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–Your servant. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> I will spend my days and nights in Your abode singing Your Name. Your servant, Bhakti Vinod, prays for the supremely cooling shade of Your feet.
(4<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">suśītala: </span>“The supremely cooling shade of Your feet.” Śrīla Narottam Dās Ṭhākur describes the feet of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu in this way (<span class="e3">Prārthanā</span>: 36.1):
nitāi-pada-kamala,<span class="e5">	koṭī-chandra-suśītala,</span><br /><span class="e6">	ye chhāyāya jagata juḍāya</span>
“Cooling like ten million moons, Nitāi’s lotus feet soothe the world with their shade (they relieve the burning pain of the threefold miseries of material existence).”
(৮)
(8)
এমন দুর্ম্মতি,<span class="e25">	সংসার ভিতরে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পড়িয়া আছিনু আমি ।<br /></span>তব নিজ-জন,<span class="e25">	কোন মহাজনে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পাঠাইয়া দিলে তুমি ॥১॥</span>
emana durmati,<span class="e10">	saṁsāra bhitare,<br /></span><span class="e11">	paḍiyā āchhinu āmi<br /></span>tava nija-jana,<span class="e10">	kona mahājane,<br /></span><span class="e11">	pāṭhāiyā dile tumi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">emana</span>–such; <span class="e2">durmati</span>–evil-hearted;<span class="e2"> saṁsāra</span>–material world; <span class="e2">bhitare</span>–within; <span class="e2">paḍiyā</span>–falling; <span class="e2">āchhinu</span>–am; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nija-jana (pārṣada)</span>–own person (eternal, personal associate); <span class="e2">kona</span>–who; <span class="e2">mahājane (āchārya śrī-gurudeva)</span>–great soul (exemplary teacher, spiritual master); <span class="e2">pāṭhāiyā</span>–sending; <span class="e2">dile</span>–gave; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I am a most sinful-hearted person and have fallen into this material world, but You have sent a great soul, Your own associate (to rescue me).
দয়া করি’ মোরে,<span class="e25">	পতিত দেখিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কহিল আমারে গিয়া ।<br /></span>ওহে দীনজন,<span class="e25">	শুন ভাল কথা,<br /></span><span class="e26">	উল্লসিত হবে হিয়া ॥২॥</span>
dayā kari’ more,<span class="e10">	patita dekhiyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kahila āmāre giyā<br /></span>ohe dīna-jana,<span class="e10">	śuna bhāla kathā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ullasita habe hiyā </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">patita</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">dekhiyā</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">kahila</span>–said; <span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">giyā</span>–going; <span class="e2">ohe</span>–oh!; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–humble; <span class="e2">jana</span>–person; <span class="e2">śuna</span>–please listen; <span class="e2">bhāla</span>–good; <span class="e2">kathā</span>–word; <span class="e2">ullasita</span>–elated; <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">hiyā</span>–heart. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> Seeing my fallen condition and being merciful to me, he came to me and said, “O humble soul, listen to this wonderful message and your heart will rejoice.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> śuna bhāla kathā: </span>“Listen to this wonderful message.” Kṛṣṇa prefaces His final teaching in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(18.64) similarly:
sarva-guhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ<br />iṣṭo ’si me dṛḍham iti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
“Now again hear from Me My supreme teaching, the most hidden treasure of all. I tell you this for your benefit as you are most dear to Me.”
Śrīman Mahāprabhu also alludes to a wonderful message while narrating a parable to Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta</span> (Madhya-līlā, 20.127–8):
‘sarvajña’ āsi’ duḥkha dekhi’ puchhaye tāhāre<br />‘tumi kene duḥkhī, tomāra āchhe pitṛ-dhana’
“Coming to the house of a poor man (a fallen soul) and obser­ving his suffering, Sarvajña (the personification of the revealed scriptures) questioned him, ‘Why are you so miserable? You have a great inheritance!’”
তোমারে তারিতে,<span class="e25">	শ্রীকৃষ্ণচৈতন্য,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নবদ্বীপে অবতার ।<br /></span>তোমা হেন কত,<span class="e25">	দীনহীন জনে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	করিলেন ভবপার ॥৩॥</span>
<span class="e2">tomāre tārite,</span><span class="e10">	śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya,<br /></span><span class="e11">	navadvīpe avatāra<br /></span><span class="e2">tomā hena kata,</span><span class="e10">	dīna-hīna jane,<br /></span><span class="e11">	karilena bhava-pāra</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāre</span>–to you; <span class="e2">tārite</span>–to deliver; <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya</span>–Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">navadvīpe</span>–in Nabadwīp; <span class="e2">avatāra</span>–descent; <span class="e2">tomā</span>–you; <span class="e2">hena</span>–similar; <span class="e2">kata</span>–so many; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–poor; <span class="e2">hīna</span>–lowly; <span class="e2">jane</span>–to persons; <span class="e2">karilena</span>–did; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–of the material existence; <span class="e2">pāra</span>–deliverance. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> “‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya has descended in Nabadwīp to deliver you. He has safely conducted many humble and fallen souls like you across the ocean of material existence.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> śrī kṛṣṇa chaitanya:</span> “Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya.” This name of the Lord is mentioned in the <span class="e3">Padma-purāṇa</span>:
nāma chintāmaṇiḥ kṛṣṇa-chaitanyo rasa-vigrahaḥ<br />pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-mukto ’bhinnatvān nāma-nāminoḥ
“The Name ‘Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya’ is a wish-fulfilling jewel and an embodiment of rasa. He is complete, pure, eternally liberated, and non-different from whom He names.”
<span class="e2">navadvīpe avatāra: </span>“Descended in Nabadwīp.” This is described in the <span class="e3">Ananta-saṁhitā</span>:
avatīrṇo bhaviṣyāmi kalau nija-gaṇaiḥ saha<br />śāchī-garbhe navadvīpe svardhunī-parivārite
“In the Age of Kali, I will descend in Nabadwīp with My eternal associates beside the banks of the Ganges, taking birth from the womb of Śachī Devī.”
<span class="e2">bhava-pāra:</span> “The shore of the ocean of material existence.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(11.5.34), Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu is described as the deliverer of the fallen souls from the ocean of material existence:
dhyeyaṁ sadā paribhava-ghnam abhīṣṭa-dohaṁ<br />tīrthāspadaṁ śiva-viriñchi-nutaṁ śaraṇyam<br />bhṛtyārti-haṁ praṇata-pāla bhavābdhi-potaṁ<br />vande mahā-puruṣa te charaṇāravindam
“O Mahāprabhu! I offer my obeisance unto Your lotus feet, which are the ultimate object of eternal meditation; which destroy illusion and fulfil all desires; which are the supreme place of pilgrimage; which are worshipped by Sadāśiva and Brahmā; which are the shelter of everything; which dispel the suffering of Your servants; which maintain all who surrender unto them; and which are the boat to cross the ocean of material existence.”
বেদের প্রতিজ্ঞা,<span class="e25">	রাখিবার তরে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	রুক্মবর্ণ বিপ্রসুত ।<br /></span>মহাপ্রভু নামে,<span class="e25">	নদীয়া মাতায়,<br /></span><span class="e26">	সঙ্গে ভাই অবধূত ॥৪॥</span>
vedera pratijñā,<span class="e10">	rākhibāra tare,<br /></span><span class="e11">	rukma-varṇa vipra-suta<br /></span>mahāprabhu nāme,<span class="e10">	nadīyā mātāya,<br /></span><span class="e11">	saṅge bhāi avadhūta </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vedera</span>–of the Vedas; <span class="e2">pratijñā</span>–the prophecies; <span class="e2">rākhibāra</span>–to maintain; <span class="e2">tare</span>–for; <span class="e2">rukma-varṇa (gaura-varṇa, puraṭa sundara dyuti)</span>–golden-coloured (beautiful golden radiance); <span class="e2">vipra</span>–of a brāhmaṇ; <span class="e2">suta</span>–a son; <span class="e2">mahāprabhu</span>–<span class="e2">‘</span>Mahāprabhu’; <span class="e2">nāme</span>–Named; <span class="e2">nadīyā</span>–Nadia, the whole world; <span class="e2">mātāya</span>–intoxicated; <span class="e2">saṅge</span>–in the company; <span class="e2">bhāi</span>–brother; <span class="e2">avadhūta</span>–Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> “‘To fulfil the prophecies of the Vedas, He has appeared with a golden complexion as a brāhmaṇ’s son bearing the name ‘Mahāprabhu’ and driven all of Nadia mad with prema in the company of His brother Nityānanda.
(<span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> vedera pratijñā:</span> “The prophecies of the Vedas.” This refers to the promises made in the Vedas that the Supreme Lord would appear as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.
<span class="e2">rukma-varṇa: </span>“Golden complexion.” That the Lord would appear with a golden complexion is prophesied in <span class="e3">Śrī Muṇḍaka-upaniṣad </span>(3.1.3):
yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukma-varṇaṁ<br />kartāram īśaṁ puruṣaṁ brahma-yonim<br />tadā vidvān puṇya-pāpe vidhūya<br />nirañjanaḥ paramaṁ sāmyam upaiti
“When a soul sees the golden Lord, who is the supreme controller and the source of Brahma, they become wise, free from the reactions of both pious and impious activities­, and pure, and they attain supreme equanimity.”
The <span class="e3">Viṣṇu-sahasra-nāma</span> of the <span class="e3">Mahābhārata </span>(Dāna-dharma-parva, 189) has also prophesied the divine form and Pastimes of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu:
suvarṇa-varṇo hemāṅgo varāṅgaś chandanāṅgadī<br />sannyāsa-kṛch chhamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā-śānti-parāyaṇaḥ
“His complexion is golden, His limbs appear like molten gold, His beautiful body is adorned with sandalwood paste and flower garlands, He accepts sannyās, He is equanimous and peaceful, and He is the supreme abode of steadfast devotion (mahābhāva).”
<span class="e2">mahāprabhu: </span>“Bearing the Name ‘Mahāprabhu’.” That the Lord would be known by the Name ‘Mahāprabhu’ is prophesied in <span class="e3">Śrī Śvetāśvatara-upaniṣad</span> (2.12):
mahān prabhur vai puruṣaḥ sattvasyaiṣa pravartakaḥ<br />sunirmalam imaṁ prāptiṁ īśāno jyotir avyayaḥ
“Śrī Mahāprabhu, the supreme master, is verily the Supreme Person­ality of Godhead. He is the originator of existence, the eternally effulgent Lord. By His grace one attains ultimate purity.”
<span class="e2">avadhūta:</span> “Nityānanda.” An avadhūt has been described by Śrīla Śrīdhar Swāmī in his commentary on <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>as <span class="e3">avajñayā-janais tyakto yaḥ</span>, one who is abandoned by general people with disregard (because his ecstatic, purely devotional behaviour is incomprehensible).
নন্দসুত যিনি,<span class="e25">	চৈতন্য গোসাঞী,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নিজ নাম করি’ দান ।<br /></span>তারিল জগৎ,<span class="e25">	তুমিও যাইয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	লহ নিজ পরিত্রান ॥৫॥</span>
nanda-suta yini,<span class="e10">	chaitanya gosāñi,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nija nāma kari’ dāna<br /></span>tārila jagat,<span class="e10">	tumio yāiyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	laha nija paritrāna </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nanda</span>–of Nanda Mahārāj; <span class="e2">suta</span>–the son (Kṛṣṇa); <span class="e2">yini</span>–who; <span class="e2">chaitanya</span>–Chaitanya; <span class="e2">gosāñi</span>–great personage; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–Name; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">dāna</span>–gift; <span class="e2">tārila</span>–delivered;<span class="e2"> jagat</span>–the world; <span class="e2">tumio</span>–you also, too; <span class="e2">yāiyā</span>–going; <span class="e2">laha</span>–accept; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own;<span class="e2"> paritrāṇa</span>–deliverance. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> “‘Śrī Chaitanya Gosāñi, who is Nanda Suta Himself, has delivered the universe by distributing His Name. You too should go and accept your deliverance.’”
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> nanda-suta:</span> “The son of Nanda.” Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu has described the identity of Śrīman Mahāprabhu in his <span class="e3">Tattva-­sandarbha </span>(2):
antaḥ kṛṣṇaṁ bahir gauraṁ darśitāṅgādi-vaibhavam<br />kalau saṅkīrtanādyaiḥ sma kṛṣṇa-chaitanyam āśritāḥ
“Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya is internally Kṛṣṇa Himself and outwardly golden. He has manifest in the Age of Kali in all His glory, accompanied by His entourage. We take shelter of Him by performing Hari-nām-saṅkīrtan and related devotional services.”
Śrīman Mahāprabhu is also described in the <span class="e3">Kapila-tantra</span>:
premāliṅgana-yogena chāchintya-śakti-yogataḥ<br />rādhā-bhāva-kānti-yutāṁ mūrtim ekāṁ prakāśayet
“By the loving embrace of His inconceivable potency, Kṛṣṇa has mani­fested a form enriched with the heart and halo of Śrī Rādhā—the divine form of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu.”
সে কথা শুনিয়া,<span class="e25">	আসিয়াছি নাথ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তোমার চরণতলে ।<br /></span>ভকতিবিনোদ,<span class="e25">	কাঁদিয়া কঁদিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	আপন কাহিনী বলে ॥৬॥</span>
se kathā śuniyā,<span class="e10">	āsiyāchhi, nātha!<br /></span><span class="e11">	tomāra charaṇa-tale<br /></span>bhakati-vinoda,<span class="e10">	kā̐diyā kā̐diyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	āpana kāhinī bale </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">se</span>–this; <span class="e2">kathā</span>–message; <span class="e2">śuniyā</span>–hearing; <span class="e2">āsiyāchhi</span>–I have come; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">tale</span>–beneath; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–crying; <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–and crying; <span class="e2">āpana</span>–personal; <span class="e2">kāhinī (kathā)</span>–tale <span class="e2">(</span>narrative); <span class="e2">bale</span>–speaks. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Hearing this message, I have come before Your feet. Crying incessantly, Bhakti Vinod tells the story of his life.

(9)
না করলুঁ করম,<span class="e25">	গেয়ান নাহি ভেল,<br /></span><span class="e26">	না সেবিলুঁ ছরণ তোহার ।<br /></span>জড়সুখে মাতিয়া,<span class="e25">	আপনকু বঞ্চই,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পেখহুঁ ছৌদিশ আন্ধিয়ার ॥১॥</span>
nā karalu̐ karama,<span class="e10">	geyāna nāhi bhela,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nā sevilu̐ charaṇa tohāra<br /></span>jaḍa-sukhe mātiyā,<span class="e10">	āpanaku vañcha-i<br /></span><span class="e11">	pekhahu̐ chaudiśa āndhiyāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">karalu̐ (karilāma)</span>–I did; <span class="e2">karama (karma)</span>–pious deeds; <span class="e2">geyāna (jñāna)</span>–knowledge; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">bhela</span>–happened; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">sevilu̐ (sevilāma)</span>–I served; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">tohāra (tomāra)</span>–Your; <span class="e2">jaḍa</span>–material; <span class="e2">sukhe</span>–by pleasures; <span class="e2">mātiyā</span>–being intoxicated; <span class="e2">āpanaku (āpanake)</span>–to myself; <span class="e2">vañcha-i (vañchanā kariyā)</span>–cheating; <span class="e2">pekhahu̐ (dekhitechhi)</span>–I see; <span class="e2">chaudiśa (chāridik)</span>–in the four directions; <span class="e2">āndhiyāra (andhakāra)</span>–blinding darkness. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I have never performed any good works. I have never acquired any knowledge. I have never served Your feet. Maddened by mundane pleasures, cheating my own self, I see darkness in all directions.
<span class="e26">	তুহুঁ নাথ! করুণানিদান ।<br /></span>তুয়া পদপঙ্কজে,<span class="e25">	আত্মসমর্পিলুঁ<br /></span><span class="e26">	মোরে কৃপা করবি বিধান ॥২॥</span>
<span class="e11">	tuhu̐ nātha! karuṇā-nidāna</span><span class="e6"><br /></span>tuyā pada-paṅkaje,<span class="e10">	ātma-samarpilu̐</span><span class="e5"><br /></span><span class="e11">	more kṛpā karabi vidhāna </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–Lord!; <span class="e2">karuṇā</span>–of mercy; <span class="e2">nidāna (ākara)</span>–ocean (source); <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">paṅkaje</span>–at the lotus; <span class="e2">ātma</span>–self; <span class="e2">samarpilu̐ (samarpaṇa karilāma)</span>–I fully offered; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">karabi</span>–please make; <span class="e2">vidhāna (vyavasthā)</span>–arrangements. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! You are the source of all mercy. I have fully surrendered myself at Your lotus feet; please make arrangements to bestow Your mercy upon me.
প্রতিজ্ঞা তোহার ঐ<span class="e25">	য়োহি শরণাগত<br /></span><span class="e26">	নাহি সো জানব পরমাদ ।<br /></span>সো হাম দুষ্কৃতি,<span class="e25">	গতি না হেরই আন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	আব্ মগোঁ তুয়া পরসাদ ॥৩॥</span>
pratijñā tohāra ai<span class="e10">	yohi śaraṇāgata<br /></span><span class="e11">	nāhi so jānaba paramāda<br /></span>so hāma duṣkṛti,<span class="e10">	gati nā hera-i āna,<br /></span><span class="e11">	āb mago̐ tuyā parasāda </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">pratijñā</span>–promise; <span class="e2">tohāra (tomāra)</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ai</span>–that; <span class="e2">yohi</span>–who; <span class="e2">śaraṇāgata</span>–a surrendered soul; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">so (sei)</span>–he; <span class="e2">jānaba</span>–will know; <span class="e2">paramāda</span>–illusion; <span class="e2">so</span>–he; <span class="e2">hāma</span>–I; <span class="e2">duṣkṛti</span>–misbehaviour; <span class="e2">gati</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">hera-i</span>–I see; <span class="e2">āna</span>–another; <span class="e2">āb</span>–now<span class="e2">;</span> <span class="e2">māgo̐ (māgitechhi)</span>–I beg; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">parasāda (prasāda)</span>–mercy. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Your promise is that one who is surrendered will never know illusion. I am most sinful and see no other shelter but You; I now pray for Your mercy.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> pratijñā tohāra: </span>“Your promise.” As Rāmchandra proclaims:
sakṛd eva prapanno yas tavāsmīti cha yāchate
abhayam sarvadā tasmai dadāmy etad vrataṁ mama
(Rāmāyaṇa: Yuddha-kāṇḍa, 18.33)
“Anyone who even once sincerely surrenders unto Me, declaring, ‘I am Yours’, and prays for fearlessness—it is My vow that I will always grant that to them.”
<span class="e2">gati nā hera-i:</span> “I see no other shelter.” This sentiment has been expressed by Śrī Yāmun Āchārya in his <span class="e3">Śrī Stotra-ratna </span>(22):
na dharma-niṣṭho ’smi na chātma-vedī<br />na bhaktimāṁs tvach-charaṇaravinde<br />akiñchano ’nanya-gatiḥ śaraṇya<br />tvat-pāda-mūlaṁ śaraṇam prapadye
“O Supreme Refuge, I am not religious, I do not know the nature of the soul, and I do not have any devotion to Your lotus feet. I am bereft and have no other shelter. Such as I am, I surrender unto the soles of Your feet.”
আন মনোরথ,<span class="e25">	নিঃশেষ ছোড়ত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কব্ হাম্ হউবুঁ তোহারা ।<br /></span>নিত্য-সেব্য তুহুঁ<span class="e25">	নিত্য-সেবক মুঞি<br /></span><span class="e26">	ভকতিবিনোদ ভাব-সারা ॥৪॥</span>
āna manoratha,<span class="e10">	niḥśeṣa chhoḍata,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kab hām ha-ubhu̐ tohārā<br /></span>nitya-sevya tuhu̐<span class="e10">	nitya-sevaka muñi<br /></span><span class="e11">	bhakati-vinoda bhāva sārā </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āna (anya)</span>–other; <span class="e2">manoratha (abhilāṣa)</span>–wishes (desires); <span class="e2">niḥśeṣa (sampūrṇa-rūpe)</span>–completely (fully); <span class="e2">chhoḍata</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">kab</span>–when?; <span class="e2">hām</span>–I; <span class="e2">ha-ubhu̐ (ha-iba)</span>–will be; <span class="e2">tohārā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternally; <span class="e2">sevya</span>–who is to be served; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">sevaka</span>–servant;<span class="e2"> muñi</span>–I; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–of Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">bhāva</span>–of the heart; <span class="e2">sārā (sāra, athavā samasta)</span>–essence (substance, or everything). [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> When will I completely abandon all other desires and become Yours? You are my eternal Lord, and I am Your eternal servant. This is the essence of Bhakti Vinod’s heart.
(১০)
(10)
<span class="e26">	(প্রাণেশ্বর!) কহবুঁ কি সরম কি বাত ।<br /></span>ঐছন পাপ নাহি,<span class="e25">	যো হাম্ না করলুঁ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	সহস্র সহস্র বেরি নাথ! ॥১॥</span>
<span class="e11">	(prāṇeśvara!) kahabu̐ ki sarama ki bāta</span><span class="e6"><br /></span>aichhana pāpa nāhi,<span class="e10">	yo hām nā karalu̐,</span><span class="e5"><br /></span><span class="e11">	sahasra sahasra beri nātha! </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">prāṇa</span>–of my heart; <span class="e2">īśvara!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">kahabu̐</span>–I will tell; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what?; <span class="e2">sarama</span>–shame; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what?; <span class="e2">bāta</span>–explanation; <span class="e2">aichhana (airūpa)</span>–such (that kind); <span class="e2">pāpa</span>–sin; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">yo</span>–which; <span class="e2">hām</span>–I; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">karalu̐</span>–did; <span class="e2">sahasra</span>–thousands; <span class="e2">sahasra</span>–and thousands; <span class="e2">beri (bāra)</span>–of times; <span class="e2">nātha</span>–O Lord! [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord of my heart! How can I explain my shame? O Lord! There is no sin I have not committed thousands and thousands of times.
(1<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">kahabu̐ ki sarama ki bāta: “</span>How can I explain my shame?” This can also be expressed as, “How shall I express the tale of my shame?”
<span class="e2">aichhana pāpa nāhi … sahasra beri nātha!:</span> “There is no sin I have not committed thousands of times.” This sentiment is expressed by Śrī Yāmun Āchārya in his <span class="e3">Śrī Stotra-ratna</span> (20):
na ninditaṁ karma tad asti loke<br />sahasraśo yan na mayā vyadhāyi<br />so ’haṁ vipākāvasare mukunda<br />krandāmi sampraty agatis tavāgre
“O Mukunda! There is no sinful act in this world that I have not committed thousands and thousands of times. Now, as the reactions for these sins strike down upon me, I have no alternative but to simply weep before You.”
সোহি করম-ফল,<span class="e25">	ভবে মোকে পেশই<br /></span><span class="e26">	দোখ্ দেওব আব কাহি ।<br /></span>তখনক পরিণাম,<span class="e25">	কছু না বিচারলুঁ<br /></span><span class="e26">	আব্ পছু তরইতে চাহি ॥২॥</span>
sohi karama-phala,<span class="e10">	bhave moke peśa-i<br /></span><span class="e11">	dokh deoba āba kāhi<br /></span>takhanaka pariṇāma,<span class="e10">	kachhu nā vichāralu̐<br /></span><span class="e11">	āb pachhu tara-ite chāhi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sohi (sei)</span>–those; <span class="e2">karama</span>–actions; <span class="e2">phala</span>–results; <span class="e2">bhave (saṁsāre)</span>–in the material world; <span class="e2">moke (āmāke)</span>–to me; <span class="e2">peśa-i (peṣaṇa kare)</span>–crush; <span class="e2">dokh (doṣa)</span>–fault; <span class="e2">deoba (diba)</span>–I will give; <span class="e2">āba</span>–now; <span class="e2">kāhi (kāke)</span>–to whom? <span class="e2">takhanaka (takhana)</span>–then; <span class="e2">pariṇāma</span>–the results; <span class="e2">kachhu (kichhu)</span>–some; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">vichāralu̐</span>–I considered; <span class="e2">āb</span>–now; <span class="e2">pachhu (pichhe)</span>–afterwards; <span class="e2">tara-ite (uttīrṇa ha-ite)</span>–to be delivered; <span class="e2">chāhi</span>–I want. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> The consequences of those sinful actions crash down upon me in this material world. Who shall I now blame? Previ­ously I did not consider the consequences, yet now I want to be exonerated.
দোখ বিচারই,<span class="e25">	তুহুঁ দণ্ড দেওবি,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হাম ভোগ করবুঁ সংসার ।<br /></span>করত গতাগতি,<span class="e25">	ভকত-জন-সঞে<br /></span><span class="e26">	মতি রহুঁ চরণে তোহার ॥৩॥</span>
dokha vichāra-i,<span class="e10">	tuhu̐ daṇḍa deobi,<br /></span><span class="e11">	hāma bhoga karabu̐ saṁsāra<br /></span>karata gatāgati,<span class="e10">	bhakata-jana-sañe<br /></span><span class="e11">	mati rahu̐ charaṇe tohāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dokha</span>–faults; <span class="e2">vichāra-i (vichāra kariyā)</span>–judging; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">daṇḍa</span>–punishment; <span class="e2">deobi (dibe)</span>–will give; <span class="e2">hāma</span>–I; <span class="e2">bhoga</span>–experience; <span class="e2">karabu̐</span>–will do; <span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–the material world; <span class="e2">karata (karite karite)</span>–while doing; <span class="e2">gatāgati</span>–coming and going; <span class="e2">bhakata</span>–of devotees; <span class="e2">jana</span>–persons; <span class="e2">sañe</span>–in the association; <span class="e2">mati</span>–heart; <span class="e2">rahu̐ (thākuka)</span>–may remain; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">tohāra</span>–Your. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Judging my sins, You will punish me, and I will endure the sufferings of this material world. Yet as I come and go (revolve within the cycle of perpetual birth and death), please let me remain in the association of Your devotees, my heart fixed upon Your feet.
আপন চতুরপণ,<span class="e25">	তুয়া পদে সোঁপলুঁ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হৃদয়-গরব দূরে গেলা ।<br /></span>দীন দয়াময়,<span class="e25">	তুয়া কৃপা নিরমল<br /></span><span class="e26">	ভকতিবিনোদ আশা ভেলা ॥৪॥</span>
āpana chaturapaṇa,<span class="e10">	tuyā pade so̐palu̐,<br /></span><span class="e11">	hṛdaya-garava dūre gelā<br /></span>dīna dayā-maya,<span class="e10">	tuyā kṛpā niramala<br /></span><span class="e11">	bhakati-vinoda āśā bhelā </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āpana</span>–my own; <span class="e2">chaturapaṇa (buddhimattā)</span>–intelligence; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">so̐palu̐</span>–I place in the care of; <span class="e2">hṛdaya</span>–of the heart; <span class="e2">garava (garva)</span>–pride; <span class="e2">dūre</span>–far away; <span class="e2">gelā</span>–went; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–to the fallen; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">maya</span>–full of; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">niramala (nirmala)</span>–spotless, pure; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">āśā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">bhelā (ha-ila)</span>–became. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> I offer my intelligence at Your feet; the pride in my heart has gone away. You are merciful to the fallen, and Your pure mercy has become the desire of Bhakti Vinod.
(১১)
(11)
মানস, দেহ, গেহ, যো কিছু মোর ।<br />অর্পিলুঁ তুয়া পদে নন্দকিশোর ॥১॥
mānasa, deha, geha, yo kichhu mora<br />arpilu̐ tuyā pade nanda-kiśora <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">mānasa (mana)</span>–mind; <span class="e2">deha</span>–body; <span class="e2">geha (gṛha)</span>–home; <span class="e2">yo</span>–which; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–something; <span class="e2">mora</span>–mine; <span class="e2">arpilu̐ (arpaṇa karilāma)</span>–I offered; <span class="e2">tuyā (tomāra)</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">nanda</span>–of Nanda Mahārāj; <span class="e2">kiśora</span>–adolescent son. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I have offered my mind, my body, my household, and whatever else may be mine at Your feet, O Nanda Kiśor!
সম্পদে বিপদে জীবনে মরণে ।<br />দায় মম গেলা তুয়া ও পদ বরণে ॥২॥
sampade vipade jīvane maraṇe<br />dāya mama gelā tuyā o pada varaṇe <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sampade</span>–in happiness, good fortune, affluence, health; <span class="e2">vipade</span>–in distress, danger, poverty, sickness, misfortune; <span class="e2">jīvane</span>–in life; <span class="e2">maraṇe</span>–in death; <span class="e2">dāya (dāyitva)</span>–responsibility, anxiety; <span class="e2">mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">gelā</span>–went; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">o</span>–those;<span class="e2"> pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">varaṇe</span>–by accepting, choosing. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> In good times and in bad, in life and in death, all responsibility has gone away by embracing Your feet.
মারবি রাখবি যো ইচ্ছা তোহারা ।<br />নিত্যদাস প্রতি তুয়া অধিকারা ॥৩॥
mārabi rākhabi yo ichchhā tohārā<br />nitya-dāsa prati tuyā adhikārā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">mārabi (māribe)</span>–You may kill; <span class="e2">rākhabi</span>–You may protect; <span class="e2">yo (ye)</span>–which; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">tohārā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–to Your servant; <span class="e2">prati</span>–towards; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">adhikāra</span>–authority. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> You may kill me or protect me as You wish. You have full authority over Your eternal servant.
জন্মাওবি মোয়ে ইচ্ছা যদি তোর ।<br />ভক্তগৃহে জনি জন্ম হউ মোর ॥৪॥
janmāobi moye ichchhā yadi tora<br />bhakta-gṛhe jani janma ha-u mora <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">janmāobi</span>–You may cause to take birth; <span class="e2">moye</span>–to me; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">yadi</span>–if; <span class="e2">tora</span>–Your; <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–(of a) devotee; <span class="e2">gṛhe</span>–in the home; <span class="e2">jani (yena)</span>–so that; <span class="e2">janma</span>–birth; <span class="e2">ha-u (ha-uka)</span>–let be; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> If it is Your desire that I take birth again, let me do so in the home of Your devotee.
কীট জন্ম হউ যথা তুয়া দাস ।<br />বহির্মুখ ব্রহ্মজন্মে নাহি আশ ॥৫॥
kīṭa janma ha-u yathā tuyā dāsa<br />bahir-mukha brahma-janme nāhi āśa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kīṭa</span>–a worm, insect; <span class="e2">janma</span>–birth; <span class="e2">ha-u</span>–may be; <span class="e2">yathā</span>–as long as; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servant; <span class="e2">bahir</span>–outward; <span class="e2">mukha</span>–facing; <span class="e2">brahma</span>–as Brahmā, the universal creator; <span class="e2">janme</span>–such a birth; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">āśa</span>–desire. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Let me be born again even as a worm, so long as I can remain Your servant. I have no desire to be born even as Brahmā, if I will be averse to You.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> kīṭa janma ha-u:</span> “Let me be born again even as a worm …” This sentiment has been expressed by Śrī Yāmun Āchārya in his <span class="e3">Śrī Stotra-ratna </span>(55):
tava dāsya-sukhaika saṅgināṁ<br />bhavaneṣv astv api kīṭa-janma me<br />itarāv asatheṣu mā sma bhūd<br />api me janma chaturmukhātmanā
“O Lord! Let me take birth, even as a worm, in the home of those whose sole happiness is Your service. O Lord, never let me take birth, even as Brahmā, among those who are averse to You.”
ভুক্তি-মুক্তিস্পৃহা-বিহীন যে ভক্ত ।<br />লভইতে তাঁ’ক সঙ্গ অনুরক্ত ॥৬॥
bhukti-mukti-spṛhā-vihīna ye bhakta<br />labha-ite tā̐’ka saṅga anurakta <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
