<span class="e2">bhukti</span>–mundane enjoyment, exploitation; <span class="e2">mukti</span>–liberation, renunciation; <span class="e2">spṛhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">vihīna</span>–without; <span class="e2">ye</span>–who; <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–devotees;<span class="e2"> labha-ite (lābha karite)</span>–to obtain; <span class="e2">tā̐’ka (tā̐dera)</span>–their; <span class="e2">saṅga</span>–association; <span class="e2">anurakta (anurāga)</span>–attachment (loving attachment). [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> I am always eager to attain the association of devotees who are completely devoid of all desire for mundane enjoyment and liberation.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">6</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> bhukti-mukti-spṛhā: </span>“Desire for mundane enjoyment and liberation.” In this regard the following verse from <span class="e3">Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span> (1.2.22) should be mentioned:
bhukti-mukti-spṛhā yāvat piśāchī hṛdi vartate<br />tāvad bhakti-sukhasyātra katham abhyudayo bhavet
“So long as the desires for mundane enjoyment and liberation, which are like two witches, remain in the heart, how can the ecstasy of devotion manifest there?”
জনক, জননী, দয়িত, তনয় ।<br />প্রভু, গুরু, পতি তুহুঁ—সর্ব্বময় ॥৭॥
janaka, jananī, dayita, tanaya<br />prabhu, guru, pati tuhu̐—sarva-maya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">janaka</span>–father; <span class="e2">jananī</span>–mother; <span class="e2">dayita (priya)</span>–beloved; <span class="e2">tanaya</span>–son; <span class="e2">pra­bhu</span>–Lord; <span class="e2">guru</span>–spiritual master; <span class="e2">pati</span>–husband; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–all; <span class="e2">maya</span>–consist of. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> Father, mother, lover, son, Lord, Guru, husband—You are everywhere.
(7<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">tuhu̐ sarva-maya: </span>“You are everywhere.” That is to say, “The deep touch of Your connection is all-pervading. (Essentially, in all my relationships I am relating with You.)”
ভকতিবিনোদ কহে শুন কান! ।<br />রাধানাথ! তুহুঁ হামার পরাণ ॥৮॥
bhakati-vinoda kahe śuna kāna!<br />rādhānātha! tuhu̐ hāmāra parāṇa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kahe</span>–says; <span class="e2">śuna</span>–please listen; <span class="e2">kāna! (kānāi!)</span>–O Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">rādhānātha!</span>–O Lord of Rādhā; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">hāmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">parāṇa</span>–life, soul (the sole focus of my loving attachment). [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> Bhakti Vinod says, “Please listen, O Kān! O Rādhānāth! You are my life and soul.”
(১২)
(12)
‘অহং’-‘মম’-শব্দ অর্থে যাহা কিছু হয় ।<br />অর্পিলুঁ তোমার পদে ওহে দয়াময়! ॥১॥
‘ahaṁ’-‘mama’-śabda arthe yāhā kichhu haya<br />arpilu̐ tomāra pade ohe dayā-maya! <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">‘aham’</span>–<span class="e2">‘</span>I’; ‘<span class="e2">mama’</span>–<span class="e2">‘</span>mine’; <span class="e2">śabda</span>–of the words; <span class="e2">arthe</span>–by the meaning; <span class="e2">yāhā</span>–which; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–anything; <span class="e2">haya</span>–happens; <span class="e2">arpilu̐</span>–I offered; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">ohe</span>–oh!; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">maya</span>–made of. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O merciful Lord! I have surrendered all that is meant by the words ‘I’ and ‘mine’ at Your feet.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> ‘ahaṁ’ ‘mama’-śabda arthe:</span> “Meant by the words ‘I’ and ‘mine’.” Śrī Yāmun Āchārya has explained this in his <span class="e3">Śrī Stotra-­ratna </span>(49):
vapur-ādiṣu yo ’pi ko ’pi vā<br />guṇato ’sāni yathā-tathā-vidhaḥ<br />tad ahaṁ tava pāda-padmayor<br />aham adyaiva mayā samarpitaḥ
“O Lord, whatever I possess in terms of this body and its paraphernalia, and whatever character I have acquired through the modes of nature—this whole sense of ego I offer at Your lotus feet today.”
‘আমার’ আমি ত’ নাথ! না রহিনু আর ।<br />এখন হইনু আমি কেবল তোমার ॥২॥
‘āmāra’ āmi ta’ nātha! nā rahinu āra<br />ekhana ha-inu āmi kevala tomāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">‘āmāra’</span>–‘my’; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">nā</span>–does not; <span class="e2">rahinu</span>–I remained; <span class="e2">āra</span>–more; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>–became; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">kevala</span>–only; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Yours. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! I no longer remain ‘mine’. I have now become Yours exclusively.
‘আমি’-শব্দে দেহী জীব অহংতা ছাড়িল ।<br />ত্বদীয়াভিমান আজি হৃদয়ে পশিল ॥৩॥
‘āmi’-śabde dehī jīva ahaṁtā chhāḍila<br />tvadīyābhimāna āji hṛdaye paśila <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">‘āmi’</span>–‘I’; <span class="e2">śabde</span>–by the word; <span class="e2">dehī</span>–animator of the material body; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–the life, the soul; <span class="e2">ahaṁtā</span>–the conception of ‘I’, false egotism; <span class="e2">chhāḍila</span>–abandoned; <span class="e2">tvadīya</span>–Your own; <span class="e2">abhimāna</span>–ego; <span class="e2">āji</span>–today; <span class="e2">hṛdaye</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">paśila (praveśa karila)</span>–entered. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> I now understand that the word ‘I’ means the soul who animates the material body and have thus abandoned all false egotism. Today the ego of being ‘Your own’ has entered my heart.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> tvadīyābhimāna: </span>“The ego of being ‘Your own’.” This means the ego of being Your (the Lord’s) faithfully devoted follower (anu­gata-jan).
আমার সর্ব্বস্ব, দেহ, গেহ, অনুচর ।<br />ভাই, বন্ধু, দারা, সুত, দ্রব্য, দ্বার, ঘর ॥৪॥<br />সে সব হইল তব, আমি হইনু দাস ।<br />তোমার গৃহেতে এবে আমি করি বাস ॥৫॥
āmāra sarvasva, deha, geha, anuchara<br />bhāi, bandhu, dārā, suta, dravya, dvāra, ghara <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />se saba ha-ila tava, āmi ha-inu dāsa<br />tomāra gṛhete ebe āmi kari vāsa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">sarvasva</span>–the whole of my wealth; <span class="e2">deha</span>–body; <span class="e2">geha</span>–home; <span class="e2">anuchara</span>–servants; <span class="e2">bhāi</span>–brothers; <span class="e2">bandhu</span>–friends and relatives; <span class="e2">dārā</span>–wife; <span class="e2">suta</span>–children; <span class="e2">dravya</span>–possessions; <span class="e2">dvāra</span>–door; <span class="e2">ghara</span>–house; <span class="e2">se</span>–them; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Yours; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>–became; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>– servant; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">gṛhete</span>–in Your house; <span class="e2">ebe</span>–now; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">kari</span>–do; <span class="e2">vāsa</span>–residence. [<span class="e24">4</span>–<span class="e24">5</span>]
(4–5<span class="e14">)</span> Everything I considered mine­—my body, home, servants, brothers, friends, wife, children, personal belongings, and household—has become Yours. I have become Your servant, and I now reside in Your house.
তুমি গৃহস্বামী, আমি সেবক তোমার ।<br />তোমার সুখেতে চেষ্টা এখন আমার ॥৬॥
tumi gṛha-svāmī, āmi sevaka tomāra<br />tomāra sukhete cheṣṭā ekhana āmāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">gṛha</span>–of the house; <span class="e2">svāmī</span>–the master; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">sevaka</span>–servant; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sukhete</span>–for Your pleasure; <span class="e2">cheṣṭā</span>–endeavours; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> You are the master of the house, and I am Your servant. All my endeavours are now for Your satisfaction.
স্থূল-লিঙ্গ-দেহে মোর সুকৃত দুষ্কৃত ।<br />আর মোর নহে, প্রভু! আমি ত’ নিষ্কৃত ॥৭॥
sthūla-liṅga-dehe mora sukṛta duṣkṛta<br />āra mora nahe, prabhu! āmi ta’ niṣkṛta <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sthūla</span>–gross; <span class="e2">liṅga</span>–subtle; <span class="e2">dehe</span>–with the bodies; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">sukṛta</span>–good deeds; <span class="e2">duṣkṛta</span>–bad deeds; <span class="e2">āra</span>–any more; <span class="e2">mora</span>–mine; <span class="e2">nahe</span>–not; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">niṣkṛta</span>–free, liberated. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> Whatever good or bad deeds are performed by my gross and subtle bodies are no longer mine, O Lord! I am free.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">7</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> sukṛta duṣkṛta: </span>“Good or bad deeds.” The state of being beyond the scope of both good and bad actions and reactions is described in <span class="e3">Śrī Muṇḍaka-upaniṣad </span>(3.1.3):
yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukma-varṇaṁ<br />kartāram īśaṁ puruṣaṁ brahma-yonim<br />tadā vidvān puṇya-pāpe vidhūya<br />nirañjanaḥ paramaṁ sāmyam upaiti
“When a soul sees the golden Lord, who is the supreme controller and the source of Brahma, they become wise, free from the reactions of both pious and impious activities­, and pure, and they attain supreme equanimity.”
তোমার ইচ্ছায় মোর ইচ্ছা মিশাইল ।<br />ভকতিবিনোদ আজ আপনে ভুলিল ॥৮॥
tomāra ichchhāya mora ichchhā miśāila<br />bhakati-vinoda āja āpane bhulila <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhāya</span>–with desire; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">miśāila</span>–mixed; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">āja</span>–today; <span class="e2">āpane</span>–himself; <span class="e2">bhulila</span>–forgot. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> My desires have merged with Your desires. Today, Bhakti Vinod has forgotten himself.
(১৩)
(13)
‘আমার’ বলিতে প্রভু! আর কিছু নাই ।<br />তুমি-ই আমার মাত্র পিতা-বন্ধু-ভাই ॥১॥
‘āmāra’ balite prabhu! āra kichhu nāi<br />tumi-i āmāra mātra pitā-bandhu-bhāi <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">‘āmāra’</span>–‘mine’; <span class="e2">balite</span>–to consider; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">āra</span>–another; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–something; <span class="e2">nāi</span>–is not; <span class="e2">tumi-i</span>–You alone; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">pitā</span>–father; <span class="e2">bandhu</span>–friend; <span class="e2">bhāi</span>–brother. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Nothing else is to be considered ‘mine’. You alone are my father, my friend, and my brother.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> pitā-bandhu-bhāi: </span>“You alone are my father, my friend, and my brother.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(11.44), Arjun prays to Kṛṣṇa similarly:
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṁ<br />prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam<br />piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ<br />priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum
“Offering my prostrate obeisance unto You, I pray for Your mercy, O worshippable Lord! As a father, friend, or lover forgives his son, dear companion, or beloved, please mercifully forgive my offences.”
বন্ধু, দারা, সুত, সুতা, তব দাসী, দাস ।<br />সেই ত’ সম্বন্ধে সবে আমার প্রয়াস ॥২॥
bandhu, dārā, suta, sutā, tava dāsī, dāsa<br />sei ta’ sambandhe sabe āmāra prayāsa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bandhu</span>–friends; <span class="e2">dārā</span>–wife;<span class="e2"> suta</span>–sons; <span class="e2">sutā</span>–daughters; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dāsī</span>–maidservants; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servants;<span class="e2"> sei</span>–that; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">sambandhe</span>–in relationship; <span class="e2">sabe</span>–with all; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">prayāsa</span>–endeavours. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> My friends, wife, sons, and daughters are all Your servants and maidservants. All my endeavours are based on that relationship.
ধন, জন, গৃহ, দ্বার, ‘তোমার’ বলিয়া ।<br />রক্ষা করি আমি মাত্র সেবক হইয়া ॥৩॥
dhana, jana, gṛha, dvāra, ‘tomāra’ baliyā<br />rakṣā kari āmi mātra sevaka ha-iyā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dhana</span>–wealth; <span class="e2">jana</span>–people; <span class="e2">gṛha</span>–household; <span class="e2">dvāra</span>–gateway; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Yours; <span class="e2">baliyā</span>–considering; <span class="e2">rakṣā</span>–protection; <span class="e2">kari</span>–do; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">matra</span>–only; <span class="e2">sevaka</span>–servant; <span class="e2">ha-iyā</span>–being. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Considering my wealth, relatives, and household to be ‘Yours’, only as Your servant do I maintain them.
তোমার কার্য্যের তরে উপার্জ্জিব ধন ।<br />তোমার সংসারব্যয় করিব বহন ॥৪॥
tomāra kāryera tare upārjiba dhana<br />tomāra saṁsāra-vyaya kariba vahana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">kāryera</span>–of the duty; <span class="e2">tare</span>–for; <span class="e2">upārjiba</span>–I will earn; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–money; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–of the household; <span class="e2">vyaya</span>–expenses; <span class="e2">kariba</span>–I will do; <span class="e2">vahana</span>–bearing. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> In order to maintain what is Yours, I will earn money and bear the expenses of Your household.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> tomāra kāryera tare upārjiba dhana: “</span>In order to maintain what is Yours, I will earn money.” This practice is described as an integral limb of devotion in <span class="e3">Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span>: <span class="e3">tad arthe </span>’<span class="e3">khila cheṣṭitam</span>, “Performing all of one’s endeavours for Kṛṣṇa’s sake.”
ভালমন্দ নাহি জানি সেবামাত্র করি ।<br />তোমার সংসারে আমি বিষয়-প্রহরী ॥৫॥
bhāla-manda nāhi jāni sevā-mātra kari<br />tomāra saṁsāre āmi viṣaya-praharī <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhāla</span>–good; <span class="e2">manda</span>–bad; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">jāni</span>–I know; <span class="e2">sevā</span>–service; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">kari</span>–I do; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the household;<span class="e2"> āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">viṣaya</span>–property; <span class="e2">praharī</span>–watchman. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> I do not know what is good or what is bad; I only serve. I am simply a guardian of the property within Your household.
তোমার ইচ্ছায় মোর ইন্দ্রিয়-চালনা ।<br />শ্রবণ, দর্শন, ঘ্রাণ, ভোজন-বাসনা ॥৬॥
tomāra ichchhāya mora indriya-chālanā<br />śravaṇa, darśana, ghrāṇa, bhojana-vāsanā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhāya</span>–by the desire; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">indriya</span>–of the senses; <span class="e2">chālanā</span>–direction; <span class="e2">śravaṇa</span>–hearing; <span class="e2">darśana</span>–seeing; <span class="e2">ghrāṇa</span>–smelling; <span class="e2">bhojana</span>–eating; <span class="e2">vāsanā</span>–desires. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> I direct my senses—my desires for hearing, seeing, smelling, tasting, and so forth—in accordance with Your will.
নিজসুখ লাগি’ কিছু নাহি করি আর ।<br />ভকতিবিনোদ বলে তব সুখ সার ॥৭॥
nija-sukha lāgi’ kichhu nāhi kari āra<br />bhakati-vinoda bale tava sukha sāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness;<span class="e2"> lāgi’</span>–for (the sake of); <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–something; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">kari</span>–I do; <span class="e2">āra</span>–more; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">bale</span>–declares; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">sāra</span>–the essence. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> I no longer endeavour for my own happiness. Bhakti Vinod understands, “Your satisfaction is the essence.”
(১৪)
(14)
বস্তুতঃ সকলি তব, জীব কেহ নয় ।<br />‘অহং’-‘মম’-ভ্রমে ভ্রমি’ ভোগে শোক-ভয় ॥১॥
vastutaḥ sakali tava, jīva keha naya<br />‘ahaṁ’-‘mama’-bhrame bhrami’ bhoge śoka-bhaya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vastutaḥ</span>–actually; <span class="e2">sakali</span>–everything; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Yours; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–the individual soul; <span class="e2">keha</span>–someone; <span class="e2">naya</span>–is not; ‘<span class="e2">aham’</span>–‘I’; ‘<span class="e2">mama’</span>–<span class="e2">‘m</span>ine’; <span class="e2">bhrame</span>–mistaken by; <span class="e2">bhrami’</span>–wandering; <span class="e2">bhoge</span>–experiences; <span class="e2">śoka</span>–lamentation; <span class="e2">bhaya</span>–fear. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> In reality, everything is Yours; nothing belongs to the soul. However, wandering (throughout material existence), bewildered by misconceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’, the soul laments and fears.
‘অহং’-‘মম’ অভিমান এই মাত্র ধন ।<br />বদ্ধ জীব নিজ বলি’ জানে মনে মন ॥২॥
‘ahaṁ’-‘mama’ abhimāna ei mātra dhana<br />baddha-jīva nija bali’ jāne mane mana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">‘aham’</span>–‘I’; ‘<span class="e2">mama’</span>–‘mine’; <span class="e2">abhimāna</span>–misconceptions; <span class="e2">ei</span>–these; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–wealth; <span class="e2">baddha</span>–bound; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–individual souls; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">bali’</span>–considering; <span class="e2">jāne</span>–knows; <span class="e2">mane</span>–in their mind; <span class="e2">mana</span>–mind. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> Deep within, the conditioned soul considers his misconceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ to be his only wealth.
সেই অভিমানে আমি সংসারে পড়িয়া ।<br />হাবুডুবু খাই ভবসিন্ধু সাঁতারিয়া ॥৩॥
sei abhimāne āmi saṁsāre paḍiyā<br />hābuḍubu khāi bhava-sindhu sā̐tāriyā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sei</span>–this;<span class="e2"> abhimāne</span>–by the conception; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the material world; <span class="e2">paḍiyā</span>–falling; <span class="e2">hābuḍubu</span>–bobbing up and down; <span class="e2">khāi</span>–I experience; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–of mundanity, repeated birth and death; <span class="e2">sindhu</span>–the ocean; <span class="e2">sā̐tariyā</span>–swimming. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Having fallen into this world due to such misconception, I flounder as I try to swim within this ocean of material existence.
তোমার অভয় পদে লইয়া শরণ ।<br />আজি আমি করিলাম আত্মনিবেদন ॥৪॥
tomāra abhaya pade laiyā śaraṇa<br />āji āmi karilāma ātma-nivedana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">abhaya</span>–fearless; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">laiyā</span>–taking; <span class="e2">śaraṇa</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">āji</span>–today; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">karilāma</span>–did; <span class="e2">ātma</span>–self; <span class="e2">nivedana</span>–submission. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Taking shelter at Your feet, which are the abode of fearlessness, I have submitted myself unto You today.
‘অহং’-‘মম’ অভিমান ছাড়িল আমায় ।<br />আর যেন মম হৃদে স্থান নাহি পায় ॥৫॥<br />এইমাত্র বল প্রভু! দিবে হে আমারে ।<br />অহংতা-মমতা দূরে পারি রাখিবারে ॥৬॥
‘ahaṁ’-‘mama’ abhimāna chhāḍila āmāya<br />āra yena mama hṛde sthāna nāhi pāya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />ei mātra bala prabhu! dibe he āmāre<br />ahaṁtā-mamatā dūre pāri rākhibāre <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">‘aham’</span>–‘I’; ‘<span class="e2">mama’</span>–‘mine’; <span class="e2">abhimāna</span>–conceptions; <span class="e2">chhāḍila</span>–abandoned; <span class="e2">āmāya</span>–to me; <span class="e2">āra</span>–again; <span class="e2">yena</span>–so that;<span class="e2"> mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">hṛde</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">sthāna</span>–place; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">pāya</span>–obtain; <span class="e2">ei</span>–this; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">bala (śakti)</span>–strength (ability); <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">dibe</span>–will give; <span class="e2">he</span>–oh; <span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">ahaṁtā</span>–false egotism, ‘I’; <span class="e2">mamatā</span>–possessiveness, ‘mine’; <span class="e2">dūre</span>–far away; <span class="e2">pāri</span>–I am able; <span class="e2">rākhibāre</span>–to keep. [<span class="e24">5</span>–<span class="e24">6</span>]
(5–6<span class="e14">)</span> Those misconceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ have now left me. O Lord! So that they will never attain a place within my heart again, please give me just this one ability: that I may be able to keep all false egotism and possessiveness far away.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span>–<span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> vastutaḥ sakali tava … sthāna nāhi pāya: </span>“Everything is Yours … (may) the misconceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ never attain a place within my heart again.” The principle underlying this prayer to surrender oneself to the Lord is expressed in the <span class="e3">Padma-purāṇa</span> and cited in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam</span>:
ahaṅkṛtir ma-kāraḥ syān na-kāras tan niṣedhakaḥ<br />tasmāt tu namasā kṣetri-svātantryaṁ pratiṣidhyate<br />bhagavat-paratantro ’sau tadāyatātma-jīvanaḥ<br />tasmāt sva-sāmarthya-vidhiṁ tyajet sarvam aśeṣataḥ
“In the word <span class="e3">namaḥ </span>(‘obeisance’), the syllable <span class="e3">ma</span> indicates the self-asserting ego (<span class="e3">ahaṅkār</span>, lit. ‘I am the doer’), and the syllable <span class="e3">na</span> indicates its prevention. Thus, the act of offering obeisance (namaḥ) nullifies the offerer’s independence. The soul is by nature subordinate to the Supreme Lord; the soul’s innate function is servitude to Him. Therefore, all actions performed with the conception, ‘I am the doer’, should be utterly abandoned.”
আত্মনিবেদন-ভাব হৃদে দৃঢ় রয় ।<br />হস্তিস্নান সম যেন ক্ষণিক না হয় ॥৭॥
ātma-nivedana-bhāva hṛde dṛḍha raya<br />hasti-snāna sama yena kṣaṇika nā haya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ātma</span>–self; <span class="e2">nivedana</span>–submission; <span class="e2">bhāva</span>–mood; <span class="e2">hṛde</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">dṛḍha</span>–firm; <span class="e2">raya</span>–stays; <span class="e2">hasti</span>–elephant; <span class="e2">snāna</span>–bath; <span class="e2">sama</span>–same;<span class="e2"> yena</span>–like; <span class="e2">kṣaṇika (sāmayika mātra)</span>–momentarily (only temporarily); <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">haya</span>–be. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> May the mood of self-submission remain steadfast within my heart. May it not remain only momentarily, like the cleanliness of an elephant.
ভকতিবিনোদ প্রভু নিত্যনন্দ-পায় ।<br />মাগে পরসাদ, যাহে অভিমান যায় ॥৮॥
bhakati-vinoda prabhu nityānanda-pāya<br />māge parasāda, yāhe abhimāna yāya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">prabhu</span>–Lord; <span class="e2">nityānanda</span>–Nityānanda; <span class="e2">pāya</span>–feet; <span class="e2">māge</span>–begs; <span class="e2">parasāda</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">yāhe</span>–by which; <span class="e2">abhimāna</span>–misconceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’; <span class="e2">yāya</span>–go. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> At Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu’s feet, Bhakti Vinod prays for the mercy by which the misconceptions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ are dispelled forever.
<span class="e2">(8) nityānanda pāya: </span>“At Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu’s feet.” By the mercy of Śrī Guru, who is non-different from Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, all misconception (self-establishing ego) is destroyed and servitude to the Vaiṣṇavas is realised.
(১৫)
(15)
নিবেদন করি প্রভু! তোমার চরণে ।<br />পতিত অধম আমি, জানে ত্রিভুবনে ॥১॥
nivedana kari prabhu! tomāra charaṇe<br />patita adhama āmi jāne tribhuvane <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nivedana</span>–submission; <span class="e2">kari</span>–I do; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> charaṇe</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">patita</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">adhama</span>–low; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">jāne</span>–know; <span class="e2">tribhuvane</span>–in the three worlds. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! I submit myself at Your feet. It is known throughout the three worlds that I am fallen and lowly.
আমা-সম পাপী নাই জগৎ-ভিতরে ।<br />মম-সম অপরাধী নাহিক সংসারে ॥২॥
āmā-sama pāpī nāhi jagat-bhitare<br />mama-sama aparādhī nāhika saṁsāre <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āmā</span>–like me; <span class="e2">sama</span>–equal; <span class="e2">pāpī</span>–sinner; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–is not; <span class="e2">jagat</span>–the world; <span class="e2">bhitare</span>–within; <span class="e2">mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">sama</span>–equal; <span class="e2">aparādhī</span>–offender; <span class="e2">nāhika</span>–is not; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the world. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> There is no sinner within this world so sinful as I. There is no offender within this material world so offensive as I.
সেই সব পাপ আর অপরাধ আমি ।<br />পরিহারে পাই লজ্জা, সব জান তুমি ॥৩॥
sei saba pāpa āra aparādha āmi<br />parihāre pāi lajjā, saba jāna tumi <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sei</span>–these; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">pāpa</span>–sins; <span class="e2">āra</span>–and; <span class="e2">aparādha</span>–offences; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">parihāre (kṣamāpane)</span>–in giving up (in begging forgiveness); <span class="e2">pāi</span>–I feel; <span class="e2">lajjā</span>–shame; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">jāna</span>–know; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> I feel ashamed to beg for forgiveness for all my sins and offences. You know all of this.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> parihāre pāi lajjā:</span> “I feel ashamed to beg for forgiveness.” This sentiment is described in the <span class="e3">Padma-purāṇa </span>(and was expressed by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu and Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu when they surrendered unto Śrīman Mahāprabhu):
mat-tulyo nāsti pāpātmā nāparādhī cha kaśchana<br />parihāre ’pi lajjā me kiṁ bruve puruṣottama
“There is no sinner so sinful as I. There is no offender so offensive as I. O Supreme Lord, I am ashamed to pray for forgiveness for all of my sins and offences (and all the more ashamed of my attempts to abandon them). What more can I say than this?”
তুমি বিনা কা’র আমি লইব শরণ ?<br />তুমি সর্ব্বেশ্বরেশ্বর, ব্রজেন্দ্রনন্দন ॥৪॥
tumi vinā kā’ra āmi la-iba śaraṇa?<br />tumi sarveśvareśvara, vrajendra-nandana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">vinā</span>–without; <span class="e2">kā’ra</span>–of whom?; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">la-iba</span>–will take; <span class="e2">śaraṇa</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–of all;<span class="e2"> īśvara</span>–Lords; <span class="e2">īśvara</span>–the Lord; <span class="e2">vraja</span>–of Vṛndāvan; <span class="e2">indra</span>–of the king; <span class="e2">nandana</span>–darling son, Kṛṣṇa. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Yet of whom shall I take shelter other than You? You are the Lord of all Lords, Vrajendra Nandan.
জগৎ তোমার নাথ! তুমি সর্ব্বময় ।<br />তোমা প্রতি অপরাধ তুমি কর ক্ষয় ॥৫॥
jagata tomāra nātha! tumi sarva-maya<br />tomā prati aparādha tumi kara kṣaya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jagata</span>–universe; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–everything; <span class="e2">maya</span>–consisting of; <span class="e2">tomā</span>–of You; <span class="e2">prati</span>–towards; <span class="e2">aparādha</span>–offences; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">kara</span>–do; <span class="e2">kṣaya</span>–destroy. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> The world is Yours, O Lord! You are present everywhere, and You destroy all offences committed against You.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> jagata tomāra nātha … tumi kara kṣaya:</span> “The world is Yours, O Lord! … You destroy all offences committed against You.”
tasmin tuṣṭe jagat tuṣṭaṁ prīṇite prīṇitaṁ jagat
“By satisfying the Supreme Lord, the whole world becomes satisfied. By pleasing the Supreme Lord, the whole world becomes pleased.”
তুমি ত’ স্খলিতপদ জনের আশ্রয় ।<br />তুমি বিনা আর কিবা আছে দয়াময় ॥৬॥
tumi ta’ skhalita-pada janera āśraya<br />tumi vinā āra kibā āchhe dayā-maya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">skhalita</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">janera</span>–of the people; <span class="e2">āśraya</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">vinā</span>–without; <span class="e2">āra</span>–else; <span class="e2">kibā</span>–what; <span class="e2">āchhe</span>–there is; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">maya</span>–full of. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> You alone are the shelter of those who have fallen. What else is there besides You, O merciful Lord?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">6</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> tumi ta’ skhalita-pada … dayā-maya: </span>“O merciful Lord, You are the sole shelter of those who have fallen.” This conception is expressed in the <span class="e3">Skanda-purāṇa</span>:
bhūmau skhalita-pādānāṁ bhūmir evāvalambanam<br />tvayi jātāparādhānāṁ tvam eva śaraṇaṁ prabho
“O Lord! As the ground is the only support for those who have fallen upon it, so You are the only refuge for those who have offended You.”
সেইরূপ তব অপরাধী জন যত ।<br />তোমার শরণাগত হইবে সতত ॥৭॥
sei-rūpa tava aparādhī jana yata<br />tomāra śaraṇāgata ha-ibe satata <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sei</span>–that; <span class="e2">rūpa</span>–form; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">aparādhī</span>–offensive; <span class="e2">jana</span>–persons; <span class="e2">yata</span>–all (whom); <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">śaraṇāgata</span>–coming to the shelter; <span class="e2">ha-ibe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">satata</span>–always. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> In this way, everyone who has been offensive towards You will eventually come to Your shelter.
ভকতিবিনোদ এবে লইয়া শরণ ।<br />তুয়া পদে করে আজ আত্মসমর্পণ ॥৮॥
bhakati-vinoda ebe la-iyā śaraṇa<br />tuyā pade kare āja ātma-samarpaṇa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">ebe</span>–now; <span class="e2">la-iyā</span>–taking; <span class="e2">śaraṇa</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">kare</span>–does; <span class="e2">āja</span>–today; <span class="e2">ātma</span>–self; <span class="e2">samarpaṇa</span>–full offering. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> Now taking shelter, Bhakti Vinod today fully offers himself at Your feet.
(১৬)
(16)
আত্মনিবেদন,<span class="e25">	তুয়া পদে করি’,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হইনু পরম সুখী ।<br /></span>দুঃখ দূরে গেল,<span class="e25">	ছিন্তা না রহিল,<br /></span><span class="e26">	চৌদিকে আনন্দ দেখি ॥১॥</span>
ātma-nivedana,<span class="e10">	tuyā pade kari’,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ha-inu parama sukhī<br /></span>duḥkha dūre gela,<span class="e10">	chintā nā rahila,<br /></span><span class="e11">	chaudike ānanda dekhi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ātma</span>–self; <span class="e2">nivedana</span>–submission;<span class="e2"> tuyā</span>–Your;<span class="e2"> pade</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>–I became; <span class="e2">parama</span>–supremely; <span class="e2">sukhī</span>–happy; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress; <span class="e2">dūre</span>–far away; <span class="e2">gela</span>–went; <span class="e2">chintā</span>–thought, anxiety; <span class="e2">nā</span>–did not; <span class="e2">rahila</span>–remained; <span class="e2">chaudike</span>–in the four directions; <span class="e2">ānanda</span>–ecstasy; <span class="e2">dekhi</span>–I see. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> By surrendering myself at Your feet, I have become supremely happy. All my distress has gone away, I have no more anxiety, and I see ecstasy in all directions.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> chaudike ānanda dekhi: </span>“I see ecstasy in all directions.” This state of surrender is described by Kṛṣṇa in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(11.14.13):
mayā santuṣṭa-manasaḥ sarvāḥ sukha-mayā diśaḥ
“All directions are filled with happiness for one whose heart is completely satisfied by Me.”
অশোক-অভয়,<span class="e25">	অমৃত-আধার,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তোমার চরণদ্বয় ।<br /></span>তাহাতে এখন,<span class="e25">	বিশ্রাম লভিয়া<br /></span><span class="e26">	ছাড়িনু ভবের ভয় ॥২॥</span>
aśoka-abhaya,<span class="e10">	amṛta-ādhāra,<br /></span><span class="e11">	tomāra charaṇa-dvaya<br /></span>tāhāte ekhana,<span class="e10">	viśrāma labhiyā<br /></span><span class="e11">	chhāḍinu bhavera bhaya </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">aśoka</span>–of sorrowlessness; <span class="e2">abhaya</span>–of fearlessness; <span class="e2">amṛta</span>–of immortality; <span class="e2">ādhāra</span>–reservoir; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">dvaya</span>–two; <span class="e2">tāhāte</span>–in them; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">viśrāma</span>–rest; <span class="e2">labhiyā</span>–obtaining; <span class="e2">chhāḍinu</span>–I abandoned; <span class="e2">bhavera</span>–of material existence, cyclic birth and death;<span class="e2"> bhaya</span>–fear. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> Your feet are the abode of sorrowlessness, fearlessness, and immortality. Receiving shelter beneath them, I have abandoned all fear of material existence.
তোমার সংসারে,<span class="e25">	করিব সেবন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নহিব ফলের ভাগী ।<br /></span>তব সুখ যাহে,<span class="e25">	করিব যতন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হ’য়ে পদে অনুরাগী ॥৩॥</span>
tomāra saṁsāre,<span class="e10">	kariba sevana,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nahiba phalera bhāgī<br /></span>tava sukha yāhe,<span class="e10">	kariba yatana,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ha’ye pade anurāgī </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the household; <span class="e2">kariba</span>–I will do; <span class="e2">sevana</span>–service; <span class="e2">nahiba</span>–I will not become; <span class="e2">phalera</span>–of the fruits; <span class="e2">bhāgī</span>–shareholder; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">yāhe</span>–by which; <span class="e2">kariba</span>–I will do; <span class="e2">yatana</span>–careful endeavour; <span class="e2">ha’ye</span>–being; <span class="e2">pade</span>–to Your feet; <span class="e2">anurāgī</span>–deeply, lovingly attached. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> I will render service in Your household and will not become an enjoyer of the results. Lovingly attached to Your feet, I will carefully endeavour for whatever pleases You.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">tomāra saṁsāre, kariba sevana, nāhiba phalera bhāgī: </span>“I will render service in Your household and will not become an enjoyer of the results.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā</span> (2.47), Śrī Kṛṣṇa describes the soul’s position:
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadāchana<br />mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stv akarmaṇi
“Your right is to engage in My service, not to enjoy the results. So engage in My service without being motivated by any desire to enjoy the results, and never become inclined to abandon My service.”
তোমার সেবায়,<span class="e25">	দুঃখ হয় যত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	সেও ত’ পরম সুখ ।<br /></span>সেবা-সুখ-দুঃখ,<span class="e25">	পরম সম্পদ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নাশয়ে অবিদ্যা-দুঃখ ॥৪॥</span>
tomāra sevāya,<span class="e10">	duḥkha haya yata,<br /></span><span class="e11">	seo ta’ parama sukha<br /></span>sevā-sukha-duḥkha,<span class="e10">	parama sampada,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nāśaye avidyā-duḥkha </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sevāya</span>–in service; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress; <span class="e2">haya</span>–happens;<span class="e2"> yata</span>–all; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">o</span>–also; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">parama</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">sevā</span>–service; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–and distress; <span class="e2">parama</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">sampada</span>–fortune; <span class="e2">nāśaye</span>–destroy; <span class="e2">avidyā</span>–of ignorance; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> All the distress I encounter in Your service is also my greatest happiness. Both the distress and the happiness that come from engagement in Your service are my greatest fortune; they both destroy the distress of ignorance.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> sevā-sukha-duḥkha … nāśaye avidyā-duḥkha: </span>“Both the distress and the happiness that come from engagement in Your service … destroy the distress of ignorance.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(7.14), Śrī Kṛṣṇa explains that only those who unconditionally surrender unto Him are liberated from māyā:
daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā<br />mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṁ taranti te
“My alluring, trimodal māyā is insurmountable. Only those who surrender unto Me can transcend māyā.”
[Translator’s note: In <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-bhāgavat</span>, Madhya-khaṇḍa, 9.240, Śrīla Vṛndāvan Dās Ṭhākur comments:
yata dekha vaiṣṇavera vyavahāra duḥkha<br />niśchaya jāniha sei parānanda sukha
“You should know for certain that a devotee’s apparent distress is actually their ecstatic spiritual happiness.”]
পূর্ব্ব ইতিহাস,<span class="e25">	ভুলিনু সকল,<br /></span><span class="e26">	সেবা-সুখ পেয়ে মনে ।<br /></span>আমি ত’ তোমার,<span class="e25">	তুমি ত’ আমার,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কি কাজ অপর ধনে ॥৫॥</span>
pūrva itihāsa,<span class="e10">	bhulinu sakala,<br /></span><span class="e11">	sevā-sukha peye mane<br /></span>āmi ta’ tomāra,<span class="e10">	tumi ta’ āmāra,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ki kāja apara dhane </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">pūrva</span>–previous; <span class="e2">itihāsa</span>–history; <span class="e2">bhulinu</span>–I forgot; <span class="e2">sakala</span>–all; <span class="e2">sevā</span>–service; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">peye</span>–obtaining; <span class="e2">mane</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Yours; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–mine; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what; <span class="e2">kāja</span>–necessity; <span class="e2">apara</span>–any other; <span class="e2">dhane</span>–for wealth. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Feeling the happiness of Your service in my heart, I have completely forgotten all past history. I am Yours, and You are mine. What need is there for any other wealth?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> pūrva itihāsa:</span> “All past history.” This refers to one’s behaviour prior to the beginning of their life as a devotee. In <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta </span>(Antya-līlā, 6.236), Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu forbids His followers from continuing to behave like common people after taking up the practice of devotion:
grāmya-kathā nā śunibe, grāmya-vārtā nā kahibe
“Do not listen to mundane talks or speak of mundane news.”
Moreover, <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta </span>(Antya-līlā, 13.132) cites the absence of the tendency to discuss worldly subjects as a prominent attri­bute of a great devotee:
grāmya-vārtā nā śune, nā kahe jihvāya<br />kṛṣṇa-kathā-pūjādite aṣṭa-prahara yāya
“He never listens to mundane news, and never speaks about it either. He passes every day engaged in discussion, worship, and other services to Kṛṣṇa.”
In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (11.29.34), Kṛṣṇa describes to Uddhava the transformation of a surrendering soul:
martyo yadā tyakta-samasta-karmā<br />niveditātmā vichikīrṣito me<br />tadāmṛtatvaṁ pratipadyamāno<br />mayātma-bhūyāya cha kalpate vai
“When a mortal being completely abandons all mundane endeavours, surrenders himself unto Me, and acts according to My desires, he attains immortality and becomes fit to associate with Me.”
ভকতিবিনোদ,<span class="e25">	আনন্দে ডুবিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তোমার সেবার তরে ।<br /></span>সব ছেষ্টা করে,<span class="e25">	তব ইচ্ছা মত,<br /></span><span class="e26">	থাকিয়া তোমার ঘরে ॥৬॥</span>
bhakati-vinoda,<span class="e10">	ānande ḍubiyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	tomāra sevāra tare<br /></span>saba cheṣṭā kare,<span class="e10">	tava ichchhā mata,<br /></span><span class="e11">	thākiyā tomāra ghare </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">ānande</span>–in ecstasy; <span class="e2">ḍubiyā</span>–plunging;<span class="e2"> tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sevāra</span>–of service; <span class="e2">tare</span>–on account of; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">cheṣṭā</span>–endeavours; <span class="e2">kare</span>–does; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">mata</span>–according to; <span class="e2">thākiyā</span>–staying; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ghare</span>–in the house. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> Diving in the ecstasy of Your service, Bhakti Vinod performs all his endeavours in accordance with Your will, residing within Your home.

গোপ্তৃত্বে বরণ
<span class="e2">Goptṛtve Varaṇa:</span> <br />Embracing the Lord’s Guardianship
(১৭)
(17)
কি জানি কি বলে,<span class="e25">	তোমার ধামেতে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হইনু শরণাগত ।<br /></span>তুমি দয়াময়,<span class="e25">	পতিতপাবন,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পতিত তারণে রত ॥১॥</span>
ki jāni ki bale,<span class="e10">	tomāra dhāmete,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ha-inu śaraṇāgata<br /></span>tumi dayā-maya,<span class="e10">	patita-pāvana,<br /></span><span class="e11">	patita-tāraṇe rata </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ki</span>–what?; <span class="e2">jāni</span>–I know; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what; <span class="e2">bale</span>–by force; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dhāmete</span>–in the abode; <span class="e2">ha-inu</span>–I became; <span class="e2">śaraṇāgata</span>–surrendered; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">maya</span>–full of; <span class="e2">patita</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">pāvana</span>–saviour;<span class="e2"> patita</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">tāraṇe</span>–in delivering; <span class="e2">rata</span>–ever engaged. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I do not know by what force I have taken shelter within Your abode. You are the merciful saviour of the fallen, who is ever engaged in delivering them.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> ki jāni ki bale: </span>“I do not know by what force …” Kṛṣṇa explains to Uddhava in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(11.20.8):
yadṛchchhayā mat-kathādau jāta-śraddhas tu yaḥ pumān<br />na nirviṇṇo nāti-sakto bhakti-yogo ’sya siddhi-daḥ
“One who is neither excessively averse nor excessively attached (to mundane existence) and who, by some good fortune, develops faith in narrations about Me—his practice of bhakti-yoga results in perfection.”
ভরসা আমার,<span class="e25">	এই মাত্র নাথ!<br /></span><span class="e26">	তুমি ত’ করুণাময় ।<br /></span>তব দয়া পাত্র,<span class="e25">	নাহি মোর সম,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অবশ্য ঘুচাবে ভয় ॥২॥</span>
bharasā āmāra,<span class="e10">	ei mātra nātha!<br /></span><span class="e11">	tumi ta’ karuṇ</span><span class="e11">ā-maya<br /></span>tava dayā-pātra,<span class="e10">	nāhi mora sama,<br /></span><span class="e11">	avaśya ghuchābe bhaya </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bharasā</span>–hope; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">ei</span>–this; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">karuṇā</span>–mercy;<span class="e2"> maya</span>–full of; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">pātra</span>–recipient; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–there is not; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">sama</span>–equal; <span class="e2">avaśya</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">ghuchābe</span>–will dispel; <span class="e2">bhaya</span>–fear. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! You are merciful. This is my sole hope. There is no candidate for Your mercy like me; certainly You will dispel all my fear.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">tava dayā-pātra:</span> “Candidate for Your mercy.” In his <span class="e3">Śrī Stotra-ratna</span> (47), Śrī Yāmun Āchārya prays:
na mṛṣā paramārtham eva me<br />śṛṇu vijñāpanam ekam agrataḥ<br />yadi me na dayiṣyase tadā<br />dayanīyas tava nātha durlabhaḥ
“O Lord, please listen as I make before You this one petition, which is not false, but utterly sincere: if You do not bestow Your mercy upon me, it will be extremely difficult for You to find a more befitting recipient of Your mercy.”
আমারে তারিতে,<span class="e25">	কাহারো শকতি,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অবনী ভিতরে নাহি ।<br /></span>দয়াল ঠাকুর!<span class="e25">	ঘোষনা তোমার,<br /></span><span class="e26">	অধম পামরে ত্রাহি ॥৩॥</span>
āmāre tārite,<span class="e10">	kāhāro śakati,<br /></span><span class="e11">	avanī-bhitare nāhi<br /></span>dayāla ṭhākura!<span class="e10">	ghoṣanā tomāra,<br /></span><span class="e11">	adhama pāmare trāhi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">tārite</span>–to deliver; <span class="e2">kāhāro</span>–someone; <span class="e2">śakati</span>–power; <span class="e2">avanī</span>–Earth; <span class="e2">bhitare</span>–upon; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–there is not; <span class="e2">dayāla</span>–merciful; <span class="e2">ṭhākura</span>–Lord; <span class="e2">ghoṣaṇā</span>–declaration; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">adhama</span>–low; <span class="e2">pāmare</span>–to the sinners; <span class="e2">trāhi (trāṇa kara)</span>–You deliver. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> There is no one on Earth who has the power to deliver me. O merciful Lord! It is Your declaration that You deliver the lowest, most sinful persons.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> ghoṣanā tomāra: </span>“Your declaration.” This is described in <span class="e3">Śrī Chaitanya-charitāmṛta </span>(Antya-līlā, 4.68), wherein Śrīman Mahāprabhu says to Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu:
dīnere adhika dayā kare bhagavān
“The Supreme Lord bestows greater mercy upon the destitute.”
সকল ছাড়িয়া,<span class="e25">	আসিয়াছি আমি,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তোমার চরণে নাথ!<br /></span>আমি নিত্যদাস,<span class="e25">	তুমি পালয়িতা,<br /></span><span class="e26">	তুমি গোপ্তা, জগন্নাথ! ॥৪॥</span>
sakala chhāḍiyā,<span class="e10">	āsiyāchhi āmi,<br /></span><span class="e11">	tomāra charaṇe nātha!<br /></span>āmi nitya-dāsa,<span class="e10">	tumi pālayitā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	tumi goptā, jagannātha! </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sakala</span>–everything; <span class="e2">chhāḍiyā</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">asiyāchhi</span>–have come; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servant; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">pālayitā</span>–maintainer; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">goptā (pālana-kartā)</span>–protector; <span class="e2">jagannātha!</span>–O Lord of the universe! [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Abandoning everything, I have come to Your feet, O Lord! I am Your eternal servant, and You are my maintainer and protector, O Lord of the universe!
তোমার সকল,<span class="e25">	আমি মাত্র দাস,<br /></span><span class="e26">	আমারে তারিবে তুমি ।<br /></span>তোমার চরণ,<span class="e25">	করিনু বরণ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	আমার নাহি ত’ আমি ॥৫॥</span>
tomāra sakala,<span class="e10">	āmi mātra dāsa,<br /></span><span class="e11">	āmāre tāribe tumi<br /></span>tomāra charaṇa,<span class="e10">	karinu varaṇa,<br /></span><span class="e11">	āmāra nāhi ta’ āmi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Yours; <span class="e2">sakala</span>–everything; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–a servant; <span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">tāribe</span>–will deliver; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">karinu</span>–I did; <span class="e2">varaṇa (avalambana-rūpe grahaṇa)</span>–embrace (accept as my support); <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–mine; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Everything is Yours. I am only a servant. Certainly You will deliver me. I have embraced Your feet and no longer belong to myself.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> āmāra nāhi ta’ āmi:</span> “I no longer belong to myself.” The result of this type of wholesale surrender is described by Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(11.29.34):
mayātma-bhūyāya cha kalpate vai
“The surrendered soul becomes fit to associate with Me (he awakens to his divine form like My own).”
ভকতিবিনোদ,<span class="e25">	কাঁদিয়া শরণ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	ল’য়েছে তোমার পায় ।<br /></span>ক্ষমি’ অপরাধ,<span class="e25">	নামে রুচি দিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পালন করহে তায় ॥৬॥</span>
bhakati-vinoda,<span class="e10">	kā̐diyā śaraṇa,<br /></span><span class="e11">	la’yechhe tomāra pāya<br /></span>kṣami’ aparādha,<span class="e10">	nāme ruchi diyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	pālana karahe tāya </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kā̐diyā</span>–crying; <span class="e2">śaraṇa</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">la’yechhe</span>–has taken; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pāya</span>–feet; <span class="e2">kṣami’</span>–forgiving; <span class="e2">aparādha</span>–offences; <span class="e2">nāme</span>–for Your Name; <span class="e2">ruchi (anurāga)</span>–taste (deep loving attachment); <span class="e2">diyā</span>–giving; <span class="e2">pālana</span>–protection; <span class="e2">karahe</span>–please do; <span class="e2">tāya</span>–him. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> Crying, Bhakti Vinod has taken shelter at Your feet. Forgiving his offences and granting him taste for Your Name, please maintain him.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">6</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> kṣami’ aparādha … pālana karahe tāya: </span>“Forgiving his offen­ces … please maintain him.” Forgiving their offences and granting them taste for the Name<span class="e3"> is</span> the Lord’s maintenance of His devotees.
(১৮)
(18)
দারা, পুত্র, নিজদেহ, কুটুম্ব পালনে ।<br />সর্ব্বদা ব্যাকুল আমি ছিনু মনে মনে ॥১॥
dārā, putra, nija-deha, kuṭumba pālane<br />sarvadā vyākula āmi chhinu mane mane <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dārā</span>–wife; <span class="e2">putra</span>–children; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">deha</span>–body; <span class="e2">kuṭumba</span>–relatives; <span class="e2">pālane</span>–in the maintenance of; <span class="e2">sarvadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">vyākula</span>–anxious; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">chhinu</span>–was; <span class="e2">mane</span>–in mind; <span class="e2">mane</span>–in mind. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> Deep within, I was always anxious about the maintenance of my wife, children, body, and relatives.
কেমনে অর্জ্জিব অর্থ যশ কিসে পাব ।<br />কন্যা-পুত্র-বিবাহ কেমনে সম্পাদিব ॥২॥
kemane arjiba artha yaśa kise pāba<br />kanyā-putra-vivāha kemane sampādiba <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kemane</span>–how?; <span class="e2">arjibaḥ</span>–I will earn; <span class="e2">artha</span>–money; <span class="e2">yaśa</span>–fame; <span class="e2">kise</span>–by what means?; <span class="e2">pāba</span>–I will attain; <span class="e2">kanyā</span>–of daughters; <span class="e2">putra</span>–of sons; <span class="e2">vivāha</span>–marriage; <span class="e2">kemane</span>–how?; <span class="e2">sampādiba</span>–I will arrange. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> “How shall I earn money? How shall I attain fame? How will I arrange the marriages of my sons and daughters?”
এবে আত্মসমর্পণে চিন্তা নাহি আর ।<br />তুমি নির্ব্বাহিবে প্রভো! সংসার তোমার ॥৩॥
ebe ātma-samarpaṇe chintā nāhi āra<br />tumi nirvāhibe prabho! saṁsāra tomāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ebe</span>–now; <span class="e2">ātma</span>–myself; <span class="e2">samarpaṇe</span>–by fully offering; <span class="e2">chintā</span>–anxiety; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">āra</span>–any more; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">nirvāhibe</span>–will maintain; <span class="e2">prabho!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–household; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Yours. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Now that I have fully offered myself, I have no more anxiety. You will maintain Your household, O Lord!
তুমি ত’ পালিবে মোরে নিজ-দাস জানি’ ।<br />তোমার সেবায় প্রভু! বড় সুখ মানি ॥৪॥
tumi ta’ pālibe more nija-dāsa jāni’<br />tomāra sevāya prabhu! baḍa sukha māni <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">pālibe</span>–will protect; <span class="e2">more</span>–me; <span class="e2">nija</span>–Your own; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servant; <span class="e2">jāni’</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sevāya</span>–in the service; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">baḍa</span>–great; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">māni</span>–I find. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> You will certainly maintain me, knowing me to be Your servant. O Lord! In Your service I feel the greatest joy.
তোমার ইচ্ছায় প্রভু, সব কার্য্য হয় ।<br />জীব বলে—‘করি আমি’, সে ত’ সত্য নয় ॥৫॥
tomāra ichchhāya prabhu, saba kārya haya<br />jīva bale—‘kari āmi’, se ta’ satya naya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhāya</span>–by the desire; <span class="e2">prabhu</span>–O Lord; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">kārya</span>–activity; <span class="e2">haya</span>–happens; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–the conditioned souls; <span class="e2">bale</span>–consider; <span class="e2">kari</span>–do; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">satya</span>–truth; <span class="e2">naya</span>–is not. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> All activity happens according to Your will, O Lord, yet souls think, “I do”. This is not at all true.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> jīva bale—‘kari āmi’, se ta’ satya naya: </span>“Souls think, ‘I do’. This is not at all true.” Kṛṣṇa explains this in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(3.27):
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ<br />ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate
“Actions in the world are effected, in every respect, by the modes of material nature. Yet one deluded by false ego thinks, ‘I am the doer’.”
জীব কি করিতে পারে, তুমি না করিলে ।<br />আশা মাত্র জীব করে, তব ইচ্ছা ফলে ॥৬॥
jīva ki karite pāre, tumi nā karile<br />āśā mātra jīva kare, tava ichchhā phale <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jīva</span>–the soul; <span class="e2">ki</span>–what?; <span class="e2">karite</span>–to act; <span class="e2">pāre</span>–can; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">na</span>–do not; <span class="e2">karile</span>–if act; <span class="e2">āśā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">mātra</span>–only; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–souls; <span class="e2">kare</span>–do; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">phale</span>–manifests. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> What are the souls able to do if You do not act? The souls can only desire. It is Your will alone that comes to pass.
নিশ্ছিন্ত হইয়া আমি সেবিব তোমায় ।<br />গৃহে ভাল মন্দ হ’লে নাহি মোর দায় ॥৭॥
niśchinta ha-iyā āmi seviba tomāya<br />gṛhe bhāla-manda ha’le nāhi mora dāya <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">niśchinta</span>–devoid of anxiety; <span class="e2">ha-iyā</span>–being; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">seviba</span>–will serve; <span class="e2">tomāya</span>–unto You; <span class="e2">gṛhe</span>–in the house; <span class="e2">bhāla</span>–good; <span class="e2">manda</span>–bad; <span class="e2">ha’le</span>–when happens; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not be; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">dāya</span>–responsibility. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> Free from all anxiety, I will serve You. Whatever happens in Your household, be it good or bad, will not be my responsibility.
ভকতিবিনোদ নিজ-স্বাতন্ত্য ত্যজিয়া ।<br />তোমার চরণ সেবে অকিঞ্চন হইয়া ॥৮॥
bhakati-vinoda nija-svātantrya tyajiyā<br />tomāra charaṇa seve akiñchana ha-iyā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">svātantrya</span>–independence; <span class="e2">tyajiyā</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">seve’</span>–serves; <span class="e2">akiñchana</span>–detached; <span class="e2">ha-iyā</span>–being. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> Completely detached, Bhakti Vinod abandons his indepen­dence and serves Your feet.
(১৯)
(19)
সর্ব্বস্ব তোমার,<span class="e25">	চরণে সঁপিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	পড়েছি তোমার ঘরে ।<br /></span>তুমি ত’ ঠাকুর,<span class="e25">	তোমার কুকুর,<br /></span><span class="e26">	বলিয়া জানহ মোরে ॥১॥</span>
sarvasva tomāra,<span class="e10">	charaṇe sa̐piyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	paḍechhi tomāra ghare<br /></span>tumi ta’ ṭhākura,<span class="e10">	tomāra kukkura,<br /></span><span class="e11">	baliyā jānaha more </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sarvasva</span>–everything; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Yours; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet; <span class="e2">sa̐piyā</span>–offering; <span class="e2">paḍechhi</span>–I have fallen; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ghare</span>–in the house; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">ṭhākura</span>–the master; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">kukkura</span>–dog; <span class="e2">baliyā</span>–considering; <span class="e2">jānaha</span>–please know; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I have offered everything at Your feet and taken shelter in Your home. You are my Master. Consider me Your dog.
বাঁধিয়া নিকটে,<span class="e25">	আমারে পালিবে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	রহিব তোমার দ্বারে ।<br /></span>প্রতীপ-জনেরে,<span class="e25">	আসিতে না দিব,<br /></span><span class="e26">	রাখিব গডের পারে ॥২॥</span>
bā̐dhiyā nikaṭe,<span class="e10">	āmāre pālibe,<br /></span><span class="e11">	rahiba tomāra dvāre<br /></span>pratīpa-janere,<span class="e10">	āsite nā diba,<br /></span><span class="e11">	rākhiba gaḍera pāre </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bā̐ndhiyā</span>–tying up; <span class="e2">nikaṭe</span>–nearby; <span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">pālibe</span>–will maintain; <span class="e2">rahiba</span>–will keep; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dvāre</span>–at the door; <span class="e2">pratīpa (pratikūla, guru-vaiṣṇava-dveṣī)</span>–adverse (unfavourable, inimical to the spiritual master and the devotees);<span class="e2"> janere</span>–persons who are; <span class="e2">āsite</span>–to come;<span class="e2"> nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">diba</span>–I will allow; <span class="e2">rākhiba</span>–I will keep; <span class="e2">gaḍera (durgā, parikhā)</span>–of the moat (impassable ditch); <span class="e2">pāre</span>–on the other side. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> You will tie me up nearby and maintain me. I will remain at Your doorstep. I will not allow any inimical persons to enter; I will keep them on the far side of Your moat.
তব নিজ-জন,<span class="e25">	প্রসাদ সেবিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	উচ্ছিষ্ট রাখিবে যাহা ।<br /></span>আমার ভোজন,<span class="e25">	পরম-আনন্দে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	প্রতিদিন হবে তাহা ॥৩॥</span>
tava nija-jana,<span class="e10">	prasāda seviyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	uchchhiṣṭa rākhibe yāhā<br /></span>āmāra bhojana,<span class="e10">	parama-ānande,<br /></span><span class="e11">	prati-dina habe tāhā </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">jana</span>–person; <span class="e2">prasāda (anugraha, ekhāne anugraha pūrvaka pradatta vastu)</span>–the remnants of offerings of food unto You (mercy; in this instance meaning items mercifully bestowed); <span class="e2">seviyā</span>–serving; <span class="e2">uchchhiṣṭa</span>–remnants; <span class="e2">rākhibe</span>–will leave behind; <span class="e2">yāhā</span>–whatever; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">bhojana</span>–eating; <span class="e2">parama</span>–great; <span class="e2">ānande</span>–with joy; <span class="e2">prati</span>–every; <span class="e2">dina</span>–day; <span class="e2">habe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">tāhā</span>–that. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Whatever remnants Your devotees leave behind after honouring Your prasād I will eat every day with great joy.
বসিয়া শুইয়া,<span class="e25">	তোমার চরণ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	চিন্তিব সতত আমি ।<br /></span>নাচিতে নাচিতে,<span class="e25">	নিকটে যাইব,<br /></span><span class="e26">	যখন ডাকিবে তুমি ॥৪॥</span>
basiyā śuiyā,<span class="e10">	tomāra charaṇa,<br /></span><span class="e11">	chintiba satata āmi<br /></span>nāchite nāchite,<span class="e10">	nikaṭe yāiba,<br /></span><span class="e11">	yakhana ḍākibe tumi </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">basiyā</span>–sitting up; <span class="e2">śuiyā</span>–lying down; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">chintiba</span>–will think; <span class="e2">satata</span>–always; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">nāchite</span>–dancing; <span class="e2">nāchite</span>–and dancing; <span class="e2">nikaṭe</span>–nearby; <span class="e2">yāiba</span>–I will go; <span class="e2">yakhana</span>–when; <span class="e2">ḍākibe</span>–will call; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> While sitting up or lying down, I will always think of Your feet. I will come to You whenever You call me, dancing all the way.
নিজের পোষণ,<span class="e25">	কভু না ভাবিব,<br /></span><span class="e26">	রহিব ভাবের ভরে ।<br /></span>ভকতিবিনোদ,<span class="e25">	তোমারে পালক,<br /></span><span class="e26">	বলিয়া বরণ করে ॥৫॥</span>
nijera poṣana,<span class="e10">	kabhu nā bhāviba,<br /></span><span class="e11">	rahiba bhāvera bhare<br /></span>bhakati-vinoda,<span class="e10">	tomāre pālaka,<br /></span><span class="e11">	baliyā varaṇa kare </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nijera</span>–of my own; <span class="e2">poṣaṇa</span>–maintenance, nourishment; <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–ever; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">bhāviba</span>–I will think; <span class="e2">rahiba</span>–I will remain; <span class="e2">bhāvera</span>–of loving attachment; <span class="e2">bhare</span>–in the shelter; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">tomāre</span>–to You; <span class="e2">pālaka</span>–protector; <span class="e2">baliyā</span>–considering; <span class="e2">varaṇa</span>–choose; <span class="e2">kare</span>–does. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> I will never think about my own maintenance; I will always remain within the shelter of loving attachment to You. Bhakti Vinod embraces You as his maintainer.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> nijera poṣana kabhu nā bhāviba: </span>“I will never think about my own maintenance.” This state of surrender is described in<span class="e3"> Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span> (1.2.195):
chintāṁ kuryān na rakṣāyair vikrītasya yathā paśoḥ<br />tathārpayan harau dehaṁ viramedasya rakṣaṇāt
“As one does not worry about the maintenance of a sold animal, so one will not worry about maintaining oneself upon fully offering one’s body unto the Supreme Lord.”
(২০)
(20)
তুমি সর্ব্বেশ্বরেশ্বর, ব্রজেন্দ্রকুমার!<br />তোমার ইচ্ছায় বিশ্বে সৃজন সংহার ॥১॥
tumi sarveśvareśvara, vrajendra-kumāra!<br />tomāra ichchhāya viśve sṛjana saṁhāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">sarveśvareśvara</span>–the Lord of all Lords; <span class="e2">vrajendra</span>–of the king of Vraja; <span class="e2">kumāra</span>–the son, Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhāya</span>–by the will; <span class="e2">viśve</span>–in the universe; <span class="e2">sṛjana</span>–creation; <span class="e2">saṁhāra</span>–annihilation. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> You are the Lord of all Lords, O Vrajendra Kumār! In accor­dance with Your will, creation and annihilation take place within the universe.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">tumi sarveśvareśvara:</span> “You are the Lord of all Lords.” The supreme position and identity of Kṛṣṇa is described throughout the scriptures:
ete chāṁśa-kalāḥ puṁsaḥ kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam<br />indrāri-vyākulaṁ lokaṁ mṛḍayanti yuge yuge
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 1.3.28)
“All these Avatārs are manifestations or partial manifestations of the Puruṣ-avatārs (Kāraṇodakśāyī Viṣṇu, Garbhodakśayī Viṣṇu, and Kṣīrodakśāyī Viṣṇu), but Kṛṣṇa is Svayam Bhagavān, the Supreme Lord Himself. In every age these Avatārs protect the demon-ridden universe.”
sṛjāmi tan-niyukto ’haṁ haro harati tad-vaśaḥ<br />viśvaṁ puruṣa-rūpeṇa paripāti tri-śakti-dhṛk
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 2.6.32)
“In accordance with the order of Śrī Hari, I create the universe and Śiva annihilates it. Śrī Hari, the controller of the three modes of material nature, maintains the universe with His form of Kṣīrodakśāyī Viṣṇu.”
īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sach-chid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ<br />anādir ādir govindaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam
(Śrī Brahma-saṁhitā: 5.1)
“The embodiment of spiritual energy, consciousness, and ecstasy, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is known as Govinda, is the Supreme Lord of all Lords. He has no origin, He is the origin of all, and He is the cause of all causes.”
ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate<br />iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ
(Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā: 10.8)
[Kṛṣṇa Himself explains:] “I am the origin of everything. Everything emanates from Me. Realising this, the wise serve Me, fully imbued with divine love.”
mattaḥ parataraṁ nānyat kiñchid asti dhanañjaya<br />mayi sarvam idaṁ protaṁ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva
(Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā: 7.7)
“O Arjun, there is nothing superior to Me. All that exists is strung upon Me like jewels upon a thread.”
তব ইচ্ছামত ব্রহ্মা করেন সৃজন ।<br />তব ইচ্ছামত বিষ্ণু করেন পালন ॥২॥
tava ichchhā-mata brahmā karena sṛjana<br />tava ichchhā-mata viṣṇu karena pālana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mata</span>–according to; <span class="e2">brahmā</span>–the universal creator; <span class="e2">karena</span>–does; <span class="e2">sṛjana</span>–creation; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mata</span>–according to; <span class="e2">viṣṇu</span>–the maintainer of the material nature; <span class="e2">karena</span>–does; <span class="e2">pālana</span>–maintenance. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> In accordance with Your will, Brahmā creates the universe. In accordance with Your will, Viṣṇu maintains the universe.
তব ইচ্ছামত শিব করেন সংহার ।<br />তব ইচ্ছামতে মায়া সৃজে কারাগার ॥৩॥
tava ichchhā-mata śiva karena saṁhāra<br />tava ichchhā-mate māyā sṛje kārāgāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mata</span>–according to; <span class="e2">śiva</span>–the topmost Vaiṣṇava who serves Kṛṣṇa in a wide variety of ways; <span class="e2">karena</span>–does; <span class="e2">saṁhāra</span>–annihilation; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mate</span>–according to; <span class="e2">māyā</span>–the goddess of illusion; <span class="e2">sṛje</span>–creates; <span class="e2">kārāgāra</span>–prison. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> In accordance with Your will, Śiva annihilates the universe. In accordance with Your will, Māyā Devī creates her prison house.
তব ইচ্ছামত জীবের জনম-মরণ ।<br />সমৃদ্ধি-নিপাত দুঃখ সুখ-সংঘটন ॥৪॥
tava ichchhā-mata jīvera janama-maraṇa<br />samṛddhi-nipāta duḥkha sukha-saṁghaṭana <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mata</span>–according to; <span class="e2">jīvera</span>–of the individual souls; <span class="e2">janama</span>–birth; <span class="e2">maraṇa</span>–death; <span class="e2">samṛddhi (unnati)</span>–increase (prosperity); <span class="e2">nipāta (avanati)</span>–decline (degradation); <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness;<span class="e2"> saṁghaṭana</span>–occurrence. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> In accordance with Your will, the souls take birth and die. In accordance with Your will, they experience prosperity and ruin, happiness and distress.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> samṛddhi-nipāta: </span>“Prosperity and ruin.” The supreme authority of Kṛṣṇa’s will is described as follows:
āpane ichchhāya jīva koṭi vāñchhā kare<br />kṛṣṇa ichchhā hale tāre tabe phala dhare
“According to their will, the souls desire innumerable ends. Yet only if Kṛṣṇa wills it are their desires fulfilled.”
মিছে মায়াবদ্ধ জীব আশাপাশে ফিরে ।<br />তব ইচ্ছা বিনা কিছু করিতে না পারে ॥৫॥
michhe māyā-baddha jīva āśā-pāśe phire<br />tava ichchhā vinā kichhu karite nā pāre <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">michhe</span>–vainly; <span class="e2">māyā</span>–goddess of illusion; <span class="e2">baddha</span>–bound; <span class="e2">jīva</span>–the individual souls; <span class="e2">āśā</span>-<span class="e2">pāśe</span>–all around; <span class="e2">phire</span>–wander; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">vinā</span>–without; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–anything; <span class="e2">karite</span>–to do; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">pāre</span>–able. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Bound by Māyā, the souls vainly wander about. Unless it is Your will, they are not able to do anything.
তুমি ত’ রক্ষক আর পালক আমার ।<br />তোমার চরণ বিনা আশা নাহি আর ॥৬॥
tumi ta’ rakṣaka āra pālaka āmāra<br />tomāra charaṇa vinā āśā nāhi āra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">rakṣaka</span>–the protector; <span class="e2">āra</span>–and; <span class="e2">pālaka</span>–maintainer; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">vinā</span>–apart from; <span class="e2">āśā</span>–hope, desire; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">āra</span>–another. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> You are my protector and maintainer. I aspire for nothing other than Your feet.
নিজবল-ছেষ্টা প্রতি ভরসা ছাড়িয়া ।<br />তোমার ইচ্ছায় আছি নির্ভর করিয়া ॥৭॥
