nija-bala-cheṣṭā prati bharasā chhāḍiyā<br />tomāra ichchhāya āchhi nirbhara kariyā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">bala</span>–strength; <span class="e2">cheṣṭā</span>–endeavours; <span class="e2">prati</span>–upon; <span class="e2">bharasā</span>–reliance; <span class="e2">chhāḍiyā</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhāya</span>–according to will; <span class="e2">āchhi</span>–I am; <span class="e2">nirbhara</span>–dependence; <span class="e2">kariyā</span>–doing. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> Abandoning reliance on my own strength and endeavour, I depend upon Your will.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">7</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> nija-bala-cheṣṭā … nirbhara kariyā: </span>“Abandoning reliance upon my own strength and endeavour.” Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur also sings about this in his <span class="e3">Kalyāṇa-kalpa-taru </span>(3.3.3):
	gopīnātha, hāra ye menechhi āmi<br />(āmāra) aneka yatana,	ha-ila biphala,<br />	ekhana bharasā tumi
“O Gopīnāth, I have accepted defeat. All of my endeavours were useless. I now rely upon You.”
ভকতিবিনোদ অতি দীন অকিঞ্চন ।<br />তোমার ইচ্ছায় তা’র জীবন মরণ ॥৮॥
bhakati-vinoda ati dīna akiñchana<br />tomāra ichchhāya tā’ra jīvana maraṇa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">ati</span>–very; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–surrendered; <span class="e2">akiñchana</span>–detached; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhāya</span>–according to will; <span class="e2">tā’ra</span>–his; <span class="e2">jīvana</span>–life; <span class="e2">maraṇa</span>–death. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> Bhakti Vinod is completely surrendered and detached. He lives and dies in accordance with Your will.

বিশ্রম্ভাত্মিকা
<span class="e2">Viśrambhātmikā:</span> <br />Confidence in the Lord’s Protection
(২১)
(21)
এখন বুঝিনু প্রভু! তোমার চরণ ।<br />অশোক-অভয়ামৃত-পূর্ণ সর্ব্বক্ষণ ॥১॥
ekhana bhujhinu prabhu! tomāra charaṇa<br />aśoka-abhayāmṛta-pūrṇa sarva-kṣaṇa <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">bhujinu</span>–I have understood; <span class="e2">prabhu!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">aśoka</span>–sorrowlessness; <span class="e2">abhaya</span>–fearlessness; <span class="e2">amṛta</span>–nectar; <span class="e2">pūrṇa</span>–full of; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–all; <span class="e2">kṣaṇa</span>–moments. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Now I have understood that Your feet are always replete with sorrowlessness, fearlessness, and immortality.
সকল ছাড়িয়া তুয়া চরণকমলে ।<br />পড়িয়াছি আমি নাথ! তব পদতলে ॥২॥
sakala chhāḍiyā tuyā charaṇa-kamale<br />paḍiyāchhi āmi nātha! tava pada-tale <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sakala</span>–everything; <span class="e2">chhāḍiyā</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">kamale</span>–at the lotus; <span class="e2">paḍiyāchhi</span>–have fallen; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">tale</span>–beneath. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> I have relinquished everything at Your lotus feet and fallen before them, O Lord!
তব পাদপদ্ম, নাথ! রক্ষিবে আমারে ।<br />আর রক্ষাকর্ত্তা নাহি এ ভবসংসারে ॥৩॥
tava pāda-padma, nātha! rakṣibe āmāre<br />āra rakṣā-kartā nāhi e bhava-saṁsāre <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">pāda</span>–feet; <span class="e2">padma</span>–lotus; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">rakṣibe (rakṣā karibe)</span>–will protect; <span class="e2">āmāre</span>–to me; <span class="e2">āra</span>–other; <span class="e2">rakṣā</span>–protection; <span class="e2">kartā</span>–doer; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–is not; <span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">bhava</span>–of birth and death; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in this world. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Your lotus feet will protect me. There is no other protector in this world of birth and death.
আমি তব নিত্যদাস—জানিনু এবার ।<br />আমার পালন-ভার এখন তোমার ॥৪॥
āmi tava nitya dāsa—jāninu e-bāra<br />āmāra pālana-bhāra ekhana tomāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servant; <span class="e2">jāninu</span>–I have understood;<span class="e2"> e</span>–this; <span class="e2">bāra</span>–time; <span class="e2">āmāra</span>–my; <span class="e2">pālana</span>–protection; <span class="e2">bhāra</span>–responsibility; <span class="e2">ekhana</span>–now; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Now I have understood that I am Your eternal servant. The responsibility of maintaining me is now Yours.
বড় দুঃখ পাইয়াছি স্বতন্ত্র জীবনে ।<br />সব দুঃখ দূরে গেল, ও পদ বরণে ॥৫॥
baḍa duḥkha pāiyāchhi svatantra jīvane<br />saba duḥkha dūre gela, o pada varaṇe <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">baḍa</span>–great; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress; <span class="e2">pāiyāchhi</span>–I have experienced; <span class="e2">svatantra (anāśrita)</span>–independent (unsheltered); <span class="e2">jīvane</span>–in life; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">duḥkha</span>–distress; <span class="e2">dūre</span>–far away; <span class="e2">gela</span>–went; <span class="e2">o</span>–those; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">varaṇe</span>–by accepting. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> I experienced only great distress in my independent life. All my distress has gone away by embracing Your feet.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> o pada varaṇe: </span>“By embracing Your feet.” In <span class="e3">Prārthanā</span> (43.1), Śrīla Narottam Ṭhākur has written:
āśraya la-iyā bhaje,<span class="e5">	tāre kṛṣṇa nāhi tyaje</span><br /><span class="e6">	āra saba mare akāraṇa</span>
“Kṛṣṇa never abandons one who takes shelter and serves Him. All others die in vain.”
যে পদ লাগিয়া রমা তপস্যা করিল ।<br />যে পদ পাইয়া শিব ‘শিবত্ব’ লভিল ॥৬॥<br />যে পদ লভিয়া ব্রহ্মা কৃতার্থ হইল ।<br />যে পদ নারদ-মুনি হৃদয়ে ধরিল ॥৭॥<br />সেই সে অভয় পদ শিরেতে ধরিয়া ।<br />পরম আনন্দে নাচি পদগুণ গাইয়া ॥৮॥
ye pada lāgiyā ramā tapasyā karila<br />ye-pada pāiyā śiva ‘śivatva’ labhila <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />ye-pada labhiyā brahmā kṛtārtha ha-ila<br />ye-pada nārada-muni hṛdaye dharila <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span><br />sei se abhaya pada śirete dhariyā<br />parama-ānande nāchi pada-guṇa gāiyā <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ye</span>–whose; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">lāgiyā</span>–for attaining; <span class="e2">ramā</span>–the Goddess of fortune Lakṣmī Devī; <span class="e2">tapasyā</span>–austerity; <span class="e2">karila</span>–did; <span class="e2">ye</span>–whose; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">pāiyā</span>–obtaining; <span class="e2">śiva</span>–the chief of the demigods and topmost devotee, Mahādev; ‘<span class="e2">śivatva’</span>–auspiciousness, the status of being ‘Śiva’; <span class="e2">labhila</span>–obtained; <span class="e2">ye</span>–whose; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">labhiyā</span>–obtaining; <span class="e2">brahmā</span>–the universal creator; <span class="e2">kṛtārtha</span>–fulfilled; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–became; <span class="e2">ye</span>–whose; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">nārada muni</span>–Devarṣi Nārad, the son of Brahmā and Guru of Vedavyās; <span class="e2">hṛdaye</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">dharila</span>–embraced; <span class="e2">sei</span>–those very; <span class="e2">se</span>–those; <span class="e2">abhaya</span>–fearless; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet;<span class="e2"> śirete</span>–on the head; <span class="e2">dhariyā</span>–holding; <span class="e2">parama</span>–great; <span class="e2">ānande</span>–with joy; <span class="e2">nāchi</span>–I dance; <span class="e2">pada</span>–of the feet; <span class="e2">guṇa</span>–the qualities; <span class="e2">gāiyā</span>–singing. [<span class="e24">6</span>–<span class="e24">8</span>]
(6–8<span class="e14">)</span> Those feet which Lakṣmī Devī performed austerities to attain; those feet from which Śiva attained the quality of śivatva, auspiciousness; those feet by which Brahmā became fulfilled; those feet which Nārad Muni embraced in his heart—holding upon my head those very feet, which are the abode of fearlessness, I dance with great joy, chanting their glories.
(6<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">śiva ‘śivatva’ labhila: </span>“Śiva attained the quality of śivatva, auspiciousness.” This is described by Śrī Kapiladev in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(3.28.22):
yach-chhaucha-niḥsṛta-sarit-pravarodakena<br />tīrthena mūrdhny adhikṛtena śivaḥ śivo ’bhūt<br />dhyātur manaḥ śamala-śaila-nisṛṣṭa-vajraṁ<br />dhyāyech chiraṁ bhagavataś charaṇāravindam
“Śiva became imbued with the quality of śivatva, auspiciousness, by bearing upon his head the holy waters of the greatest of all rivers, the Ganges, whose origin is the foot-wash of the Supreme Lord. The sins in the heart of one who meditates on that Supreme Lord’s lotus feet are destroyed just as a mountain is levelled by an onslaught of thunderbolts. Thus one should always meditate on the Supreme Lord’s lotus feet.”
সংসার-বিপদ্ হ’তে অবশ্য উদ্ধার ।<br />ভকতিবিনোদ (ও)পদ করিবে তোমার ॥৯॥
saṁsāra-vipada ha’te avaśya uddhāra<br />bhakati-vinoda (o)-pada karibe tomāra <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">9</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">saṁsāra</span>–of this material world; <span class="e2">vipada</span>–dangers; <span class="e2">ha’te</span>–from; <span class="e2">avaśya</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">uddhāra</span>–deliverance; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">o</span>–those; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">karibe</span>–will do; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your. [<span class="e24">9</span>]
(9<span class="e14">)</span> Your feet will surely deliver Bhakti Vinod from the dangers of material existence.
(২২)
(22)
তুমি ত’ মারিবে যারে,<span class="e22">	কে তারে রাখিতে পারে<br /></span><span class="e23">	তব ইচ্ছা-বশ ত্রিভুবন ।<br /></span>ব্রহ্মা আদি-দেবগণ,<span class="e22">	তব দাস অগণন,<br /></span><span class="e23">	করে তব আজ্ঞার পালন ॥১॥</span>
tumi ta’ māribe yāre,<span class="e5">	ke tāre rākhite pāre<br /></span><span class="e6">	tava ichchhā-vaśa tribhuvana<br /></span>brahmā ādi-deva-gaṇa,<span class="e5">	tava dāsa aganaṇa<br /></span><span class="e6">	kare tava ājñāra pālana </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">māribe</span>–will kill; <span class="e2">yāre</span>–whom; <span class="e2">ke</span>–who?; <span class="e2">tāre</span>–him; <span class="e2">rākhite</span>–to protect; <span class="e2">pāre</span>–can; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">vaśa</span>–under the control; <span class="e2">tribhuvana</span>–the three worlds—Svarga, Martya, and Pātāl (heaven, earth, and hell); <span class="e2">brahmā</span>–the universal creator; <span class="e2">ādi</span>–and so forth; <span class="e2">deva</span>–of demigods; <span class="e2">gaṇa</span>–the group; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servants; <span class="e2">aganaṇa</span>–numberless; <span class="e2">kare</span>–do; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ājñāra</span>–of the orders; <span class="e2">pālana</span>–following. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> Who can protect one whom You will kill? The three worlds are subservient to Your will. Brahmā and the countless demigods are Your servants and carry out Your orders.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> tumi ta’ māribe … tava ichchhā-vaśa tribhuvana: “</span>The three worlds are subservient to Your will.” Kṛṣṇa describes His unassailable will to Arjun just before the battle of Kurukṣetra:
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva<br />nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sāchin
(Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā: 11.33)
“All the warriors on this battlefield have already been killed by Me. O Arjun, simply be My instrument.”
<span class="e2">brahmā-ādi-deva-gaṇa … kare tava ājñāra pālana:</span> “Brahmā and the countless demigods … carry out Your orders.” Brahmā himself describes this in <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(2.6.32):
sṛjāmi tan-niyukto ’haṁ haro harati tad-vaśaḥ<br />viśvaṁ puruṣa-rūpeṇa paripāti tri-śakti-dhṛk
“In accordance with the order of Śrī Hari, I create the universe and Śiva annihilates it. Śrī Hari, the controller of the three modes of material nature, maintains the universe with His form of Kṣīrodakśāyī Viṣṇu.”
তব ইচ্ছা-মতে যত,<span class="e22">	গ্রহগণ অবিরত<br /></span><span class="e23">	শুভাশুভ ফল করে দান ।<br /></span>রোগ-শোক-মৃতি-ভয়,<span class="e22">	তব ইচ্ছা-মতে হয়<br /></span><span class="e23">	তব আজ্ঞা সদা বলবান্ ॥২॥</span>
tava ichchhā-mate yata,<span class="e5">	graha-gaṇa avirata<br /></span><span class="e6">	śubhāśubha phala kare dāna<br /></span>roga-śoka-mṛti-bhaya,<span class="e5">	tava ichchhā-mate haya<br /></span><span class="e6">	tava ājñā sadā balavān </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mate</span>–in accordance with; <span class="e2">yata</span>–all; <span class="e2">graha</span>–planets; <span class="e2">gaṇa</span>–the group of; <span class="e2">avirata</span>–uninterruptedly; <span class="e2">śubha</span>–auspicious; <span class="e2">aśubha</span>–inauspicious; <span class="e2">phala</span>–results; <span class="e2">kare</span>–do; <span class="e2">dāna</span>–grant; <span class="e2">roga</span>–disease; <span class="e2">śoka</span>–lamen­tation; <span class="e2">mṛti (maraṇa)</span>–death; <span class="e2">bhaya</span>–fear; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–will; <span class="e2">mate</span>–in accordance with; <span class="e2">haya</span>–happen; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">ājñā</span>–orders; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">balavān</span>–powerful. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> In accordance with Your will, all the planets per­petually exert their auspicious and inauspicious influences. Disease, lamentation, death, and fear all occur in accordance with Your will. Your orders are always predominant.
তব ভয়ে বায়ু বয়,<span class="e22">	চন্দ্র-সূর্য্য সমুদয়<br /></span><span class="e23">	স্ব-স্ব-নিয়মিত-কার্য্য করে ।<br /></span>তুমি ত’ পরমেশ্বর,<span class="e22">	পরব্রহ্ম পরাৎপর<br /></span><span class="e23">	তব বাস ভকত-অন্তরে ॥৩॥</span>
tava bhaye vāyu vaya,<span class="e5">	chandra-sūrya samudaya<br /></span><span class="e6">	sva-sva-niyamita-kārya kare<br /></span>tumi ta’ parameśvara,<span class="e5">	parabrahma parātpara<br /></span><span class="e6">	tava vāsa bhakata-antare </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tava</span>–of You; <span class="e2">bhaye</span>–out of fear; <span class="e2">vāyu</span>–the wind; <span class="e2">vaya</span>–blows; <span class="e2">chandra</span>–the moon; <span class="e2">sūrya</span>–and the sun; <span class="e2">samudaya</span>–all the celestial bodies; <span class="e2">sva</span>–own; <span class="e2">sva</span>–respective; <span class="e2">niyamita</span>–prescribed; <span class="e2">kārya</span>–duties; <span class="e2">kare</span>–do; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">parama</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">īśvara</span>–controller; <span class="e2">parabrahma</span>–the supreme; Absolute; <span class="e2">parātpara (asamorddhva)</span>–greater than the greatest (unparalleled); <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">vāsa</span>–residence; <span class="e2">bhakata</span>–the devotees; <span class="e2">antare</span>–within. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Out of fear of You, the wind blows, and the moon, the sun, and all the celestial bodies perform their respective duties. You are the Supreme Lord, the unparalleled Supreme Absolute. You reside in the hearts of Your devotees.
(3<span class="e14">)</span> <span class="e2">tava vāsa bhakata-antare: </span>“You reside in the hearts of Your devotees.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(9.4.68), Viṣṇu explains:
sādhavo hṛdayaṁ mahyaṁ sādhūnāṁ hṛdayaṁ tv aham<br />mad-anyat te na jānanti nāhaṁ tebhyo manāg api
“Sādhus are My heart, and I alone am their heart. They do not know anyone other than Me, and I do not know anyone other than them.”
Śrīla Narottam Ṭhākur sings about this in <span class="e3">Prārthanā </span>(45.5):
tomāra hṛdaye sadā govinda-viśrāma<br />govinda kahena—mama vaiṣṇava parāṇa
“Govinda always rests in your heart, and He declares, ‘My devotees are My heart.’”
সদা শুদ্ধ সিদ্ধকাম,<span class="e22">	ভকতবৎসল নাম,<br /></span><span class="e23">	ভকত-জনের নিত্য স্বামী ।<br /></span>তুমি ত’ রাখিবে যারে,<span class="e22">	কে তারে মারিতে পারে<br /></span><span class="e23">	সকল বিধির বিধি তুমি ॥৪॥</span>
sadā-śuddha siddha-kāma,<span class="e5">	bhakata-vatsala nāma,<br /></span><span class="e6">	bhakata-janera nitya-svāmī<br /></span>tumi ta’ rākhibe yāre,<span class="e5">	ke tāre mārite pāre<br /></span><span class="e6">	sakala vidhira vidhi tumi</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sadā</span>–eternally; <span class="e2">śuddha</span>–pure;<span class="e2"> siddha</span>–fulfilled; <span class="e2">kāma</span>–desire; <span class="e2">bhakata</span>–devotees; <span class="e2">vatsala</span>–affectionate; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–name; <span class="e2">bhakata</span>–devotees; <span class="e2">janera</span>–of the persons; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">svāmī</span>–Master; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">rākhibe</span>–will protect; <span class="e2">yāre</span>–whom; <span class="e2">ke</span>–who?; <span class="e2">tāre</span>–him; <span class="e2">mārite</span>–to kill; <span class="e2">pāre</span>–can; <span class="e2">sakala</span>–all; <span class="e2">vidhira</span>–of destinies, laws, providence; <span class="e2">vidhi</span>–determining element; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> You are eternally pure. Your desires are always fulfilled. You are known as <span class="e3">Bhakta-vatsal</span>, He who is affectionate to His devotees. You are the eternal master of Your devotees. Who can kill one whom You will protect? You are the author of all destinies.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> siddha-kāma:</span> “Your desires are always fulfilled.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam </span>(6.9.22), the demigods describe the Lord in this way:
avismitaṁ taṁ paripūrṇa-kāmaṁ<br />svenaiva lābhena samaṁ praśāntam<br />vinopasarpaty aparaṁ hi bāliśaḥ<br />śva-lāṅgulenātititarti sindhum
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 6.9.22)
“The eternally smiling Supreme Lord is never surprised by anything. His desires are always fulfilled. He is self-sufficient, equanimous, and peaceful. One who rejects Him and approaches anyone else for shelter is certainly a fool; he is like one who desires to cross the ocean by taking hold of a dog’s tail.”
<span class="e2">bhakata-janera nitya-svāmī:</span> “You are the eternal master of Your devotees.” In <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhagavad-gītā </span>(9.29), Kṛṣṇa says:
samo ’haṁ sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣyo ’sti na priyaḥ<br />ye bhajanti tu māṁ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu chāpy aham
“I am equally disposed to all; no one is My enemy or My friend. Yet, those who serve Me with devotion—as they are lovingly attached to Me, so I am lovingly attached to them.”
তোমার চরণে নাথ!<span class="e22">	করিয়ছে প্রণিপাত,<br /></span><span class="e23">	ভকতিবিনোদ তব দাস ।<br /></span>বিপদ্ হইতে স্বামী!<span class="e22">	অবশ্য তাহারে তুমি,<br /></span><span class="e23">	রক্ষিবে,—তাহার এ বিশ্বাস ॥৫॥</span>
tomāra charaṇe nātha!<span class="e5">	kariyāchhe praṇipāta,<br /></span><span class="e6">	bhakati-vinoda tava dāsa<br /></span>vipada ha-ite svāmī!<span class="e5">	avaśya tāhāre tumi,<br /></span><span class="e6">	rakṣibe,—tāhāra e viśvāsa</span> <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–at the feet;<span class="e2"> nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">kariyāchhe</span>–have done; <span class="e2">praṇipāta</span>–obeisance; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dāsa</span>–servant; <span class="e2">vipada</span>–danger; <span class="e2">ha-ite</span>–from; <span class="e2">svāmī!</span>–Master!; <span class="e2">avaśya</span>–surely; <span class="e2">tāhāre</span>–him; <span class="e2">tumi</span>–You; <span class="e2">rakṣibe</span>–will protect; <span class="e2">tāhāra</span>–his; <span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">viśvāsa</span>–faith. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Your servant Bhakti Vinod has offered his obeisance at Your feet. O Master! You will certainly protect him from all danger—this is his faith.
(২৩)
<span class="e2">(23)</span>
আত্মসমর্পণে গেলা অভিমান ।<br />নাহি করবুঁ নিজ রক্ষা-বিধান ॥১॥
ātma-samarpaṇe gelā abhimāna<br />nāhi karabu̐ nija rakṣā-vidhāna <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">ātma</span>–myself; <span class="e2">samarpaṇe</span>–by fully offering; <span class="e2">gelā</span>–went; <span class="e2">abhimāna (svasāmarthya-buddhi)</span>–false egotism (conception of self-sufficiency); <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">karabu̐</span>–I will make; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">rakṣā</span>–protection; <span class="e2">vidhāna</span>–arrangements. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> By fully offering myself unto You, my false egotism has gone away. I will no longer make any arrangements to protect myself.
তুয়া ধন জানি’ তুহুঁ রাখবি নাথ!<br />পাল্য গোধন জানি করি’ তুয়া সাথ ॥২॥
tuyā dhana jāni’ tuhu̐ rākhabi nātha!<br />pālya go-dhana jāni kari’ tuyā sātha <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–property; <span class="e2">jāni’</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">tuhu̐</span>–You; <span class="e2">rākhabi</span>–will protect; <span class="e2">nātha!</span>–O Lord!; <span class="e2">pālya</span>–to be protected; <span class="e2">go</span>–cow; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–property; <span class="e2">jāni</span>–knowing; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">sātha</span>–company. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! Knowing me to be Your property, You will maintain me and keep me with You as one of Your protected cows.
চরাওবি মাধব! যামুনতীরে ।<br />বংশী বাজাওত ডকবি ধীরে ॥৩॥

<span class="e2">charāobi (paśu chāraṇa karibe)</span>–You will herd (You will tend Your cows); <span class="e2">mādhava!</span>–O Kṛṣṇa!; <span class="e2">yāmunā</span>–of the river Yamunā; <span class="e2">tire</span>–on the bank; <span class="e2">vaṁśī</span>–flute;<span class="e2"> bājāota (bājāiyā)</span>–sounding; <span class="e2">ḍakabi</span>–You will call; <span class="e2">dhīre</span>–gently. (3<span class="e14">)</span> O Mādhava! You will herd me along the bank of the Yamunā. You will play Your flute and call me gently.
অঘ-বক মারত রক্ষা বিধান ।<br />করবি সদা তুহুঁ গোকুল-কান! ॥৪॥

(4<span class="e14">)</span> By killing Aghāsura, Bakāsura, and so on, You will always make all arrangements for my protection, O Kān of Gokul!
রক্ষা করবি তুহুঁ নিশ্চয় জানি ।<br />পান করবুঁ হাম্ যামুনপানি ॥৫॥

কালীয়-দোখ করবি বিনাশা ।<br />শোধবি নদীজল বাড়াওবি আশা ॥৬॥

(6<span class="e14">)</span> You will absolve Kāliya’s offences, purify the Yamunā’s waters, and thus increase my faith.
পিয়ত দাবানল রখবি মোয় ।<br />গোপাল গোবিন্দ নাম তব হোয় ॥৭॥

<span class="e2">piyata (pāna kariyā)</span>–swallowing; <span class="e2">dāva</span>–forest; <span class="e2">anala</span>–fire; <span class="e2">rakhabi</span>–You will protect; <span class="e2">moya (āmāke)</span>–to me; <span class="e2">‘gopāla’</span>–<span class="e2">‘</span>He who maintains the cows’; <span class="e2">‘govinda’</span>–<span class="e2">‘</span>He who pleases the cows’; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–names; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">hoya (haya)</span>–happen. সুরপতি দুর্ম্মতি-নাশ বিচারি’ ।<br />রাখবি বর্ষণে গিরিবরধারি! ॥৮॥

<span class="e2">surapati (indra)</span>–king of the demigods (‘Indra’); <span class="e2">durmati</span>–wicked-hearted; <span class="e2">nāśa</span>–destruction; <span class="e2">vichāri’ (vichāra kariyā)</span>–deciding; <span class="e2">rākhabi</span>–You will protect; <span class="e2">varṣaṇe</span>–from the rains; <span class="e2">giri</span>–of all mountains; <span class="e2">vara</span>–the best (Girirāj Govardhan); <span class="e2">dhāri</span>–lifter. (8<span class="e14">)</span> Deciding to level the pride of Devarāj Indra, You will protect me from his rains, O Lifter of Girirāj Govardhan!
চতুরানন করব যব চোরি ।<br />রক্ষা করবি মোয়ে গোকুল হরি! ॥৯॥

<span class="e2">chaturānana</span>–Brahmā (‘He who possesses four faces’); <span class="e2">karaba</span>–will do; <span class="e2">yava</span>–when; <span class="e2">chori (churi)</span>–steals; <span class="e2">rakṣā</span>–protection; <span class="e2">karabi</span>–You will do; <span class="e2">moye</span>–me; <span class="e2">gokula</span>–of Gokul; <span class="e2">hari!</span>–O Lord! <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">tuyā</span>–Your; <span class="e2">gokula</span>–in Gokul; <span class="e2">dhana</span>–property (cow); <span class="e2">rākhabi</span>–You will protect; <span class="e2">keśava!</span>–O Kṛṣṇa!; <span class="e2">karata</span>–doing; <span class="e2">yatana</span>–care. বরজ-বিপিনে সখীসাথ ।<br />সেবন করবুঁ রাধানাথ! ॥২॥

গাঁথবি মালা মনোহারিণী ।<br />নিতি রাধাকৃষ্ণ-বিমোহিনী ॥৭॥
