kabe vṛṣabhānu-pūre,<span class="e5">	āhirī gopera ghare,</span><br /><span class="e6">	tanayā ha-iyā janamiba</span><br />yāvaṭe āmāra kabe,<span class="e5">	e-pāṇi grahaṇa habe</span><br /><span class="e6">	vasati kariba kabe tāya</span>
“When will I be born as a daughter in the home of an Āhirī cowherd man in the village of Vṛṣabhānu? When will I be married in the village of Yāvaṭ? When will I reside there (and serve Śrī Rādhā’s intimate friends)?”
নিজ সিদ্ধদেহ,<span class="e25">	নিজ সিদ্ধনাম,<br /></span><span class="e26">	নিজ-রূপ-স্ববসন ।<br /></span>রাধাকৃপা-বলে,<span class="e25">	লভিব বা কবে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কৃষ্ণপ্রেম প্রকরণ ॥৩॥</span>
nija-siddha-deha,<span class="e10">	nija-siddha-nāma,<br /></span><span class="e11">	nija-rūpa-sva-vasana<br /></span>rādhā-kṛpā-bale,<span class="e10">	labhiba vā kabe,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kṛṣṇa-prema-prakaraṇa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">siddha</span>–perfect; <span class="e2">deha</span>–body; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">siddha</span>–perfect; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–name; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">rūpa</span>–form; <span class="e2">sva</span>–own; <span class="e2">vasana</span>–garments; <span class="e2">rādhā (rādhābhinna śrī guru)</span>–of Śrī Rādhā (of Śrī Rādhā’s non-different form of Śrī Guru); <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–of the mercy; <span class="e2">bale</span>–by the strength; <span class="e2">labhiba</span>–I will obtain; <span class="e2">vā</span>–[an emphatic particle]; <span class="e2">kabe</span>–when; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">prema</span>–divine love; <span class="e2">prakaraṇa (paddhati)</span>–method (path). [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> When will I attain, by the mercy of Śrī Rādhā (Śrī Guru), my eternal name, eternal body, eternal dress, and the path of Kṛṣṇa-prema?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> nija-siddha-deha … kṛṣṇa-prema-prakaraṇa:</span> “When will I obtain … the path of Kṛṣṇa-prema?” Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur has described this path in further detail in his <span class="e3">Śrī Hari-nāma-chintāmaṇi</span> as follows:
“A practitioner whose natural propensity is to pursue a relationship of amorous love (madhura-rasa) with the Lord must accept the practice of subser­vience (ānugatya) to a Vraja-gopī. If he does not accept the nature of a Vraja-gopī, he will not become qualified for a relationship of amorous love with the Lord. When a practitioner accepts the eleven aspects of a Vraja-gopī’s the nature (bhāva), he will attain the position of a Vraja-gopī.
“The eleven aspects of a Vraja-gopī’s nature are: (1) sambandha: relationship in madhura-rasa; (2) vayas: age; (3) nām: name; (4) rūpa: form; (5) yūtha-praveś: group of girlfriends; (6) veś: dress; (7) ājnā: duties; (8) vāsa-sthān: place of residence; (9) sevā: service to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; (10) parākāṣṭhā: paramount aspiration; and (11) pālya-dāsī-bhāva: mood of a protected maidservant.
“In whatever form a practitioner may live in within this world, he will engage in service, having embraced within his heart these eleven aspects of Vraja-gopī-bhāva.”
যামুন সলিল<span class="e25">	আহরণে গিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e26">	বুঝিব যুগল-রস ।<br /></span>প্রেমমুগ্ধ হ’য়ে,<span class="e25">	পাগলিনী-প্রায়,<br /></span><span class="e26">	গাইব রাধার যশ ॥৪॥</span>
yāmuna-salila-<span class="e10">	āharaṇe giyā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	bujhiba yugala-rasa<br /></span>prema-mugdha ha’ye,<span class="e10">	pāgalinī-prāya,<br /></span><span class="e11">	gāiba rādhāra yaśa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">yāmuna</span>–of the river Yamunā; <span class="e2">salila</span>–water; <span class="e2">āharaṇe</span>–to collect; <span class="e2">giyā</span>–going; <span class="e2">bujhiba</span>–I will understand; <span class="e2">yugala</span>–of the Divine Couple; <span class="e2">rasa</span>–ecstatic relationship; <span class="e2">prema</span>–with divine love; <span class="e2">mugdha</span>–overwhelmed; <span class="e2">ha’ye</span>–becoming; <span class="e2">pāgalinī</span>–madwoman; <span class="e2">prāya</span>–almost; <span class="e2">gāiba</span>–I will sing; <span class="e2">rādhāra</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">yaśa</span>–the glories. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Then as I collect water from the river Yamunā, I will have realisations about the Divine Couple’s loving relationship. I will become overwhelmed with prema and sing Śrī Rādhā’s glories like a madwoman.
(১৬)
(16)
বৃষভানুসুতা-<span class="e25">	চরণ-সেবনে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	হইব যে পাল্যদাসী ।<br /></span>শ্রীরাধার সুখ,<span class="e25">	সতত সাধনে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	রহিব আমি প্রয়াসী ॥১॥</span>
vṛṣabhānu-sutā-<span class="e10">	charaṇa-sevane,<br /></span><span class="e11">	ha-iba ye pālya-dāsī<br /></span>śrī-rādhāra sukha,<span class="e10">	satata sādhane,<br /></span><span class="e11">	rahiba āmi prayāsī </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">vṛṣabhānu</span>–of Vṛṣabhānu; <span class="e2">sutā</span>–of the daughter; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">sevane</span>–in the service; <span class="e2">ha-iba</span>–I will become; <span class="e2">ye</span>–which; <span class="e2">pālya</span>–to be maintained; <span class="e2">dāsī (nitya-siddhā sakhī-gaṇa āśritā)</span>–maidservant (sheltered maidservant of the eternal, spiritual girlfriends of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī); <span class="e2">śrī-rādhāra</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">satata</span>–always; <span class="e2">sādhane</span>–in pursuits; <span class="e2">rahiba</span>–will remain; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">prayāsī</span>–one who endeavours. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I will become a maintained maidservant engaged in the service of Vṛṣabhānu Sutā’s feet and constantly endeavour for Her happiness.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> pālya-dāsī: </span>“A maintained maidservant.” Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī has described the mood (bhāva) of a pālya-dāsī in his compo­sition <span class="e3">Vraja-vilāsa-stava </span>(29):
sāndra-prema-rasaiḥ plutā priyatayā prāgalbhyam āptā tayoḥ<br />prāṇa-preṣṭha-vayasyayor anudinaṁ līlābhisāraṁ kramaiḥ<br />vaidagdhyena tathā sakhīṁ prati sadā mānasya śikṣāṁ rasair<br />yeyaṁ kārayatīha hanta lalitā gṛhṇātu sā māṁ gaṇaiḥ
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur has translated this verse in his <span class="e3">Jaiva-dharma </span>as follows: “Śrī Lalitā Devī, steeped in intense divine love and impu­dent as an expression of her affection, makes daily arrangements for the secluded amorous union of her dearly beloved Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa. With her cunning, she teaches her dearest girlfriend, Śrī Rādhikā, the art of exhibiting jealous anger (mān). May that Lalitā Devī accept me within her group of associates; may she accept me as her maintained maidservant (pālya-dāsī).”
শ্রীরাধার সুখে,<span class="e25">	কৃষ্ণের যে সুখ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	জানিব মনেতে আমি ।<br /></span>রাধাপদ ছাড়ি’,<span class="e25">	শ্রীকৃষ্ণ-সঙ্গমে,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কভু না হইব কামী ॥২॥</span>
śrī-rādhāra sukhe,<span class="e10">	kṛṣṇera ye sukha,<br /></span><span class="e11">	jāniba manete āmi<br /></span>rādhā-pada chhāḍi’,<span class="e10">	śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅgame,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kabhu nā ha-iba kāmī </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">śrī-rādhāra</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">sukhe</span>–in the happiness; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇera</span>–of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">ye</span>–which; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">jāniba</span>–I will know; <span class="e2">manete</span>–in my heart; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">rādhā</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">pada</span>–the feet; <span class="e2">chhāḍi’</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa</span>–with Śrī Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">saṅgame</span>–for union; <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–ever; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">ha-iba</span>–I will become; <span class="e2">kāmī</span>–desirous. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> I will know within my heart the pleasure that Kṛṣṇa finds in the pleasure of Śrī Rādhā. I will never abandon Śrī Rādhā’s feet and become desirous of direct union with Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> śrī rādhāra sukhe … kāmī: </span>“I will never become desirous of direct union with Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” This mood of chastity has been explained by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur in his <span class="e3">Jaiva-dharma</span> as follows:
“You are a maidservant of Śrī Rādhikā—Her service alone is your service. If, being sent by Her, you enter into the presence of Kṛṣṇa in a solitary place and Kṛṣṇa approaches you amorously, you should not consent to His advances. You are Śrī Rādhikā’s maidservant; without Śrī Rādhikā’s permission you should not independently serve Kṛṣṇa. Although you should maintain equal affection for both Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, you should be more eager to engage in the loving service (dāsya-prema) of Śrī Rādhikā than the loving service of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. This is known as <span class="e3">sevā</span>. Your only sevā is to engage in Śrī Rādhā’s service during all eight periods of the day (aṣṭa-kālīn).”
সখীগণ মম<span class="e25">	পরম-সুহৃৎ,<br /></span><span class="e26">	যুগল-প্রেমের গুরু ।<br /></span>তদনুগ হ’য়ে,<span class="e25">	সেবিব রাধার<br /></span><span class="e26">	চরণ-কলপ-তরু ॥৩॥</span>
sakhī-gaṇa mama<span class="e10">	parama-suhṛt,<br /></span><span class="e11">	yugala-premera guru<br /></span>tad anuga ha’ye,<span class="e10">	seviba rādhāra<br /></span><span class="e11">	charaṇa-kalapa-taru </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sakhī</span>–of girlfriends; <span class="e2">gaṇa</span>–group; <span class="e2">mama</span>–my; <span class="e2">parama</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">suhṛt</span>–the well-wishers; <span class="e2">yugala</span>–of the Divine Couple; <span class="e2">premera</span>–of divine love; <span class="e2">guru</span>–guardians, instructors; <span class="e2">tad</span>–of them; <span class="e2">anuga</span>–the follower; <span class="e2">ha’ye</span>–being; <span class="e2">seviba</span>–I will serve; <span class="e2">rādhāra</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–of the feet; <span class="e2">kalapa-taru</span>–the wish-fulfilling tree. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Śrī Rādhā’s girlfriends are my greatest well-wishers. They are my Gurus who teach me about the Divine Couple’s prema. As their follower, I will serve the wish-fulfilling tree of Śrī Rādhā’s feet.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> sakhī-gaṇa … kalpa-taru: </span>“Śrī Rādhā’s girlfriends are my Gurus … As their follower, I will serve Śrī Rādhā.” This practice of subservience unto Śrī Rādhā’s girlfriends has been explained by Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Prabhu in his <span class="e3">Vraja-vilāsa-stava </span>(38):
tāmbūlārpaṇa-pāda-mardana-payo-dānābhisārādibhir<br />vṛndāraṇya-maheśvarīṁ priyatayā yās toṣayanti priyāḥ<br />prāṇa-preṣṭha-sakhī-kulād api kilāsaṅkochitā bhūmikāḥ<br />kelī-bhūmiṣu rūpa-mañjarī-mukhās tā dāsikāh saṁśraye
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur translates this verse as follows in his <span class="e3">Jaiva-dharma</span>: “The group of Śrī Rādhikā’s maidservants led by Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī always please Her by offering Her betel-rolls, massaging Her feet, bringing Her water, arranging for Her secluded amorous unions with Her paramour, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and by performing other such services with affection. They are by nature more unreserved in their service activities than the prāṇa-preṣṭha-sakhīs (Lalitā Devī, Viśākhā Devī, and so forth). I take complete shelter of them (I accept them as my instructing guardians (Śikṣā-gurus) who guide me in my service activities).”
রাধা-পক্ষ ছাড়ি’<span class="e25">	যে জন সে জন<br /></span><span class="e26">	যে ভাবে সে ভাবে থাকে ।<br /></span>আমি ত’ রাধিকা-<span class="e25">	পক্ষপাতী সদা,<br /></span><span class="e26">	কভু নাহি হেরি তাকে ॥৪॥</span>
rādhā-pakṣa chhāḍi’<span class="e10">	ye-jana se-jana<br /></span><span class="e11">	ye bhāve se bhāve thāke<br /></span>āmi ta’ rādhikā-<span class="e10">	pakṣapātī sadā,<br /></span><span class="e11">	kabhu nāhi heri tā’ke </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">rādhā</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">pakṣa</span>–the party; <span class="e2">chhāḍi’</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">ye</span>–which; <span class="e2">jana</span>–persons; <span class="e2">se</span>–those; <span class="e2">jana</span>–persons; <span class="e2">ye</span>–which; <span class="e2">bhāve</span>–nature; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">bhāve</span>–mood; <span class="e2">thāke</span>–stay; <span class="e2">āmi</span>–I; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">rādhikā</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">pakṣapātī</span>–partial; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">kabhu</span>–ever; <span class="e2">nāhi</span>–not; <span class="e2">heri</span>–I see; <span class="e2">tā’ke</span>–to them. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> I am always completely partial to Śrī Rādhā’s party. I never even look at those who have abandoned Her party, whoever they are, and whatever their nature may be.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> rādhā-pakṣa … tā’ke:</span> “I am always completely partial to Śrī Rādhā’s party …” This conviction has been expressed by Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Prabhu in the sixth verse of his <span class="e3">Svaniyama-daśakam</span>:
anādṛtyodgītām api muni-gaṇair vaiṇika-mukhaiḥ<br />pravīṇāṁ gāndharvām api cha nigamais tat-priyatamām<br />ya ekaṁ govindaṁ bhajati kapaṭī dāmbhikatayā<br />tad-abhyarṇe śīrṇe kṣaṇam api na yāmi vratam idam
“I never, even for a moment, go near the impure vicinity of a con­ceited charlatan who worships Śrī Govinda alone, having disregarded His dearmost beloved Śrīmatī Gāndharvā, whose super-excellent glories are sung throughout all the scriptures by the great sages headed by the vīṇā player Nārad Muni. This is my solemn vow.”
Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur expresses the same conviction in the ninth verse of his <span class="e3">Svaniyama-dvādaśakam</span>:
arādhaṁ govindaṁ bhajati nitarāṁ dāmbhikatayā<br />tad-abhyāse kintu kṣaṇam api na yāmi vratam idam
“I will never, even for a moment, go anywhere near those who, ridden with extreme conceit, worship Śrī Govinda without Śrī Rādhā. This is my vow.”

বিজ্ঞপ্তি
<span class="e2">Vijñapti:</span> <br />Prayer of Heartfelt Hankering
<span class="e27">	কবে হবে বল সে দিন আমার ।<br /></span>(আমার) অপরাধ ঘুচি’,<span class="e28">	শুদ্ধ নামে রুচি,<br /></span><span class="e27">	কৃপা-বলে হবে হৃদয়ে সঞ্চর ॥১॥</span>
<span class="e6">	kabe ha’be bala se dina āmāra<br /></span>(āmāra) aparādha ghuchi’,<span class="e17">	śuddha nāme ruchi,<br /></span><span class="e18">	kṛpā-bale ha’be hṛdaye sañchara </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–when?; <span class="e2">ha’be</span>–will be; <span class="e2">bala</span>–please tell; <span class="e2">se</span>–that; <span class="e2">dina</span>–day;<span class="e2"> āmāra</span>–mine; <span class="e2">aparādha</span>–offences; <span class="e2">ghuchi’</span>–dispelling; <span class="e2">śuddha</span>–pure; <span class="e2">nāme</span>–for the Name; <span class="e2">ruchi (anurāga)</span>–taste (deep loving attachment); <span class="e2">kṛpā (nāma vā guru kṛpā)</span>–of mercy (of the mercy of the Name, or, of the mercy of Śrī Guru); <span class="e2">bale</span>–by the power; <span class="e2">ha’be</span>–will be; <span class="e2">hṛdaye</span>–in my heart; <span class="e2">sañchara</span>–infused. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> Please tell me, when will that day be mine when my offences will be dispelled and taste for the pure Name will be infused within my heart by the power of mercy?
তৃণাধিক হীন,<span class="e28">	কবে নিজে মানি,<br /></span><span class="e27">	সহিষ্ণুতা-গুণ হৃদয়েতে আনি’ ।<br /></span>সকলে মানদ,<span class="e28">	আপনি অমানী,<br /></span><span class="e27">	হয়ে আস্বাদিব নাম-রস-সার ॥২॥</span>
tṛṇādhika hīna,<span class="e17">	kabe nije māni,<br /></span><span class="e18">	sahiṣṇutā-guṇa hṛdayete āni’<br /></span>sakale mānada,<span class="e17">	āpani amānī,<br /></span><span class="e18">	ha’ye āsvādiba nāma-rasa-sāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tṛṇa</span>–a blade of grass; <span class="e2">adhika</span>–more than; <span class="e2">hīna</span>–low; <span class="e2">kabe</span>–when?; <span class="e2">nije</span>–towards myself; <span class="e2">māni</span>–considering; <span class="e2">sahiṣṇutā</span>–of tolerance; <span class="e2">guṇa</span>–the quality; <span class="e2">hṛdayete</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">āni’</span>–bringing; <span class="e2">sakale</span>–to all; <span class="e2">mānada</span>–desire to offer honour; <span class="e2">āpani</span>–myself; <span class="e2">amānī</span>–without desire for honour; <span class="e2">ha’ye</span>–being; <span class="e2">āsvādiba</span>–I will taste; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–of the Name; <span class="e2">rasa</span>–of the ecstatic nectar; <span class="e2">sāra</span>–the essence. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> When will I feel myself to be lower than a blade of grass, bring the quality of tolerance within my heart, become eager to honour everyone and devoid of desire for honour from anyone, and relish the essence of the Name’s rasa?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">2</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> tṛṇādhika hīna … nāma-rasa-sāra: </span>“When will I relish the Name’s rasa?”<span class="e2"> </span>This verse was written in accordance with the third verse of Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s <span class="e3">Śikṣāṣṭakam</span>:
tṛṇād api sunīchena taror iva sahiṣṇunā<br />amāninā mānadena kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ
“One who is more humble than a blade of grass, is as tolerant as a tree, and gives due honour to everyone without desiring honour from anyone, is capable of always chanting the Lord’s Name (without offence).”
ধন জন আর,<span class="e28">	কবিতা-সুন্দরী,<br /></span><span class="e27">	বলিব না চাহি দেহ-সুখকরী ।<br /></span>জন্মে জন্মে দাও,<span class="e28">	ওহে গৌরহরি!<br /></span><span class="e27">	অহৈতুকী ভক্তি চরণে তোমার ॥৩॥</span>
dhana jana āra,<span class="e17">	kavitā-sundarī,<br /></span><span class="e18">	baliba nā chāhi deha-sukha-karī<br /></span>janme janme dāo,<span class="e17">	ohe gaurahari!<br /></span><span class="e18">	ahaitukī bhakti charaṇe tomāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dhana</span>–wealth;<span class="e2"> jana</span>–followers (family); <span class="e2">āra</span>–and; <span class="e2">kavitā</span>–erudition; <span class="e2">sundarī</span>–beautiful women; <span class="e2">baliba</span>–I will say; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">chāhi</span>–I desire; <span class="e2">deha</span>–<span class="e2"> </span>the material body; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–pleasure; <span class="e2">karī</span>–doing; <span class="e2">janme</span>–in birth; <span class="e2">janme</span>–after birth; <span class="e2">dāo</span>–please give; <span class="e2">ohe</span>–oh; <span class="e2">gaurahari!</span>–Śrīman Mahāprabhu!; <span class="e2">ahaitukī</span>–causeless; <span class="e2">bhakti</span>–devotion; <span class="e2">charaṇe</span>–for the feet; <span class="e2">tomāra</span>–Your. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> When will I declare that I do not desire wealth, followers, erudition, beautiful women, or any other bodily plea­sure? O Gaurahari! Birth after birth, please give me unconditional devotion to Your feet.”
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">3</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> dhana jana āra … charaṇe tomāra: </span>“When will I declare that I do not desire wealth … Please give me unconditional devotion to Your feet.” This verse was written in accordance with the fourth verse of Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s <span class="e3">Śikṣāṣṭakam</span>:
na dhanaṁ na janaṁ na sundarīṁ<br />kavitāṁ vā jagad-īśa kāmaye<br />mama janmani janmanīśvare<br />bhavatād bhaktir ahaitukī tvayi
“O Lord of the universe, I do not desire wealth, followers, beautiful women, or erudition (dharma, artha, kāma, or mokṣa). Birth after birth, I desire only unconditional devotion to You.”
(কবে) করিতে শ্রীকৃষ্ণ-<span class="e28">	নাম উচ্চারণ,<br /></span><span class="e27">	পুলকিত দেহ গদ্গদ বচন ।<br /></span>বৈবর্ণ্য-বেপথু,<span class="e28">	হবে সংঘটন,<br /></span><span class="e27">	নিরন্তর নেত্রে ব’বে অশ্রুধার ॥৪॥</span>
(kabe) karite śrī-kṛṣṇa-<span class="e17">	nāma uchchāraṇa,<br /></span><span class="e6">	</span><span class="e18">pulakita deha gadgada vachana<br /></span>vaivarṇya-vepathu,<span class="e17">	ha’be saṁghaṭana,<br /></span><span class="e18">	nirantara netre va’be aśru-dhāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–when?; <span class="e2">karite</span>–in doing; <span class="e2">śrī-kṛṣṇa</span>–of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the Name; <span class="e2">uchchāraṇa</span>–expression aloud; <span class="e2">pulakita</span>–horripilation; <span class="e2">deha</span>–body; <span class="e2">gadgada</span>–choked up; <span class="e2">vachana</span>–utterances; <span class="e2">vaivarṇya</span>–turning; <span class="e2">vepathu</span>–trembling; <span class="e2">ha’be</span>–will be; <span class="e2">saṁghaṭana</span>–occurrence; <span class="e2">nirantara</span>–incessantly; <span class="e2">netre</span>–in the eyes; <span class="e2">va’be</span>–will flow; <span class="e2">aśru</span>–of tears; <span class="e2">dhāra</span>–streams. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> When will my hair stand on end, my voice falter, my complexion turn pale, my body tremble, and tears pour incessantly from my eyes while I call aloud Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s Name?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> vaivarṇya-vepathu ityādi:</span> The symptoms of turning pale, trembling, and so forth, refer to aṣṭa-sāttvika-vikār, the eight primary transformations of divine ecstasy.
[Translator’s note: this verse is reminiscent of the sixth verse of Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s <span class="e3">Śikṣāṣṭakam</span>:
nayanaṁ galad-aśru-dhārayā<br />vadanaṁ gadgada-ruddhayā girā<br />pulakair nichitaṁ vapuḥ kadā<br />tava nāma-grahaṇe bhaviṣyati
“When will tears stream from my eyes, my voice falter, and the hair of my body stand on end as I call Your Name?”]
কবে নবদ্বীপে,<span class="e28">	সুরধুনী-তটে,<br /></span><span class="e27">	‘গৌর-নিত্যানন্দ’ বলি’ নিষ্কপটে ।<br /></span>নাচিয়া গাইয়া,<span class="e28">	বেড়াইব ছুটে,<br /></span><span class="e27">	বাতুলের প্রায় ছাড়িয়া বিচার ॥৫॥</span>
kabe navadvīpe,<span class="e17">	suradhunī-taṭe,<br /></span><span class="e18">	‘gaura-nityānanda’ bali’ niṣkapaṭe<br /></span>nāchiyā gāiyā,<span class="e17">	beḍāiba chhuṭe,<br /></span><span class="e18">	vātulera prāya chhāḍiyā vichāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–when?; <span class="e2">navadvīpe</span>–in Nabadwīp; <span class="e2">suradhunī</span>–of the Ganges; <span class="e2">taṭe</span>–on the bank; <span class="e2">gaura-nityānanda</span>–<span class="e2">‘</span>Gaura-Nityānanda!’; <span class="e2">bali’</span>–saying; <span class="e2">niṣkapaṭe</span>–sincerely; <span class="e2">nāchiyā</span>–dancing; <span class="e2">gāiyā</span>–singing; <span class="e2">beḍāiba</span>–I will wander; <span class="e2">chhuṭe</span>–running about; <span class="e2">vātulera</span>–as a madman; <span class="e2">prāya</span>–almost; <span class="e2">chhāḍiyā</span>–abandoning; <span class="e2">vichāra</span>–concern, prudence. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> When will I wander along the banks of the Ganges in Nabadwīp, sincerely calling out, “Gaura-Nityānanda!”, while dancing, singing, and running about, having abandoned all concerns as though mad?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">5</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> kabe navadvīpe … chhāḍiyā vichāra: </span>“When will I wander in Nabadwīp … as though mad?” A similar expression of longing to feel separation from the Lord is cited in <span class="e3">Śrī Śrī Prapanna-jīvanāmṛtam </span>(3.25):
kadāhaṁ yamunā-tīre nāmāni tava kīrtayan<br />udbāṣpaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa rachayiṣyāmi tāṇḍavam
(Nārada-pañcharatra)
“O lotus-eyed Lord! When will I dance on the banks of the Yamunā chanting Your Names as tears pour from my eyes?”
কবে নিত্যানন্দ,<span class="e28">	মোরে করি’ দয়া,<br /></span><span class="e27">	ছাড়াইবে মোর বিষয়ের মায়া ।<br /></span>দিয়া মোরে নিজ-<span class="e28">	চরণের ছায়া,<br /></span><span class="e27">	নামের হাটেতে দিবে অধিকার ॥৬॥</span>
kabe nityānanda,<span class="e17">	more kari’ dayā,<br /></span><span class="e18">	chhāḍāibe mora viṣayera māyā<br /></span>diyā more nija-<span class="e17">	charaṇera chhāyā,<br /></span><span class="e18">	nāmera hāṭete dibe adhikāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–when?; <span class="e2">nityānanda</span>–Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">kari’</span>–doing; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">chhāḍāibe</span>–will cause to abandon; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">viṣayera</span>–of mundanity; <span class="e2">māyā</span>–attachment; <span class="e2">diyā</span>–giving; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">charaṇera</span>–of His feet; <span class="e2">chhāyā</span>–shade; <span class="e2">nāmera</span>–of the Name; <span class="e2">hāṭete</span>–in the marketplace; <span class="e2">dibe</span>–will give; <span class="e2">adhikāra</span>–qualification. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> When will Nityānanda be merciful to me and cause me to abandon my attachment to mundanity? When will He give me the shade of His feet and grant me a place in the marketplace of the Name?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">6</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> kabe nityānanda … viṣayera māyā:</span> “When will Nityānanda cause me to abandon my attachment to mundanity?” Śrīla Narottam Ṭhākur has similarly prayed in <span class="e3">Prārthanā </span>(1.2):
āra kabe nitāichā̐da karuṇā karibe<br />saṁsāra-vāsanā more kabe tuchchha ha’be
“When will Śrī Nitāichā̐d bestow His mercy? When will my worldly desires become insignificant?”
কিনিব লুটিব,<span class="e28">	হরি-নাম-রস,<br /></span><span class="e27">	নম-রসে মাতি’ হইব বিবশ ।<br /></span>রসের রসিক-<span class="e28">	চরণ-পরশ,<br /></span><span class="e27">	করিয়া মজিব রসে অনিবার ॥৭॥</span>
kiniba luṭiba,<span class="e17">	hari-nāma-rasa,<br /></span><span class="e18">	nama-rase māti’ ha-iba vivaśa<br /></span>rasera rasika-<span class="e17">	charaṇa-paraśa,<br /></span><span class="e18">	kariyā majiba rase anibāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kiniba</span>–I will buy; <span class="e2">luṭiba</span>–I will festively scatter; <span class="e2">hari</span>–of Śrī Hari; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–of the Name; <span class="e2">rasa</span>–the nectar; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–of the Name; <span class="e2">rase</span>–with the nectar; <span class="e2">māti’</span>–being intoxicated; <span class="e2">ha-iba</span>–I will become; <span class="e2">vivaśa (ātma-vismṛta)</span>–overwhelmed (self-forgetful); <span class="e2">rasera</span>–of nectar; <span class="e2">rasika (nāma rasa-dātā śrī guru­deva)</span>–of a relisher, of a topmost devotee (of Śrī Gurudev, the distributer of the rasa of the Name); <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–feet; <span class="e2">paraśa</span>–touch; <span class="e2">kariyā</span>–doing; <span class="e2">majiba</span>–I will become submerged; <span class="e2">rase</span>–in nectar; <span class="e2">anibāra</span>–incessantly. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> When will I buy and festively scatter the rasa of the Lord’s Name? When will I become intoxicated and overwhelmed with that rasa? When will I touch the feet of a relisher of that rasa and become immersed in that rasa perpetually?
কবে জীবে দয়া,<span class="e28">	হইবে উদয়,<br /></span><span class="e27">	নিজ সুখ ভুলি’ সুদীন-হৃদয় ।<br /></span>ভকতিবিনোদ,<span class="e28">	করিয়া বিনয়,<br /></span><span class="e27">	শ্রীআজ্ঞা-টহল করিবে প্রচার ॥৮॥</span>
kabe jīve dayā,<span class="e17">	ha-ibe udaya,<br /></span><span class="e18">	nija-sukha bhuli’ sudīna-hṛdaya<br /></span>bhakati-vinoda,<span class="e17">	kariyā vinaya,<br /></span><span class="e18">	śrī-ājñā-ṭahala karibe prachāra </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kabe</span>–when?; <span class="e2">jīve</span>–for souls; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">ha-ibe</span>–will be; <span class="e2">udaya</span>–an arising; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">sukha</span>–happiness; <span class="e2">bhuli’</span>–forgetting; <span class="e2">sudīna</span>–most humble; <span class="e2">hṛdaya</span>–heart; <span class="e2">bhakati-vinoda</span>–Bhakti Vinod; <span class="e2">kariyā</span>–doing; <span class="e2">vinaya</span>–humility; <span class="e2">śrī-ājñā</span>–divine order; <span class="e2">ṭahala</span>–patrol; <span class="e2">karibe</span>–will do; <span class="e2">prachāra</span>–preaching. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> When will compassion for all souls arise within me? When will Bhakti Vinod forget his own happiness and travel about respectfully preaching the divine order with a most humble heart?
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">8</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> jīve dayā:</span> “Compassion for all souls.” <span class="e3">Jīve dayā</span> means to make souls who are averse to Kṛṣṇa become conscious of Him.
<span class="e2">śrī ājñā-ṭahal:</span> “The divine order.” This refers to following Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s order to travel about continuously engaged in Nām-kīrtan. Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur has described Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s order as follows:
prabhura ājñāya bhāi, māgi ei bhikṣā<br />bala kṛṣṇa, bhaja kṛṣṇa, kara kṛṣṇa-śikṣā
“O brothers, on the order of Śrīman Mahāprabhu, I beg from you this favour: chant ‘Kṛṣṇa’, serve Kṛṣṇa, and learn about Kṛṣṇa.
aparādha-śūnya ha’ye laha kṛṣṇa-nāma<br />kṛṣṇa mātā kṛṣṇa pitā kṛṣṇa dhana prāṇa
“Be free from offences and chant Kṛṣṇa’s Name. Kṛṣṇa is your mother. Kṛṣṇa is your father. Kṛṣṇa is your wealth and life.
kṛṣṇera saṁsāra kara chhāḍi’ anāchāra<br />jīve dayā kṛṣṇa-nāma sarva-dharma-sāra
“Abandon sinful behaviour and dedicate your family life to Kṛṣṇa. Being merciful to all souls by practicing Kṛṣṇa-nām-saṅkīrtan is the essence of all religion.”

শ্রীনাম-মাহাত্ম্য
<span class="e2">Śrī Nāma-Māhātmya:</span> <br />The Glories of the Name
<span class="e23">	কৃষ্ণনাম ধরে কত বল ।<br /></span>বিষয়বাসনানলে,<span class="e22">	মোর চিত্ত সদা জ্বলে,<br /></span><span class="e23">	রবিতপ্ত মরুভূমি-সম ।<br /></span>কর্ণরন্ধ্র পথ দিয়া,<span class="e22">	হৃদি মাঝে প্রবেশিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e23">	বরিষয় সুধা অনুপম ॥১॥</span>
<span class="e6">	kṛṣṇa-nāma dhare kata bala<br /></span>viṣaya-vāsanānale,<span class="e5">	mora chitta sadā jvale,<br /></span><span class="e6">	ravi-tapta maru-bhūmi-sama<br /></span>karṇa-randhra patha diyā,<span class="e5">	hṛdi mājhe praveśiyā,<br /></span><span class="e6">	variṣaya sudhā anupama </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa;<span class="e2"> nāma</span>–the Name; <span class="e2">dhare</span>–bears; <span class="e2">kata</span>–how much?; <span class="e2">bala</span>–power; <span class="e2">viṣaya</span>–mundane; <span class="e2">vāsanā</span>–of desire; <span class="e2">anale</span>–in the fire; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">chitta</span>–heart; <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">jvale</span>–burns; <span class="e2">ravi</span>–by the sun; <span class="e2">tapta</span>–burned; <span class="e2">maru</span>–desert; <span class="e2">bhūmi</span>–land; <span class="e2">sama</span>–like; <span class="e2">karṇa</span>–of the ears; <span class="e2">randhra</span>–of the holes; <span class="e2">patha</span>–the pathway; <span class="e2">diyā</span>–through; <span class="e2">hṛdi</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">mājhe</span>–in the middle; <span class="e2">praveśiyā</span>–entering; <span class="e2">variṣaya (varṣaṇa kare)</span>–showers; <span class="e2">sudhā</span>–nectar; <span class="e2">anu­pama (atulanīya)</span>–unequalled (incomparable). [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> How much power does Kṛṣṇa’s Name possess? My heart constantly burns in the fire of mundane desire like a desert scorched by the blazing sun. The Name enters the core of my heart through the gateway of my ears (upon being transmitted to me by Śrī Guru) and showers incomparable nectar.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">1</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> karṇa-randhra patha … sudhā anupama:</span> “The Name enters the core of my heart through the gateway of my ears and showers incomparable nectar.” Śrī Chaṇḍī Dās has described Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī’s experience of the Name’s descent as follows:
kānera bhitara diyā,<span class="e5">	marame paśila go,</span><br /><span class="e6">	ākula karila mama prāṇa</span><br />nā jāni kateka madhu,<span class="e5">	śyāma-nāme āchhe go,</span><br /><span class="e6">	parāṇa chhāḍite nāhi pāre</span>
“Śyām’s Name entered through My ears into the core of My being and overwhelmed My heart. I do not know how much nectar is present within Śyām’s Name. My heart is unable to leave Him.”
হৃদয় হইতে বলে,<span class="e22">	জিহ্বার অগ্রেতে চলে,<br /></span><span class="e23">	শব্দরূপে নাচে অনুক্ষণ ।<br /></span>কণ্ঠে মোর ভঙ্গে স্বর,<span class="e22">	অঙ্গ-কাঁপে থর থর,<br /></span><span class="e23">	স্থির হইতে না পারে চরণ ॥২॥</span>
hṛdaya ha-ite bale,<span class="e5">	jihvāra agrete chale,<br /></span><span class="e6">	śabda-rūpe nāche anukṣaṇa<br /></span>kaṇṭhe mora bhaṅge svara,<span class="e5">	aṅga-kā̐pe thara thara,<br /></span><span class="e6">	sthira ha-ite nā pāre charaṇa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">hṛdaya</span>–heart; <span class="e2">ha-ite</span>–from; <span class="e2">bale (bala pūrvaka)</span>–by force; <span class="e2">jihvāra</span>–of my tongue; <span class="e2">agrete</span>–on the tip; <span class="e2">chale</span>–goes; <span class="e2">śabda</span>–of sound; <span class="e2">rūpe</span>–in the form; <span class="e2">nāche</span>–dances; <span class="e2">anukṣaṇa</span>–at every moment; <span class="e2">kaṇṭhe</span>–in the throat; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">bhaṅge</span>–falters; <span class="e2">svara</span>–voice;<span class="e2"> aṅga</span>–body; <span class="e2">kā̐pe</span>–trembles;<span class="e2"> thara</span>–shaking; <span class="e2">thara</span>–quaking; <span class="e2">sthira</span>–still; <span class="e2">ha-ite</span>–to be; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">pāre</span>–able; <span class="e2">charaṇa</span>–legs. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> Forcefully, the Name moves from my heart to the tip of my tongue and continuously dances there in the form of sound. My voice falters in my throat, my body trembles violently, and my legs become unable to remain steady.
চক্ষে ধারা দেহে ঘর্ম্ম,<span class="e22">	পুলকিত সব চর্ম্ম,<br /></span><span class="e23">	বিবর্ণ হইল কলেবর ।<br /></span>মূর্চ্ছিত হইল মন,<span class="e22">	প্রলয়ের আগমন,<br /></span><span class="e23">	ভাবে সর্ব্ব-দেহ জর জর ॥৩॥</span>
chakṣe dhārā dehe gharma,<span class="e5">	pulakita saba charma,<br /></span><span class="e6">	vivarṇa ha-ila kalevara<br /></span>mūrchhita ha-ila mana,<span class="e5">	pralayera āgamana,<br /></span><span class="e6">	bhāve sarva-deha jara jara </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">chakṣe</span>–from my eyes; <span class="e2">dhārā</span>–streams; <span class="e2">dehe</span>–on my body; <span class="e2">gharma</span>–perspiration; <span class="e2">pulakita</span>–horripilation <span class="e2">saba</span>–all over; <span class="e2">charma</span>–my skin; <span class="e2">vivarṇa</span>–pale; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–becomes; <span class="e2">kalevara</span>–my body; <span class="e2">mūrchhita</span>–fainted; <span class="e2">ha-ila</span>–becomes; <span class="e2">mana</span>–mind; <span class="e2">pralayera (mṛtyera nyāya avasthā)</span>–of devastation (a condition like that of death); <span class="e2">āgamana</span>–coming; <span class="e2">bhāve</span>–with divine emotion; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–entire; <span class="e2">deha</span>–body; <span class="e2">jara</span>-<span class="e2">jara (jāḍya-bhāva-maya)</span>–traumatised (a condition of being utterly inert). [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> Tears stream from my eyes, perspiration soaks my body, my hair stands on end, my complexion turns pale, my mind becomes dazed, a death-like state overtakes me, and my entire body becomes stunned with emotion.
করি’ এত উপদ্রব,<span class="e22">	চিত্তে বর্ষে সুধাদ্রব,<br /></span><span class="e23">	মোরে ডারে প্রেমের সাগরে ।<br /></span>কিছু না বুঝিতে দিল,<span class="e22">	মোরে ত’ বাতুল কৈল,<br /></span><span class="e23">	মোর চিত্ত-বিত্ত সব হরে ॥৪॥</span>
kari’ eta upadrava,<span class="e5">	chitte varṣe sudhā-drava,<br /></span><span class="e6">	more ḍāre premera sāgare<br /></span>kichhu nā bujhite dila,<span class="e5">	more ta’ vātula ka-ila,<br /></span><span class="e6">	mora chitta-vitta saba hare </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kari’ (kariyāo)</span>–(although) making; <span class="e2">eta</span>–such; <span class="e2">upadrava (bāhya dṛṣṭite utpāta)</span>–disturbance (what appears to be mayhem through external vision); <span class="e2">chitte</span>–in the heart; <span class="e2">varṣe</span>–showers; <span class="e2">sudhā (amṛta)</span>–nectarean; <span class="e2">drava (rasa)</span>–liquid (juice); <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">ḍāre (ḍhāilyā deya)</span>–submerges; <span class="e2">premera</span>–of divine love; <span class="e2">sāgare</span>–in an ocean; <span class="e2">kichhu</span>–anything; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">bujhite</span>–to know; <span class="e2">dila</span>–allowed; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">ta’</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">vātula</span>–madman; <span class="e2">ka-ila</span>–made; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">chitta</span>–heart; <span class="e2">vitta</span>–wealth; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">hare</span>–steals. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> Although making such a severe disturbance externally, Kṛṣṇa’s Name showers nectar upon my heart and submerges me in an ocean of prema. Kṛṣṇa’s Name has prevented me from understanding anything, made me a madman, and stolen my heart and wealth.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">4</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> mora chitta-vitta saba hare:</span> “Stolen my heart and wealth.” Śrīla Bilvamaṅgal Ṭhākur describes this:
advaita-vīthī-pathikair upāsyāḥ<br />svānanda-siṁhāsana-labdha-dīkṣāḥ<br />śaṭhena kenāpi vayaṁ haṭhena<br />dāsī-kṛtā gopa-vadhū-viṭena
(Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu: 3.1.44)
“Although consecrated on the throne of self-satisfaction and worshipped by wanderers on the path of non-dualism, I have been forcibly converted into a maidservant by some deceitful hunter of cowherd men’s wives.”
লইনু আশ্রয় যা’র,<span class="e22">	হেন ব্যবহার তা’র,</span><br /><span class="e23">	বলিতে না পারি এ সকল ।</span><br />কৃষ্ণনাম ইচ্ছাময়,<span class="e22">	যাহে যাহে সুখী হয়,</span><br /><span class="e23">	সেই মোর সুখের সম্বল ॥৫॥</span>
la-inu āśraya yā’ra,<span class="e5">	hena vyavahāra tā’ra,<br /></span><span class="e6">	varṇite nā pāri e sakala<br /></span>kṛṣṇa-nāma ichchhā-maya,<span class="e5">	yāhe yāhe sukhī haya,<br /></span><span class="e6">	sei mora sukhera sambala </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">la-inu</span>–I took; <span class="e2">āśraya</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">yā’ra</span>–of whom; <span class="e2">hena</span>–such; <span class="e2">vyavahāra</span>–behaviour; <span class="e2">tā’ra</span>–of Him; <span class="e2">balite</span>–to describe; <span class="e2">nā</span>–not; <span class="e2">pāri</span>–I am able;<span class="e2"> e</span>–this; <span class="e2">sakala</span>–all; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the Name; <span class="e2">ichchhā</span>–desire; <span class="e2">maya</span>–made of; <span class="e2">yāhe</span>–with which; <span class="e2">yāhe</span>–with whom; <span class="e2">sukhī</span>–happy; <span class="e2">haya</span>–becomes; <span class="e2">sei</span>–that, they; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">sukhera (sādhanera)</span>–of happiness (of endeavour to serve Him); <span class="e2">sambala (upakaraṇa)</span>–means (ingredients). [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> Such is the behaviour of the Name of whom I have taken shelter. I am not able to describe all this. Howsoever Kṛṣṇa’s whimsical Name becomes pleased—that is my means of happiness (the basis of my endeavour to serve Him).
প্রেমের কলিকা নাম,<span class="e22">	অদ্ভূত রসের ধাম,<br /></span><span class="e23">	হেন বল করয়ে প্রকাশ ।<br /></span>ঈষৎ বিকশি’ পুনঃ,<span class="e22">	দেখায় নিজ রূপগুণ,<br /></span><span class="e23">	চিত্ত হরি’ লয় কৃষ্ণপাশ ॥৬॥</span>
premera kalikā nāma,<span class="e5">	adbhūta rasera dhāma,<br /></span><span class="e6">	hena bala karaye prakāśa<br /></span>īṣat vikaśi’ punaḥ,<span class="e5">	dekhāya nija-rūpa-guṇa,<br /></span><span class="e6">	chitta hari’ laya kṛṣṇa-pāśa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">premera</span>–of divine love; <span class="e2">kalikā (ku̐ḍi)</span>–the bud; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the Name; <span class="e2">adbhūta</span>–wonderful;<span class="e2"> rasera</span>–of nectar; <span class="e2">dhāma (ādhāra)</span>–abode (reservoir); <span class="e2">hena</span>–such; <span class="e2">bala</span>–power; <span class="e2">karaye</span>–does; <span class="e2">prakāśa</span>–manifestation; <span class="e2">īṣat (svalpa)</span>–slightly; <span class="e2">vikaśi’ (ātma-prakāśa kariyā)</span>–blossoming (revealing Himself); <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again, further; <span class="e2">dekhāya</span>–shows; <span class="e2">nija</span>–own; <span class="e2">rūpa</span>–form; <span class="e2">guṇa</span>–and qualities; <span class="e2">chitta</span>–heart;<span class="e2"> hari’</span>–stealing; <span class="e2">laya</span>–takes; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">pāśa</span>–the side. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> As a bud of the flower of prema, the Name, the abode of wondrous rasa, manifests such power! Upon blossoming slightly further, the Name shows me His personal form and qualities, steals my heart, and takes me to Kṛṣṇa’s side.
পূর্ণ বিকশিত হঞা,<span class="e22">	ব্রজে মোরে যায় লঞা,<br /></span><span class="e23">	দেখায় মোরে স্বরূপ-বিলাস ।<br /></span>মোরে সিদ্ধ দেহ দিয়া,<span class="e22">	কৃষ্ণপাশে রাখে গিয়া,<br /></span><span class="e23">	এ দেহের করে সর্ব্বনাশ ॥৭॥</span>
pūrṇa vikaśita hañā,<span class="e5">	vraje more yāya lañā,<br /></span><span class="e6">	dekhāya more svarūpa-vilāsa<br /></span>more siddha-deha diyā,<span class="e5">	kṛṣṇa-pāśe rākhe giyā,<br /></span><span class="e6">	e dehera kare sarva-nāśa </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">pūrṇa</span>–fully; <span class="e2">vikaśita</span>–blossomed; <span class="e2">hañā</span>–becoming; <span class="e2">vraje</span>–in Vraja; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">yāya</span>–goes; <span class="e2">lañā</span>–taking; <span class="e2">dekhāya</span>–shows; <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">svarūpa (chid)</span>–own (spiritual); <span class="e2">vilāsa (vaichitrya)</span>–Pastimes (beauty, variegated activities); <span class="e2">more</span>–to me; <span class="e2">siddha</span>–perfect; <span class="e2">deha (śrī rādhā-kṛṣṇa-sevanopayogī chinmaya deha)</span>–body (a spiritual body suitable for engaging in the service of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa); <span class="e2">diyā</span>–giving; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">pāśe</span>–by the side; <span class="e2">rākhe</span>–keeps; <span class="e2">giyā</span>–going; <span class="e2">e</span>–this; <span class="e2">dehera</span>–of the body; <span class="e2">kare</span>–does; <span class="e2">sarva</span>–complete; <span class="e2">nāśa (vastu-siddhi dāna kare)</span>–destruction (grants me supreme perfection). [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> Upon fully blossoming, the Name takes me to Vraja and shows me His divine Pastimes. He gives me an eternal body, keeps me by Kṛṣṇa’s side, and completely destroys this material body (grants me supreme perfection).
(<span class="e2">7</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> pūrṇa vikaśita … svarūpa-vilāsa: “</span>Upon fully blossoming, the Name takes me to Vraja and shows me His divine Pastimes<span class="e2">.” </span>This refers to realisation of the non-difference between the Name and the Lord Himself.
কৃষ্ণনাম-ছিন্তামণি,<span class="e22">	অখিল রসের খনি,<br /></span><span class="e23">	নিত্য-মুক্ত শুদ্ধরসময় ।<br /></span>নামের বালাই যত,<span class="e22">	সব ল’য়ে হই হত,<br /></span><span class="e23">	তবে মোর সুখের উদয় ॥৮॥</span>
kṛṣṇa-nāma-chintāmaṇi,<span class="e5">	akhila rasera khani,<br /></span><span class="e6">	nitya-mukta śuddha-rasa-maya<br /></span>nāmera bālāi yata,<span class="e5">	saba la’ye ha-i hata,<br /></span><span class="e6">	tabe mora sukhera udaya </span><span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–the Name; <span class="e2">chintāmaṇi (abhīṣṭa phala-dātā)</span>–a spiri­tual jewel (giver of one’s desired ends); <span class="e2">akhila</span>–all; <span class="e2">rasera</span>–divine relationships; <span class="e2">khani</span>–mine; <span class="e2">nitya</span>–eternally; <span class="e2">mukta</span>–liberated; <span class="e2">śuddha</span>–pure; <span class="e2">rasa</span>–divine ecstasy; <span class="e2">maya</span>–made of; <span class="e2">nāmera</span>–of the Name; <span class="e2">bālāi (vighna, aparādha)</span>–obstacles (offences); <span class="e2">yata</span>–as many; <span class="e2">saba</span>–all; <span class="e2">la’ye</span>–taking; <span class="e2">ha-i</span>–I become; <span class="e2">hata</span>–destroyed; <span class="e2">tabe</span>–then; <span class="e2">mora</span>–my; <span class="e2">sukhera</span>–of happiness; <span class="e2">udaya</span>–arise. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> Kṛṣṇa’s Name is the fulfiller of one’s desires. He is a mine of all rasas. He is eternally liberated and an embodi­ment of spiritual rasa. If I die removing all offences to the Name (from the hearts of the souls), I will be happy.
<span class="e7">(</span><span class="e2">8</span><span class="e14">)</span><span class="e2"> kṛṣṇa-nāma chintāmaṇi … śuddha-rasa-maya:</span> “Kṛṣṇa’s Name is the fulfiller of one’s desires.” This is explained in the <span class="e3">Padma-purāṇa</span> and the <span class="e3">Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</span>:
nāma chintāmaṇiḥ kṛṣṇaś chaitanya-rasa-vigrahaḥ<br />pūrṇaḥ śuddho nitya-mukto ’bhinnatvān nāma-nāminoḥ
“The Name ‘Kṛṣṇa’ is a wish-fulfilling jewel and an embodiment of spiritual rasa. He is complete, pure, eternally liberated, and non-different from whom He names.”
[Translator’s note: A recapitulation of this song by Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj is found in his book <span class="e3">The Search for Śrī Kṛṣṇa</span>:
My heart is just like a desert, hot with the rays of the sun. This is my internal mental condition. The desire for mortal things cannot satisfy me because by nature they are death-producing. And not one or two, but thousands of such death-producing desires have taken shelter in my mind. So, my subconscious region is always burning. This is my condition.
But somehow, by the grace of Sādhu and Guru, the Name of Kṛṣṇa with its infinite prospect has entered through the holes of my ears and reached the plane of my heart. And there, with some peculiar hope, with infinite, auspicious possibilities, it touched my heart with a new kind of nectar.
New hope is aroused by that sound. Then by force, it comes from the heart towards the tongue. Not that by the endeavour of my tongue I am producing that sound—no. What came from the heart of a saint through my ear entered my heart, and that forcibly appeared upon my tongue and began to dance. That is the Name proper. It descends from above. It cannot be produced by the material form of this tongue. Its source is above.
And through an agent of the Absolute it comes through the ear to the heart. From the heart it gathers some sympathy, then the Name of Kṛṣṇa forcibly appears on the tongue and begins to dance. With great force it comes to the end of the tongue, and that sweet sound begins its dancing.
The real effects of the Divine Name have been described here. If it is a living and real Name, the voice will be choked up, there will be shivering in the body, and the legs will be unable to stand. Sometimes tears will flow in a current on the body, and one’s hairs will stand on end. Sometimes changes of colour will be found in the body, and we will be unable to find any trace of the mind or consciousness. We may fall in a swoon, the whole body and mind will appear as if it is being attacked, shivering and influenced in different ways. Apparently it may seem that so many troubles are created in the body and mind, but the real heart is overflowing with a particular kind of strange, sweet juice.
At that point Bhakti Vinod says: “I am in an ocean of nectar. My whole existence is within an ocean of nectarean liquid. I am beside myself. I can’t understand where I am. Where am I? What is this? What is all about me? It has almost made me mad. Am I a madman? Where is my past experience, my seriousness, my gravity? Where are they? What am I?
“I have been converted wholesale by a foreign thing. I am a doll in the hands of a great force, which is also so affec­tionate to me. I can’t ascertain how it is possible that by my faith I have entered this great, unknown environment, unexperienced before.
“And at last I find that I am captivated. My entire being, within and without, has been captured by a particular sweet force. I can’t help being prey to such a sweet power. I can’t give any proper description of this. I came to take shelter under Him and accept Him as my guardian; now at His hand I am being dealt with in such a merciless and despotic way. Still, I feel that everything is very pleasing, beyond my experience. What is this?
“I can’t resist anymore. I am fully captured. Let my fate go any­where. I can’t come out. I am a captive in the hand of a sweet friend; my whole independence is gone. There is no way left to me but to surrender. I am unable to describe my real posi­tion. I find that He’s an autocrat. Whatever He likes to do, He will do. Since it is not possible for me to give any resistance, I must surrender. Let me also cooperate with whatever He is pleased to do. Otherwise, what can I do? I am helpless.
“Sometimes I find that the sweetness of the Name is condensed like a blossoming flower, and very wonderful streams of sweet current are flowing from it. The Name contains so many sweet variegated forms of current within Him, and He is wonderfully expressing Himself in different ways. Sometimes He emanates a peculiar type of colour and figure, and disappears.
“So many charming aspects are shown as if to my eyes within, and He forcibly takes me to surrender at the foot of that altar. He shows Himself in His full-fledged form in Vṛndāvan, in His Vraja-līlā, with Rādhārāṇī, and He takes me there. I find that I am in the midst of His peculiar, very sweet and loving paraphernalia. And He says, ‘You see! I have so many wonderful things. This is your home. I am not merely imagination, but concrete reality. You will find here that the environment is very favourable and sweet. You are to live here.’
“I see there that He is dealing in different ways with His associates, in different rasas. And I find that I have another body that has emerged from my previous one, and that has a permanent place here in His service. Such a new life I find here. And then I find ultimately that all consideration of my past life and experience has vanished. And it is true—my real life is here. This is proper, and that was a sham. That life has vanished.
“Then I find that chanting the Name gives me new encouragement, a new prospect, and new hope. Whatever we want, whatever is our internal demand, it is supplied by the Name. If we take the Name, all our internal hankerings will be fulfilled. It is eternal. It is the purest of the pure. And it is full of ecstasy. Now I find that I have been completely converted.
“Now my innermost hankering is this: let whatever is against this sweet Name vanish eternally from the world. If anything is in opposition to this sweet life, let it vanish. And if necessary, I will give my life to make it disappear from the world forever. Then others will be able to enjoy it at their free will. No hindrance should come to that fulfilment of life. It has no parallel, no equal; it is second to nothing. So, everyone may come to this plane of realisation, and, if necessary, I will sacrifice myself to finish any opposition, so that all can smoothly, peacefully, and without any danger, enjoy this absolute, sweet, and blissful life.”]

<span class="e2"></span>Śaraṇāgatera Prārthanā: <br /><span class="e7">Prayers of Surrendered Souls</span>
tava dāsya-sukhaika-saṅgināṁ<br />bhavaneṣv astv api kīṭa-janma me<br />itarāv asatheṣu mā sma bhūd<br />api me janma chaturmukhātmanā
(Stotra-ratna: 55)
“O Lord! Let me take birth, even as a worm, in the home of those whose sole happiness is Your service. O Lord, never let me take birth, even as Brahmā, among those who are averse to You.”
kāmādināṁ kati na katidhā pālitā durnideśās<br />teṣāṁ jātā mayi na karuṇā na trapā nopaśāntiḥ<br />utsṛjyaitān atha yadu-pate sāmprataṁ labdha-buddhis<br />tvām āyātaḥ śaraṇam abhayaṁ māṁ niyuṅkṣvātma-dāsye
(Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu: Paśchima-vibhāga, 2.35)
“O Lord, I have obeyed the wicked dictates of lust, anger, and so on, for so long and in so many ways! Yet they have never taken pity upon me, and I have never felt shame or satisfaction! O Lord of the Yadus, now I have abandoned them and attained proper consciousness: I have surrendered unto You, the abode of fearlessness. Please engage me in Your service.”
naitan manas tava kathāsu vikuṇṭha-nātha<br />samprīyate durita-duṣṭam asādhu tīvram<br />kāmāturaṁ harṣa-śoka-bhayaiṣaṇārtaṁ<br />tasmin kathaṁ tava gatiṁ vimṛṣāmi dīnaḥ*
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 7.9.39)
durita-dūṣita mana asādhu mānasa<br />kāma-harṣa-śoka-bhaya-eṣaṇāra vaśa<br />tava kathā-rati kise ha-ibe āmāra?<br />kise kṛṣṇa tava līlā kariba vichāra?
“My mind is sinful, polluted, and dishonest. It is controlled by lust, pleasure, lamentation, fear, and desire. How will I obtain loving attachment for discussions about You? O Kṛṣṇa, how will I reflect upon Your Pastimes?”
jihvaikato ’chyuta vikarṣati māvitṛptā<br />śiśno ’nyatas tvag-udaraṁ śravaṇaṁ kutaśchit<br />ghrāṇo ’nyataś chapala-dṛk kva cha karma-śaktir<br />bahvyaḥ sapatnya iva geha-patiṁ lunanti
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 7.9.40)
jihvā ṭāne rasa prati upastha kadarthe<br />udara bhojane ṭāne viṣama anarthe<br />charma ṭāne śayyādite, śravaṇa kathāya<br />ghrāṇa ṭāne surabhite, chakṣu dṛśye yāya<br />karmendriya karme ṭāne, bahu-patnī yathā<br />gṛha-pati ākarṣaya mora mana tathā<br />emata avasthā mora śrī-nanda-nandana<br />ki-rūpe tomāra līlā kariba smaraṇa?
“Like a householder pulled in different directions by each of his wives, my mind is pulled by the tongue towards tastes, by the genitals towards perversion, by the belly towards eating, by the skin towards a comfortable bed, by the ears towards discussions, by the nose towards fragrances, by the eyes towards sights, and by the senses of action towards their respective functions. Such is my predicament, O Nanda Nandan! How shall I remember Your Pastimes?”
tad astu me nātha sa bhūri-bhāgo<br />bhave ’tra vānyatra tu vā tiraśchām<br />yenāhameko ’pi bhavaj-janānāṁ<br />bhūtvā niṣeve tava pāda-pallavam
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 10.14.30)
ei brahma-janmei vā anya kona bhave<br />paśu-pakṣī haye janmi tomāra vibhave<br />ei mātra āśā tava bhakta-gaṇa saṅge<br />thāki tava pada-sevā kari nānā raṅge
“In this birth as Brahmā, or in another life born as an animal or bird by Your will, I desire only to remain in the association of Your devotees and to engage in various ways in the service of Your feet.”
ko nv īśa te pāda-saroja-bhājāṁ<br />sudurlabho ’rtheṣu chaturṣv apīha<br />tathāpi nāhaṁ pravṛṇomi bhūman<br />bhavat-padāmbhoja-niṣevaṇotsukaḥ
(Śrīmad Bhagavatam: 3.4.15)
kṛṣṇa, tava pāda-padme bhakti āchhe yā̐ra<br />chatur-varga madhye kibā aprāpya tā̐hāra<br />tathāpi tomāra pada-sevā mātra chāi<br />anya kona arthe mora prayojana nāi
“O Kṛṣṇa, which of the four ends (dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa) remain unattainable for one who has devotion to Your lotus feet? Still, I desire only the service of Your feet; I have no need for any other end.”
na kāmaye nātha tad apy ahaṁ kvachin<br />na yatra yuṣmach-charaṇāmbujāsavaḥ<br />mahattamāntar-hṛdayān mukha-chyuto<br />vidhatsva karṇāyutam eṣa me varaḥ
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 4.20.24)
yāhāte tomāra pada-sevā-sukha nāi<br />sei vara āmi nātha kabhu nāhi chāi<br />bhaktera hṛdaya haite tava guṇa-gāna<br />śunite ayuta karṇa karaha vidhāna
“I never desire any benediction which does not grant the joy of service to Your feet. O Lord! Grant me ten thousand ears to hear the narrations of Your glories from the hearts of Your devotees.”
na nāka-pṛṣṭhaṁ na cha pārameṣṭhyaṁ <br />na sārva-bhaumaṁ na rasādhipatyam<br />na yoga-siddhīr apunar-bhavaṁ vā<br />samañjasa tvā virahayya kāṅkṣe
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 6.11.25)
svarga, parameṣṭhi-sthāna, sārvabhauma-pada<br />rasātala-ādhipatya, yogera sampada<br />nirvāṇa ityādi yata chhāḍi’ sevā tava<br />nāhi māgi, e mora pratijñā akaitava
“O Ultimate Principle, I do not desire residence in the heavenly planets, the post of Brahmā, dominion over the Earth, rule of the hellish planets, the powers produced by yoga practice, liberation from the material world, or any other such end, if I have to give up Your service. This is my sincere promise.”
ahaṁ hare tava pādaika-mūla<br />dāsānudāso bhavitāsmi bhūyaḥ<br />manaḥ smaretāsu-pater guṇāṁs te<br />gṛṇita vāk karma karotu kāyaḥ
(Śrīmad Bhāgavatam: 6.11.24)
chhinu tava nitya-dāsa,<span class="e5">	gale bā̐dhi’ māyā-pāśa,<br /></span><span class="e6">	saṁsāre pāinu nānā kleśa<br /></span>ebe punaḥ kari’ āśa,<span class="e5">	hañā tava dāsera dāsa,<br /></span><span class="e6">	bhaji’ pāi tava bhakti-leśa</span>
prāṇeśvara tava guṇa,<span class="e5">	smaruka mana punaḥ punaḥ,<br /></span><span class="e6">	tava nāma jihvā karuka gāna<br /></span>karadvaya tava karma,<span class="e5">	kariyā labhuka śarma,<br /></span><span class="e6">	tava pade sa̐pinu parāṇa</span>
“I was Your eternal servant but I became bound around the neck by the ropes of māyā and suffered in various ways within this mater­ial world. Now again I am hoping that by becoming the servant of Your servants and serving You, I may attain some trace of devotion. O Lord of my heart, may my mind perpetually remember Your glories. May my tongue chant Your Name. May I obtain fulfilment by engaging my hands in Your service. I have offered my heart at Your feet.”

<span class="e2">Śrī Śrī Hari-Guru-Vaiṣṇava-Vandanā:</span> <br /><span class="e7">Prayers unto Śrī Hari, Śrī Guru, and the Vaiṣṇavas</span>
vande ’haṁ śrī-guroḥ śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ śrī-gurūn vaiṣṇavāṁś cha<br />śrī-rūpaṁ sāgrajātaṁ saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ taṁ sa-jīvam<br />sādvaitaṁ sāvadhūtaṁ parijana-sahitaṁ kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-devaṁ<br />śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś cha
<span class="e2">vande</span>–offer obeisance; <span class="e2">ahaṁ</span>–I; <span class="e2">śrī-guroḥ</span>–of my initiating spiritual master and instructing spiritual masters; <span class="e2">śrī-yuta</span>–beautiful, glorious, divine; <span class="e2">pada-kamalam</span>–unto the lotus feet; <span class="e2">śrī-gurūn</span>–unto the spiritual masters of the Brahma-Mādhva-Gauḍīya paramparā; <span class="e2">vaiṣṇavān</span>–unto all of the Lord’s devotees within all universal ages (unto all devotees of the past, present, and future); <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">śrī-rūpam</span>–unto Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">sa</span>–along with; <span class="e2">agra-jātam</span>–his elder brother Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">saha</span>–along with; <span class="e2">gaṇa</span>–his devoted followers, all the devotees of the Rūpānuga sampradāya; <span class="e2">raghunātha</span>–Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī; <span class="e2">anvitam</span>–along with; <span class="e2">tam</span>–him, Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">sa</span>–along with; <span class="e2">jīvam</span>–Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">sa</span>–along with; <span class="e2">advaitam</span>–Śrī Advaita Āchārya Prabhu; <span class="e2">sa</span>–along with; <span class="e2">avadhūtam</span>–Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu; <span class="e2">parijana</span>–His associates (Śrī Gadādhar Paṇḍit, Śrī Śrīvās Ṭhākur, and so forth); <span class="e2">sahitam</span>–along with; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-devam</span>–the Supreme Lord Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa</span>–of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">pādān</span>–unto the feet; <span class="e2">saha</span>–along with; <span class="e2">gaṇa</span>–all Their associates (Their sakhīs and attendant mañjarīs); <span class="e2">lalitā</span>–Śrī Lalitā Devī; <span class="e2">śrī-viśākhā</span>–Śrī Viśākhā Devī; <span class="e2">anvitān</span>–along with; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and.
I offer my obeisance unto the lotus feet of my initiating Guru, all of my instructing Gurus, all of the Gurus within the disciplic succession, and all of the Lord’s devotees. Next, I offer my obeisance unto Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu, Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu, Śrīla Raghunāth Dās Goswāmī Prabhu, Śrīla Jīva Goswāmī Prabhu, and all of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu’s associates and followers. Thereafter, I offer my obeisance unto Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Advaita Prabhu, and all of Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu’s associates. Finally, I offer my obeisance unto the feet of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Śrī Lalitā Devī, Śrī Viśākhā Devī, and all of Their associates.
oṁ ajñāna-timirāndhasya jñānāñjana-śalākayā<br />chakṣur unmilitaṁ yena tasmai śrī-gurave namaḥ
<span class="e2">oṁ</span>–[prayerful address]; <span class="e2">ajñāna</span>–of ignorance; <span class="e2">timira</span>–by the darkness; <span class="e2">andhasya</span>–of one who is blind; <span class="e2">jñāna</span>–of knowledge; <span class="e2">añjana</span>–the collyrium (eye-salve); <span class="e2">śalākayā</span>–pencil for applying collyrium; <span class="e2">chakṣuḥ</span>–my eyes; <span class="e2">unmilitam</span>–opened; <span class="e2">yena</span>–by whom; <span class="e2">tasmai</span>–unto him; <span class="e2">śrī-gurave</span>–unto my spiritual master; <span class="e2">namaḥ</span>–I offer obeisance.
I offer my obeisance unto Śrī Gurudev, who has opened my eyes, which were blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the salve of divine knowledge.
pūjya-śrī-guru-varga-vandita-mahābhāvānvitāyāḥ sadā<br />paurvāparya-paramparā-prachalita-prājya-pramūrtākṛteḥ<br />bhakter nirmala-nirjharasya nibhṛtaṁ saṁrakṣakaṁ sādaraṁ<br />vande śrī-gurudevam ānata-śirā āchārya-varyaṁ nijam
<span class="e2">pūjya</span>–worshippable; <span class="e2">śrī-guru</span>–of spiritual masters; <span class="e2">varga</span>–group; <span class="e2">vandita</span>–worshipped; <span class="e2">mahābhāva</span>–with supreme ecstatic devotion; <span class="e2">anvitāyāḥ</span>–from She who is endowed (Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī); <span class="e2">sadā</span>–always; <span class="e2">paurva</span>–from former; <span class="e2">aparya</span>–to latter; <span class="e2">paramparā</span>–disciplic succession of spiritual masters, the Rūpānuga sampradāya; <span class="e2">prachalita</span>–set in motion; <span class="e2">prājya</span>–grand; <span class="e2">pramūrta</span>–of the manifestation<span class="e2">; ākṛteḥ</span>–from the form; <span class="e2">bhakteḥ</span>–of devotion; <span class="e2">nirmala</span>–pure, spotless; <span class="e2">nirjharasya</span>–of the waterfall; <span class="e2">nibhṛtam</span>–faithful; <span class="e2">saṁrakṣakam</span>–guardian; <span class="e2">sādaram</span>–respectful, affectionate, prema-imbued; <span class="e2">vande</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">śrī-gurudevam</span>–my spiritual master; <span class="e2">ānata</span>–bowed; <span class="e2">śirā</span>–with head; <span class="e2">āchārya</span>–of exemplary spiritual teachers;<span class="e2"> varyam</span>–best; <span class="e2">nijam</span>–my own.
I bow my head in obeisance to my Gurudev, the best of Āchāryas, Śrīla Bhakti Nirmal Āchārya Mahārāj. He is the ever vigilant, stalwart guardian of the current of pure devotion, whose highest form eternally flows from our most worshippable Śrī Rūpānuga Guru-varga in their exclusive dedication to Mahābhāva, Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
gurvābhīṣṭa-supūrakaṁ guru-gaṇair āśīṣa-saṁbhūṣitaṁ<br />chintyāchintya-samasta-veda-nipuṇaṁ śrī-rūpa-panthānugam<br />govindābhidham ujjvalaṁ vara-tanuṁ bhakty anvitaṁ sundaraṁ<br />vande viśva-guruñ cha divya-bhagavat-premṇo hi bīja-pradam
<span class="e2">guru</span>–of his spiritual master; <span class="e2">ābhīṣṭa</span>–desires; <span class="e2">supūrakam</span>–fulfilling; <span class="e2">guru</span>–of his spiritual master; <span class="e2">gaṇaiḥ</span>–associates; <span class="e2">āśīṣa</span>–blessings;<span class="e2"> saṁbhūṣitam</span>–fully adorned; <span class="e2">chintya</span>–conceivable; <span class="e2">achintya</span>–inconceivable;<span class="e2"> samasta</span>–all; <span class="e2">veda</span>–knowledge, aspects of the Vedic scriptures; <span class="e2">nipuṇam</span>–expert; <span class="e2">śrī-rūpa</span>–of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu; <span class="e2">panthā</span>–the path; <span class="e2">anugam</span>–(pre-eminent) follower; <span class="e2">govinda</span>–‘Govinda’—Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj; <span class="e2">abhidham</span>–named; <span class="e2">ujjvalam</span>–effulgent, divine; <span class="e2">vara</span>–exalted; <span class="e2">tanuṁ</span>–form; <span class="e2">bhakti</span>–devotion; <span class="e2">anvitam</span>–infused; <span class="e2">sundaram</span>–beauty; <span class="e2">vande</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">viśva</span>–of the universe; <span class="e2">gurum</span>–spiritual master; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">divya</span>–divine; <span class="e2">bhagavat</span>–of the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">premṇaḥ</span>–of divine love; <span class="e2">hi</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">bīja</span>–seed; <span class="e2">pradam</span>–bestower.
I offer my obeisance unto he who perfectly fulfils his Gurudev’s most cherished desires; who is fully adorned with the blessings of his Gurudev’s associates; who is expert in all aspects of Vedic knowledge, both conceivable and inconceivable; who is the pre-eminent follower of Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu’s line; who is known as ‘Govinda’—Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj; whose beautiful, effulgent, exalted form is infused with pure devotion; who is the Guru of the entire universe; and who is the giver of the seed of divine love for the Supreme Lord.
devaṁ divya-tanuṁ suchanda-vadanaṁ bālārka-chelāñchitaṁ<br />sāndrānanda-puraṁ sad-eka-varanaṁ vairāgya-vidyāmbudhim<br />śrī-siddhānta-nidhiṁ subhakti-lasitaṁ sārasvatānām varaṁ<br />vande taṁ śubhadaṁ mad-eka-śaraṇaṁ nyāsīśvaraṁ śrīdharam
<span class="e2">devam</span>–lord; <span class="e2">divya</span>–divine; <span class="e2">tanum</span>–form; <span class="e2">suchanda</span>–most pleasing; <span class="e2">vadanam</span>–speaking; <span class="e2">bālārka</span>–of the newly risen sun; <span class="e2">chela</span>–with garments; <span class="e2">añchitam</span>–adorned; <span class="e2">sāndra</span>–intense; <span class="e2">ānanda</span>–of ecstasy; <span class="e2">puram</span>–abode; <span class="e2">sad</span>–of the sādhus; <span class="e2">eka</span>–one; <span class="e2">varanam</span>–choice; <span class="e2">vairāgya</span>–of renunciation; <span class="e2">vidyā</span>–of know­ledge; <span class="e2">ambudhim</span>–ocean; <span class="e2">śrī-siddhānta</span>–of perfect conclusions; <span class="e2">nidhim</span>–reservoir; <span class="e2">subhakti</span>–with pure, highly advanced devotion; <span class="e2">lasitam</span>–resplendent; <span class="e2">sārasvatānām</span>–of the followers of Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">varam</span>–the best; <span class="e2">vande</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">tam</span>–unto him; <span class="e2">śubhadam</span>–bestower of goodness; <span class="e2">mad</span>–my; <span class="e2">eka</span>–sole; <span class="e2">śaraṇam</span>–shelter; <span class="e2">nyāsī</span>–of all tridaṇḍi sannyāsīs; <span class="e2">īśvaraṁ</span>–leader, master; <span class="e2">śrīdharam</span>–Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj, the carrier of the current of pure devotion to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī flowing through Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu.
I offer my obeisance unto my lord, Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Goswāmī Mahārāj, whose speech is most pleasing; whose divine form is adorned with garments the colour of the newly-risen sun; who is an abode of intense, ecstatic devotion; who is the sādhus’ sole choice; who is an ocean of renunciation and knowledge; who is a treasure-house of perfect conclusions; who is resplen­dent with pure devotion; who is the best of Śrīla Saraswatī Ṭhākur’s followers; who is the giver of all good; who is the leading general of tridaṇḍi sannyāsīs; and who is my sole shelter.
śrī-siddhānta-sarasvatīti vidito gauḍīya-gurv-anvaye<br />bhāto bhānur iva prabhāta-gagane yo gaura-saṅkīrtanaiḥ <br />māyāvāda-timiṅgilodara-gatān uddhṛtya jīvanimān <br />kṛṣṇa-prema-sudhābdhi-gāhana-sukhaṁ prādāt prabhuṁ taṁ bhaje
<span class="e2">śrī-siddhānta-sarasvatī</span>–Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">iti</span>–thus; <span class="e2">viditaḥ</span>–known; <span class="e2">gauḍīya</span>–from Śrī Svarūp Dāmodar and Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu (of madhura-rasa-bhakti); <span class="e2">guru</span>–of spiritual masters; <span class="e2">anvaye</span>–in the lineage; <span class="e2">bhātaḥ</span>–shining; <span class="e2">bhānuḥ</span>–the sun; <span class="e2">iva</span>–like; <span class="e2">prabhāta</span>–morning<span class="e2">; gagane</span>–in the sky; <span class="e2">yaḥ</span>–who; <span class="e2">gaura</span>–of Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">saṅkīrtanaiḥ</span>–through saṅkīrtan (congregational glorification of the Names, Forms, Qualities, Pastimes, Associates, and Paraphernalia); <span class="e2">māyāvāda</span>–of illusionism; <span class="e2">timiṅgila</span>–of the extraordinarily massive sea-creature (lit. whale-swallower)<span class="e2">; udara</span>–the belly; <span class="e2">gatān</span>–those situated within; <span class="e2">uddhṛtya</span>–delivering; <span class="e2">jīvanimān</span>–the souls; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">prema</span>–divine love; <span class="e2">sudhā</span>–of the nectar; <span class="e2">abdhi</span>–in the ocean; <span class="e2">gāhana</span>–of diving, swimming, bathing; <span class="e2">sukham</span>–the happiness; <span class="e2">prādāt</span>–bestowed; <span class="e2">prabhum</span>–my lord, spiritual master; <span class="e2">tam</span>–him;<span class="e2"> bhaje</span>–I serve.
I serve my lord, who is known as Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Saraswatī Ṭhākur. Within the Gauḍīya sampradāya’s lineage of Gurus, he shines like the sun in the morning sky. Through the saṅkīrtan of Śrīman Mahāprabhu he rescues the jīvas engulfed within the belly of the timiṅgila of illusionism and bestows upon them the ecstasy of swimming in the nectarean ocean of divine love for Kṛṣṇa.
namo gaura-kiśorāya bhaktāvadhūta mūrtaye<br />gaurāṅghri padma-bhṛṅgāya rādhā-bhāva-niṣeviṇe
<span class="e2">namaḥ</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">gaura-kiśorāya</span>–unto Śrīla Gaura Kiśor Dās Bābājī Mahārāj; <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–of the devotee; <span class="e2">avadhūta</span>–an itinerant mendicant transcendental to varṇāśram-dharma whose ecstatic, purely devotional behaviour is incomprehensible (and disregarded) by worldly persons (and neophyte devotees); <span class="e2">mūrtaye</span>–unto the divine form; <span class="e2">gaura</span>–of Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">aṅghri</span>–of the feet; <span class="e2">padma</span>–lotus; <span class="e2">bhṛṅgāya</span>–unto the honey-bee; <span class="e2">rādhā</span>–Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; <span class="e2">bhāva</span>–loving attachment (rati); <span class="e2">niṣeviṇe</span>–unto he who serves.
I offer my obeisance unto the divine form of the devotee-avadhūt Śrīla Gaura Kiśor Dās Bābājī Mahārāj, who is a honey-bee at Śrī Gaurasundar’s lotus feet and a servant of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī imbued with deep loving attachment.
vande bhakti-vinodaṁ śrī-gaura-śakti-svarūpakam<br />bhakti-śāstrajña-samrājaṁ rādhā-rasa-sudhā-nidhim
<span class="e2">vande</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">bhakti-vinodam</span>–Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur; <span class="e2">śrī-gaura</span>–of Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">śakti</span>–of the potency; <span class="e2">svarūpakam</span>–the personification; <span class="e2">bhakti</span>–of pure devotion; <span class="e2">śāstrajña</span>–of knowers of the scriptures; <span class="e2">samrājam</span>–king; <span class="e2">rādhā</span>–to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; <span class="e2">rasa</span>–of devotion; <span class="e2">sudhā</span>–of the nectar; <span class="e2">nidhim</span>–reservoir.
I offer my obeisance unto Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur, the embodiment of Śrī Gaurasundar’s potency. He is the king of all knowers of the scriptures of pure devotion and an ocean of the nectar of devotion to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.
gaura-vrajāśritāśeṣair vaiṣṇavair vandya-vigraham<br />jagannātha-prabhuṁ vande premābdhiṁ vṛddha-vaiṣṇavam
<span class="e2">gaura</span>–of Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām; <span class="e2">vraja</span>–of Śrī Vṛndāvan Dhām; <span class="e2">āśrita</span>–by those who have taken shelter;<span class="e2"> aśeṣaiḥ</span>–by all of those; <span class="e2">vaiṣṇavaiḥ</span>–by the devotees; <span class="e2">vandya</span>–worshippable; <span class="e2">vigraham</span>–form; <span class="e2">jagannātha</span>–Śrīla Jagannāth Dās Bābājī Mahārāj; <span class="e2">prabhuṁ</span>–my lord; <span class="e2">vande</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">prema</span>–of divine love; <span class="e2">abdhim</span>–an ocean; <span class="e2">vṛddha</span>–elder; <span class="e2">vaiṣṇavam</span>–devotee.
I offer my obeisance unto my lord, the ocean of divine love, Śrīla Jagannāth Dās Bābājī Mahārāj. He is the senior-most devotee, and worshipped by all who have taken shelter in Śrī Nabadwīp Dhām and Śrī Vraja Dhām.
vāñchhā-kalpa-tarubhyaś cha kṛpā-sindhubhya eva cha<br />patitānāṁ pāvanebhyo vaiṣṇavebhyo namo namaḥ
<span class="e2">vāñchhā</span>–of desires; <span class="e2">kalpa-tarubhyaḥ</span>–unto the wish-fulfilling trees; <span class="e2">cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">kṛpā</span>–of mercy; <span class="e2">sindhubhyaḥ</span>–unto the oceans; <span class="e2">eva</span>–certainly;<span class="e2"> cha</span>–and; <span class="e2">patitānām</span>–of the fallen;<span class="e2"> pāvanebhyaḥ</span>–unto the saviours; <span class="e2">vaiṣṇavebhyaḥ</span>–unto the devotees of the Supreme Lord; <span class="e2">namaḥ namaḥ</span>–I offer my obeisance perpetually.
I eternally offer my obeisance unto the Lord’s devotees, who are saviours of the fallen, oceans of mercy, and wish-fulfilling trees.
pañcha-tattvātmakaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam<br />bhaktāvatāraṁ bhaktākhyaṁ namāmi bhakta-śaktikam
<span class="e2">pañcha</span>–of five; <span class="e2">tattva</span>–truths; <span class="e2">ātmakam</span>–the origin; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇam</span>–Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanyadev; <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–of a devotee; <span class="e2">rūpa</span>–form (of a devotee intent upon tasting the ecstatic nature of Himself); <span class="e2">svarūpakam</span>–Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, the brother of Śrīman Mahāprabhu; <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–of a devotee; <span class="e2">avatāram</span>–descended form (Śrī Advaita Prabhu); <span class="e2">bhakta</span>–of a devotee (Śrī Śrīvās Ṭhākur and all devotees of the Lord sheltered in the rasas of śānta, dāsya, and vātsalya); <span class="e2">ākhyam</span>–known as;<span class="e2"> namāmi</span>–I offer my obeisance;<span class="e2"> bhakta</span>–as a devotee; <span class="e2">śaktikam</span>–potency (Śrī Gadādhar Paṇḍit, Śrī Svarūp Dāmodar, Śrī Rāmānanda Rāy, and so forth—all the devotees sheltered in madhura-rasa).
I offer my obeisance unto the five-fold manifestation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu known as the Pañcha-Tattva: His form as a devotee (Śrī Chaitanya Himself), His expanded form as a devotee (Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu), His Avatār as a devotee (Śrī Advaita Prabhu), His pure devotees (Śrīvās Ṭhākur, and so forth), and His devotional potency (Śrī Gadādhar Paṇḍit, and so forth).
