namo mahā-vadānyāya kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te<br />kṛṣṇāya kṛṣṇa-chaitanya-nāmne gaura-tviṣe namaḥ
<span class="e2">namaḥ</span>–I offer my obeisance; <span class="e2">mahā</span>–supremely; <span class="e2">vadānyāya</span>–unto the merciful; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa</span>–of Kṛṣṇa; <span class="e2">prema</span>–of divine love; <span class="e2">pradāya</span>–unto the bestower; <span class="e2">te</span>–unto You; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇāya</span>–unto the dearmost beloved of the gopīs; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa-chaitanya</span>–as ‘Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya’; <span class="e2">nāmne</span>–unto You who are known;<span class="e2"> gaura</span>–golden; <span class="e2">tviṣe</span>–unto You who bear an effulgence;<span class="e2"> namaḥ</span>–I perpetually offer my obeisance.
I perpetually offer my obeisance unto You, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya, the supremely merciful, golden form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the giver of Kṛṣṇa-prema.
jayatāṁ suratau paṅgor mama manda-mater gatī<br />mat-sarvasva-padāmbhojau rādhā-madana-mohanau
<span class="e2">jayatām</span>–all glories;<span class="e2"> suratau</span>–most merciful, or extremely, lovingly, attached in amorous Pastimes; <span class="e2">paṅgoḥ</span>–of one who is lame;<span class="e2"> mama</span>–my;<span class="e2"> manda-mateḥ</span>–of one who has meagre intelligence which is absorbed in mundanity (of one who is insincere and eager to pursue worldly enjoyment through selfish action, heavenly enjoyment through pious action, or liberation through knowledge); <span class="e2">gatī</span>–shelter;<span class="e2"> mat</span>–my; <span class="e2">sarvasva</span>–everything; <span class="e2">padāmbhojau</span>–lotus feet;<span class="e2"> rādhā</span>–Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; <span class="e2">madana</span>–of Cupid; <span class="e2">mohanau</span>–enchanter.
All glory to merciful Śrī Śrī Rādhā–Madan Mohan! Though I am lame and wicked, They are my sole shelter, and Their lotus feet are everything to me.
nāma-śreṣṭhaṁ manum api śachī-putram atra svarūpaṁ<br />rūpaṁ tasyāgrajam uru-purīṁ māthurīṁ goṣṭha-vāṭīm<br />rādhā-kuṇḍaṁ giri-varam aho rādhikā-mādhavāśāṁ<br />prāpto yasya prathita-kṛpayā śrī-guruṁ taṁ nato ’smi
<span class="e2">nāma</span>–Name; <span class="e2">śreṣṭham</span>–the supreme (the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra);<span class="e2"> manum</span>–the eighteen-syllable bīj-mantra heard and chanted by Brahmā at the beginning of creation;<span class="e2"> api</span>–also;<span class="e2"> śachī</span>–of Śrīmatī Śachī Devī; <span class="e2">putram</span>–the son (Śrīman Mahāprabhu);<span class="e2"> atra</span>–in this connection; <span class="e2">svarūpam</span>–Śrīla Svarūp Dāmodar;<span class="e2"> rūpam</span>–Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu;<span class="e2"> tasya</span>–his;<span class="e2"> agrajam</span>–his elder brother, Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu;<span class="e2"> uru</span>–supreme; <span class="e2">purīm</span>–abode; <span class="e2">māthurīm</span>–of Mathurā;<span class="e2"> goṣṭha</span>–pasture-land; <span class="e2">vāṭīm</span>–abode (place of the Pastimes of Kṛṣṇa—Vṛndāvan);<span class="e2"> rādhā</span>–of Śrī Rādhā; <span class="e2">kuṇḍam</span>–the pond;<span class="e2"> giri</span>–of mountains; <span class="e2">varam</span>–the best (Girirāj Govardhan);<span class="e2"> aho</span>–oh!;<span class="e2"> rādhikā-mādhava</span>–for (the service of) Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava; <span class="e2">āśām</span>–the desire, eternal aspiration;<span class="e2"> prāptaḥ</span>–obtained;<span class="e2"> yasya</span>–whose;<span class="e2"> prathita</span>–cele­brated, extended; <span class="e2">kṛpayā</span>–by mercy;<span class="e2"> śrī-gurum</span>–my spiritual master;<span class="e2"> tam</span>–to him;<span class="e2"> nataḥ</span>–one who offers obeisance;<span class="e2"> asmi</span>–I am.
I offer my obeisance unto Śrī Gurudev, by whose infinite mercy I have received the best of all the Lord’s Names (the mahāmantra), the eighteen-syllable bīj-mantra, Śrīman Mahāprabhu, Śrīla Svarūp Dāmodar, Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Pra­bhu, Śrīla Sanātan Goswāmī Prabhu, the supreme abode of Mathurā, Rādhā Kuṇḍa, Girirāj Govardhan, and the aspiration to serve Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava.
atha natvā mantra-gurūn gurūn bhāgavatārthadān<br />vyāsān jagat-gurūn natvā tato jayam udīrayet
<span class="e2">atha</span>–thus;<span class="e2"> natvā</span>–after offering obeisance;<span class="e2"> mantra-gurūn</span>–unto the spiritual masters who confer initiation;<span class="e2"> gurūn</span>–unto the spiritual masters; <span class="e2">bhāgavata</span>–of <span class="e3">Śrīmad Bhāgavatam</span> (of the scriptures of pure devotion) <span class="e2">artha</span>–of the meaning; <span class="e2">dān</span>–givers;<span class="e2"> vyāsān</span>–the authors of vedic literature); <span class="e2">jagat</span>–of the whole universe; <span class="e2">gurūn</span>–unto the spiritual masters;<span class="e2"> natvā</span>–after offering obeisance;<span class="e2"> tataḥ</span>–thereafter;<span class="e2"> jayam</span>–‘all glories’;<span class="e2"> udīrayet</span>–one should say.
After offering obeisance unto one’s initiating Guru, unto the Gurus who have taught one the meaning of the scriptures of pure devotion, and unto all the authors of Vedic literature, who are the Gurus of the entire universe, one should proclaim, “Jay!”
jayaḥ sa-parikara śrī-śrī-guru-gaurāṅga-gāndharvikā-<br />giridhārī-pādapadmānāṁ jayastu!
All glory to the lotus feet of Śrī Gurudev, Śrī Gaurāṅga, Śrī Śrī Gāndharvikā-Giridhārī, and all of Their associates!
vedartu-yuga-gaurābde gaurāvirbhāva-vāsare<br />śrī-laghu-chandrikā-bhāṣyaṁ samāptaṁ sādhu-saṅgatam
This <span class="e3">Gentle Moonlight Commentary</span> was completed in the association of sādhus in the year four hundred and sixty-four of the Gaurābda era (1949), on the appearance day of Śrīman Mahāprabhu.
samāpto ’yaṁ grantham
This book is concluded.

mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />patitaṁ ghora-saṁsāre hy avaśaṁ prakṛter vaśat <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">1</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">mā</span>–do not; <span class="e2">muñcha</span>–abandon; <span class="e2">muñcha</span>–deliver; <span class="e2">mām</span>–me; <span class="e2">kṛṣṇa!</span>–O Kṛṣṇa!; <span class="e2">dāsam</span>–servant; <span class="e2">dīna</span>–distressed; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–of mercy; <span class="e2">arṇava</span>–ocean; <span class="e2">patitam</span>–fallen; <span class="e2">ghora</span>–terrible; <span class="e2">saṁsāre</span>–in the material world;<span class="e2"> hi</span>–certainly; <span class="e2">avaśam</span>–helplessly; <span class="e2">prakṛteḥ</span>–by material nature; <span class="e2">vaśat</span>–under control. [<span class="e24">1</span>]
(1<span class="e14">)</span> I have fallen into this terrible world and am helplessly subjugated by material nature. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />anādi-bhāgya-vaiguṇyāt bhoga-mugdhaṁ durāśayam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">2</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">anādi</span>–prior to contact with the realm of time and space; <span class="e2">bhāgya</span>–of fortune; <span class="e2">vaiguṇyāt</span>–from faultiness; <span class="e2">bhoga</span>–selfish enjoyment; <span class="e2">mugdha</span>–bewildered; <span class="e2">durāśayam</span>–wicked. [<span class="e24">2</span>]
(2<span class="e14">)</span> Due to my ‘time-less’ misfortune, I have been bewil­dered by the wicked desire to selfishly enjoy. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />māyā-krīḍanakaṁ dīnaṁ nirālambaṁ nirāśrayam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">3</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">māyā</span>–of Māyā Devī; <span class="e2">krīḍanaka</span>–toy; <span class="e2">dīnam</span>–poor; <span class="e2">nirālambam</span>–devoid of support; <span class="e2">nirāśrayam</span>–devoid of shelter. [<span class="e24">3</span>]
(3<span class="e14">)</span> I am a toy of Māyā Devī. I am distressed. I have no support. I have no shelter. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distres­sed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-bhīti-chintāti-kātaram <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">4</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">janma</span>–birth; <span class="e2">mṛtyu</span>–death; <span class="e2">jarā</span>–old age; <span class="e2">vyādhi</span>–disease; <span class="e2">bhīti</span>–fear; <span class="e2">chintā</span>–anxiety; <span class="e2">ati</span>–very; <span class="e2">kātaram</span>–distressed. [<span class="e24">4</span>]
(4<span class="e14">)</span> I am deeply troubled by birth, death, old age, disease, fear, and anxiety. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />jñānājñāna-kṛtānanta-pāpa-bhoga-bhayākulam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">5</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">jñāna</span>–with knowledge; <span class="e2">ajñāna</span>–in ignorance; <span class="e2">kṛta</span>–done; <span class="e2">ananta</span>–unlimited; <span class="e2">pāpa</span>–sin; <span class="e2">bhoga</span>–undergoing; <span class="e2">bhaya</span>–fear; <span class="e2">ākulam</span>–overwhelmed. [<span class="e24">5</span>]
(5<span class="e14">)</span> I am overwhelmed with fear as I suffer the reactions for the unlimited sins I have knowingly and unknowingly committed. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />kāma-krodhādi-dasyubhir nirdayaṁ padamarditam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">6</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">kāma</span>–lust; <span class="e2">krodha</span>–anger; <span class="e2">adi</span>–and so forth; <span class="e2">dasyubhiḥ</span>–by the bandits; <span class="e2">nirdayaṁ</span>–merciless; <span class="e2">pada</span>–feet; <span class="e2">marditam</span>–trampled. [<span class="e24">6</span>]
(6<span class="e14">)</span> I have been trampled by the feet of the merciless bandits lust, anger, and so on. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />antaḥśatru-viparyastaṁ punaḥ punar vilañchhitam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">7</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">antaḥ</span>–internal; <span class="e2">śatru</span>–enemies; <span class="e2">viparyastam</span>–bewildered; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–again; <span class="e2">punaḥ</span>–and again; <span class="e2">vilañchhitam</span>–harassed. [<span class="e24">7</span>]
(7<span class="e14">)</span> I am bewildered and harassed by internal enemies again and again. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />trāṇārthaṁ prārthyamāno ’pi na māṁ paśyati kaśchanaḥ <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">8</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">trāṇa</span>–of deliverance; <span class="e2">artham</span>–purpose; <span class="e2">prārthyamānaḥ</span>–one who is praying<span class="e2">; api</span>–although; <span class="e2">na</span>–not; <span class="e2">mām</span>–me; <span class="e2">paśyati</span>–sees; <span class="e2">kaśchanaḥ</span>–someone. [<span class="e24">8</span>]
(8<span class="e14">)</span> Although I am praying for deliverance, no one sees me. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />pitaro bāndhavā devā asamarthāḥ parāṅmukhāḥ <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">9</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">pitaraḥ</span>–ancestors; <span class="e2">bāndhavāḥ</span>–friends; <span class="e2">devāḥ</span>–demigods; <span class="e2">asamarthāḥ</span>–incap­able; <span class="e2">parāṅmukhāḥ</span>–those who are averse. [<span class="e24">9</span>]
(9<span class="e14">)</span> My ancestors, my friends, and the demigods are all incapable (of delivering me) and opposed to me. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />sva-para-bharasā-hīnaṁ nirupāyaṁ nirākṛtam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">10</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sva</span>–own; <span class="e2">para</span>–others; <span class="e2">bharasā</span>–hope; <span class="e2">hīnam</span>–devoid; <span class="e2">nirupāyam</span>–devoid of any means (of deliverance); <span class="e2">nirākṛtam</span>–rejected. [<span class="e24">10</span>]
(10<span class="e14">)</span> I am devoid of any hope in myself and in others. I have no means whatsoever (of deliverance), and I am utterly spurned. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />mahāparādha-rāśi-nāmālayaṁ tyakta-sādhanam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">11</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">mahā</span>–great; <span class="e2">aparādha</span>–offences; <span class="e2">rāśi</span>–multitude; <span class="e2">nāma</span>–to the Name; <span class="e2">ālayam</span>–abode; <span class="e2">tyakta</span>–abandoned; <span class="e2">sādhanam</span>–means, practice. [<span class="e24">11</span>]
(11<span class="e14">)</span> I am an abode of a profusion of terrible offences against the Name, and I have abandoned the way of deliverance. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />he sad-asad-vichārorddha-prapannārtiharo hare! <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">12</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">he</span>–oh!; <span class="e2">sat</span>–good; <span class="e2">asat</span>–bad; <span class="e2">vichāra</span>–judgement; <span class="e2">uddha</span>–beyond; <span class="e2">prapanna</span>–surrendered souls; <span class="e2">ārti</span>–distress; <span class="e2">haraḥ</span>–who takes away; <span class="e2">hare!</span>–O Hari! [<span class="e24">12</span>]
(12<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! You remove the distress of the surrendered souls, who are beyond all consideration of good and bad. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />dāsatvaṁ dehi dāsānāṁ tava deva dayānidhe! <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">13</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">dāsatvam</span>–servitude; <span class="e2">dehi</span>–give; <span class="e2">dāsānām</span>–of the servants; <span class="e2">tava</span>–Your; <span class="e2">deva</span>–O Lord; <span class="e2">dayā</span>–mercy; <span class="e2">nidhe!</span>–O reservoir! [<span class="e24">13</span>]
(13<span class="e14">)</span> O Lord! O Ocean of Mercy! Please give me the service of Your servants. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />niyuñkṣva nityadāsye māṁ pradāya prema-vartanam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">14</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">niyuñkṣva</span>–engage<span class="e2">; nitya</span>–eternal; <span class="e2">dāsye</span>–in servitude; <span class="e2">mām</span>–me; <span class="e2">pradāya</span>–granting; <span class="e2">prema</span>–divine love; <span class="e2">vartanam</span>–salary. [<span class="e24">14</span>]
(14<span class="e14">)</span> Please engage me in Your eternal service and grant me a salary of prema. O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha muñcha māṁ kṛṣṇa! dāsaṁ dīna-dayārṇava!<br />svāntaraṅga-sevāṁ dehi he gopījana-vallabha! <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">15</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">sva</span>–own; <span class="e2">antaraṅga</span>–intimate; <span class="e2">sevām</span>–service; <span class="e2">dehi</span>–please bestow; <span class="e2">he</span>–oh; <span class="e2">gopī</span>–cowherd women; <span class="e2">jana</span>–persons; <span class="e2">vallabha!</span>–beloved! [<span class="e24">15</span>]
(15<span class="e14">)</span> Please bestow Your intimate service upon me, O Belo­ved of the gopīs! O Kṛṣṇa! O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed! Don’t abandon me. Deliver this servant.
mā muñcha-pañcha-daśakaṁ! kṛṣṇa dīna-dayārṇava!<br />tridaṇḍi-śrīdharodgītaṁ gṛhānedaṁ stavāmṛtam <span class="e15">[</span><span class="e16">16</span><span class="e7">]</span>
<span class="e2">tridaṇḍi</span>–Vaiṣṇava sannyāsī; <span class="e2">śrīdhara</span>–‘Śrīdhar’; <span class="e2">udgītam</span>–sings aloud; <span class="e2">gṛhāna</span>–please accept; <span class="e2">idam</span>–this; <span class="e2">stava</span>–prayer; <span class="e2">amṛtam</span>–nectar. [<span class="e24">16</span>]
(16) Tridaṇḍi Bhikṣu Śrī Śrīdhar sings aloud this <span class="e3">Mā Muñcha Pañcha-Daśakam</span>. O Ocean of Mercy for the distressed, Śrī Kṛṣṇa! Please accept this nectarean prayer.

Guide to Reading and Pronouncing Bengali
The Bengali Alphabet and Roman Diacritical Equivalents
Vowels (<span class="e12">Svara-varṇa</span>)
অ <span class="e29">a</span> আ <span class="e29">ā</span> ই <span class="e29">ki</span> ঈ <span class="e29">ī</span> উ <span class="e29">u</span> ঊ <span class="e29">ū</span>
ঋ <span class="e29">ṛ</span> এ <span class="e29">e</span> ঐ <span class="e29">ai</span> ও <span class="e29">o</span> ঔ <span class="e29">au</span>
Vowel Signs
Whenever a vowel follows a consonant, it is written in sign form as follows:
া <span class="e29">a</span> ি <span class="e29">i</span> ী <span class="e29">ī</span> ু <span class="e29">u</span> ূ <span class="e29">ū</span>
ৃ <span class="e29">ṛ</span> ে <span class="e29">e</span> ৈ <span class="e29">ai</span> ো <span class="e29">o</span> ৌ <span class="e29">au</span>
The only exception is the inherent vowel, <span class="e2">a</span>. This vowel is considered inherent in all consonants unless they are assigned one of the aforementioned vowel signs or are the first members of a conjunct consonant.
<span class="e29">Examples:</span> ক <span class="e29">ka</span> কা <span class="e29">kā</span> কি <span class="e29">ki</span> কী <span class="e29">kī</span> কু <span class="e29">ku</span> কূ <span class="e29">kū</span>
<span class="e29">Examples:</span> কৃ <span class="e29">kṛ</span> কে <span class="e29">ke</span> কৈ <span class="e29">kai</span> কো <span class="e29">ko</span> কৌ <span class="e29">kau</span>
<span class="e29">Examples:</span> ল্ল <span class="e29">lla</span> প্ত <span class="e29">pta</span> ঙ্গ <span class="e29">ṅga</span> ন্দ্র <span class="e29">ndra</span>
Consonants (<span class="e12">Vyañjan-varṇa</span>)
<span class="e29">Gutturals:</span> ক <span class="e29">ka</span> খ <span class="e29">kha</span> গ <span class="e29">ga</span> ঘ <span class="e29">gha</span> ঙ <span class="e29">ṅa</span>
<span class="e29">Palatals:</span> চ <span class="e29">cha</span> ছ <span class="e29">chha</span> জ <span class="e29">ja</span> ঝ <span class="e29">jha</span> ঞ <span class="e29">ña</span>
<span class="e29">Cerebrals:</span> ট <span class="e29">ṭa</span> ঠ <span class="e29">ṭha</span> ড় (ড)<span class="e29"> ḍa</span> ঢ় (ঢ)<span class="e29"> ḍha</span> ণ <span class="e29">ṇa</span>
<span class="e29">Dentals:</span> ত <span class="e29">ta</span> থ <span class="e29">tha</span> দ <span class="e29">da</span> ধ <span class="e29">dha</span> ন <span class="e29">na</span>
<span class="e29">Labials:</span> প <span class="e29">pa</span> ফ <span class="e29">pha</span> ব <span class="e29">ba (va)</span> ভ <span class="e29">bha</span> ম <span class="e29">ma</span>
<span class="e29">Semivowels:</span> য (য়)<span class="e29"> ya</span> র <span class="e29">ra</span> ল <span class="e29">la</span>
<span class="e29">Sibilants:</span> শ <span class="e29">śa</span> ষ <span class="e29">ṣa</span> স <span class="e29">sa</span>
<span class="e29">Aspirates:</span> হ <span class="e29">ha</span>
<span class="e2">Gutturals (</span><span class="e12">Kaṇṭhya-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants pronounced using the throat.
<span class="e2">Palatals (</span><span class="e12">Tālabya-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants pronounced by bringing the tongue to the palate.
<span class="e2">Cerebrals (</span><span class="e12">Mūrdhanya-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants pronounced by applying the tip of the tongue to the roof of the mouth.
<span class="e2">Dentals (</span><span class="e12">Dantya-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants pronounced by applying the tip of the tongue to the back of the front teeth.
<span class="e2">Labials (</span><span class="e12">Oṣṭhya-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants pronounced using the lips.
<span class="e2">Semivowels (</span><span class="e12">Antaḥstha-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants which also function as vowels.
<span class="e2">Sibilants (</span><span class="e12">Uṣma-varṇa</span><span class="e2">):</span> consonants pronounced by making a hissing sound. The three sibilants are also palatal (<span class="e2">śa</span>), cerebral (<span class="e2">ṣa</span>), and dental (<span class="e2">sa</span>) respectively.
<span class="e2">Aspirates:</span> consonants pronounced by exhaling air from the throat. The following consonants are aspirates: <span class="e2">kha, gha, chha, jha, ṭha, ḍha, tha, dha, pha,</span> and <span class="e2">bha</span>.
Conjunct Consonants
There are numerous conjunct characters in Bengali formed by the combination of two or more adjacent consonants. In most cases, these conjunct characters bear close resemblance to the features of the individual characters they represent; there are, however, a number of exceptions.
<span class="e29">Typical examples:</span> ল্ল <span class="e29">lla</span> প্ত <span class="e29">pta</span> ন্দ <span class="e29">nda</span> দ্ব <span class="e29">dva</span> ণ্ট <span class="e29">ṇṭa</span>
<span class="e29">Atypical examples:</span> ক্ষ <span class="e29">kṣa</span> স্থ <span class="e29">stha</span> ব্ধ <span class="e29">bdha</span> ত্য <span class="e29">tya</span> ঞ্চ <span class="e29">ñcha</span>
<span class="e29">Additional examples:</span> হ্ম <span class="e29">hma</span> ঙ্গ <span class="e29">ṅga</span> ক্ত <span class="e29">kta</span> ক্র <span class="e29">kra</span> গ্র <span class="e29">gra</span> ষ্ট <span class="e29">ṣṭa</span>
Additional Signs
<span class="e29">Anusvār:</span> ং <span class="e29">ṁ</span>
<span class="e29">Visarga:</span>ঃ <span class="e29">ḥ</span>
<span class="e29">Chandrabindu:</span> ঁ
<span class="e29">Reph:</span> র্
<span class="e29">Virām:</span> ্
<span class="e29">Examples:</span> <span class="e30">কং</span> <span class="e29">kaṁ</span> <span class="e30">কিঃ</span> <span class="e29">kiḥ</span> <span class="e30">কাঁ</span> <span class="e29">kā̐ </span> <span class="e30">র্ক</span> <span class="e29">rka</span> <span class="e30">ক্</span> <span class="e2">k</span>
Pronunciation (<span class="e12">Uchchāraṇ</span>)
<span class="e2">Vowels (</span><span class="e12">Svara-varṇa</span><span class="e2">)</span>
<span class="e29">a</span> Like the <span class="e2">o</span> in c<span class="e2">o</span>t, but like the <span class="e2">u</span> in s<span class="e2">u</span>m or the <span class="e2">o</span> in g<span class="e2">o</span> when it occurs after a conjunct consonant or in the second syllable of a word; <span class="e2">a</span> is often silent when it follows a single consonant at the end of a word.
<span class="e29">ā</span> Like the <span class="e2">a</span> in f<span class="e2">a</span>ther or st<span class="e2">a</span>r.
<span class="e29">i</span> Like the <span class="e2">i</span> in b<span class="e2">i</span>n.
<span class="e29">ī</span> Like the <span class="e2">ee</span> in d<span class="e2">ee</span>p.
<span class="e29">u</span> Like the <span class="e2">u</span> in p<span class="e2">u</span>t.
<span class="e29">ū</span> Like the <span class="e2">oo</span> in m<span class="e2">oo</span>n.
<span class="e29">ṛ</span> Like the <span class="e2">ri</span> in <span class="e2">ri</span>m.
<span class="e29">e</span> Like the <span class="e2">ay</span> in pl<span class="e2">ay</span> or like the <span class="e2">a</span> in bat.
<span class="e29">ai</span> Like the <span class="e2">o</span> in c<span class="e2">o</span>t combined with the <span class="e2">ee</span> in s<span class="e2">ee</span>.
<span class="e29">o</span> Like the <span class="e2">o</span> in g<span class="e2">o</span>.
<span class="e29">au</span> Like the <span class="e2">o</span> in g<span class="e2">o</span> combined with the <span class="e2">oo</span> in m<span class="e2">oo</span>n.
<span class="e2">Consonants (</span><span class="e12">Vyañjan-varṇa</span><span class="e2">)</span>
<span class="e29">k</span> Like the <span class="e2">c</span> in <span class="e2">c</span>ot.
<span class="e29">kh</span> <span class="e2">k</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">g</span> Like the <span class="e2">g</span> in <span class="e2">g</span>ot; never like the <span class="e2">g</span> in reli<span class="e2">g</span>ion.
<span class="e29">gh</span> <span class="e2">g</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">ṅ</span> Like the <span class="e2">ng</span> in si<span class="e2">ng</span>.
<span class="e29">ch</span> Like the <span class="e2">ch</span> in <span class="e2">ch</span>op.
<span class="e29">chh</span> <span class="e2">ch</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">j</span> Like the <span class="e2">j</span> in <span class="e2">j</span>ob.
<span class="e29">jh</span> <span class="e2">j</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">ñ</span> Like the <span class="e2">n</span> in lu<span class="e2">n</span>ch.
<span class="e29">ṭ</span> Like the <span class="e2">t</span> in <span class="e2">t</span>aught (pronounced cerebrally).
<span class="e29">ṭh</span> <span class="e2">ṭ</span> pronounced with aspiration. Never like the <span class="e2">th</span> in <span class="e2">th</span>rough.
<span class="e29">ḍ</span> In between the <span class="e2">d</span> in <span class="e2">d</span>awn and the <span class="e2">r</span> in <span class="e2">r</span>aw (pronounced cerebrally).
<span class="e29">ḍh</span> <span class="e2">ḍ</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">ṇ</span> Like the <span class="e2">n</span> in <span class="e2">n</span>on.
<span class="e29">t</span> Like the <span class="e2">t</span> in <span class="e2">t</span>aught (pronounced dentally).
<span class="e29">th</span> <span class="e2">t</span> pronounced with aspiration. Never like the <span class="e2">th</span> in <span class="e2">th</span>rough.
<span class="e29">d</span> Like the <span class="e2">d</span> in <span class="e2">d</span>awn (pronounced dentally).
<span class="e29">dh</span> <span class="e2">d</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">n</span> Like the <span class="e2">n</span> in <span class="e2">n</span>on.
<span class="e29">p</span> Like the <span class="e2">p</span> in <span class="e2">p</span>aw.
<span class="e29">ph</span> <span class="e2">p</span> pronounced with aspiration. Often sounds like the <span class="e2">f</span> in <span class="e2">f</span>all.
<span class="e29">b (v)</span> Like the <span class="e2">b</span> in <span class="e2">b</span>all. When <span class="e2">b</span> follows a consonant, it issilent and the preceding consonant is doubled.
<span class="e29">bh</span> <span class="e2">b</span> pronounced with aspiration.
<span class="e29">m</span> Like the <span class="e2">m</span> in <span class="e2">m</span>op. When <span class="e2">m</span> follows a consonant, it is often silent and the preceding consonant is doubled.
<span class="e29">y</span> When <span class="e2">y</span> is the first letter of a word, it is pronounced like the <span class="e2">j</span> in <span class="e2">j</span>ob. When <span class="e2">y</span> occurs elsewhere within a word and is preceded by a vowel, it is pronounced like the <span class="e2">y</span> in<span class="e2"> y</span>awn or the <span class="e2">w</span> in <span class="e2">w</span>and. When <span class="e2">y</span> follows a consonant, it is silent and the preceding consonant is doubled, except when it is followed by <span class="e2">r</span>, in which case it is pronounced like the <span class="e2">j</span> in job.
<span class="e29">r</span> Like the <span class="e2">r</span> in <span class="e2">r</span>aw, though the tongue is slightly trilled.
<span class="e29">l</span> Like the <span class="e2">l</span> in <span class="e2">l</span>aw.
<span class="e29">ś</span> Like the <span class="e2">sh</span> in <span class="e2">sh</span>awl.
<span class="e29">ṣ</span> Like the <span class="e2">sh</span> in <span class="e2">sh</span>awl.
<span class="e29">s</span> Like the <span class="e2">s</span> in <span class="e2">s</span>ong or the <span class="e2">sh</span> in <span class="e2">sh</span>awl.
<span class="e29">h</span> Like the <span class="e2">h</span> in <span class="e2">h</span>ot.
<span class="e2">Additional Signs and Conjuncts</span>
<span class="e29">ṁ</span> Like a softened form of the <span class="e2">ng</span> in si<span class="e2">ng</span>.
<span class="e29">ḥ</span> <span class="e2">ḥ</span> is not pronounced when it occurs at the end of a word. When it occurs in the middle of a word, the consonant which follows it is doubled.
<span class="e29"> ̐</span> The chandrabindu indicates that the vowel beneath it should be pronounced nasally.
<span class="e29">kṣ</span> Pronounced like <span class="e2">kh</span> when at the beginning of a word and like <span class="e2">k-kh</span> when in the middle of a word.
<span class="e29">jñ</span> Pronounced like <span class="e2">g</span> when at the beginning of a word and like <span class="e2">g-g</span> between vowels. An <span class="e2">ā</span> following <span class="e2">jñ</span> is pronounced like the <span class="e2">a</span> in b<span class="e2">a</span>t.
